docs.title: What's different from sibling vaults
docs.text:
• AACR Annual (../aacr-2026) is the parent meeting. AACR Annual's pancreatic-track sessions feed forward — many of the AACR Pancreatic 2026 talks will be by speakers who gave preview / mechanism talks at Annual in April.
  • SABCS / ASCO are clinical-readout-driven; AACR Pancreatic is hybrid. Single-disease focus but with a strong basic-biology / translational backbone — the per-trial template from SABCS doesn't fully fit, and the per-tool template from EuroBioC doesn't fit. The hybrid talks/ template is the resolution.
  • Smaller corpus than the Annual Meeting. ~400–600 posters + ~80–120 oral / mini-symposium talks vs Annual's thousands. Deeper per-talk coverage is feasible.
  • September timing. Lands between AACR Annual (April), ASCO (May/June), EHA (June), ESMO (October), and the late-year readout-heavy cycle (SABCS / ASH / ASCO GI). Good window for Phase 2 maturation data and mechanism-level translational reveals.
  • No AACR virtual-platform replay this year (per the 2024 / 2025 pattern). Slide decks are not centrally archived; primary capture is the abstract supplement + AACR Meeting News + KOL trade-press recaps.

docs.title: Conference chairs and stated programmatic priorities
docs.text:
Six co-chairs:

  • Andrew J. Aguirre (Dana-Farber) — KRAS biology, functional genomics, PDX. Programmatic emphasis on KRAS-directed therapy and combination genomic screens.
  • Florencia McAllister (MD Anderson) — microbiome, immune microenvironment, prevention / interception. Programmatic emphasis on tumor-microbiome cross-talk, early detection, and racial/ethnic disparities.
  • Kenneth P. Olive (Columbia / Herbert Irving) — stroma biology, GEMMs, drug-delivery biology. Programmatic emphasis on the immunosuppressive microenvironment and stromal reprogramming.
  • Eileen O'Reilly (MSK) — clinical pancreatic-cancer trials lead. Programmatic emphasis on Phase 2/3 readouts, novel agents in metastatic and adjuvant settings.
  • Diane M. Simeone (UC San Diego) — early detection, cancer stem cells, host institution lead. Programmatic emphasis on biomarker development and high-risk cohort surveillance.
  • Colin D. Weekes (Mass General / Harvard) — translational clinical, KRAS-directed trials. Programmatic emphasis on biomarker-driven Phase 1/2 design.

The co-chair composition signals a balanced KRAS-and-stroma-and-microenvironment-and-clinical program. Compared to AACR Pancreatic 2024 (where the KRAS / immunology axis was front-and-center for the sotorasib / adagrasib reveal cycle), 2026 likely tilts toward (a) Phase 2 maturation data for the pan-RAS / G12D-selective classes and (b) combination-trial design questions, while keeping the basic-biology and early-detection programs intact.

docs.title: Expected program shape
docs.text: Based on the 2024 and 2025 AACR Pancreatic recurring pattern:

docs.title: Friday Sep 25 (opening)
docs.text:
• Afternoon: registration opens, opening reception.
  • Evening: Opening keynote — typically a field-defining figure (Tuveson, Vonderheide, di Magliano, Hingorani lineage). The 2024 / 2025 lineups have alternated between basic-science and clinical-leadership figures.

docs.title: Saturday Sep 26 (full day 1)
docs.text:
• Plenary session 1 — KRAS-directed therapy and combinations. Likely centered on pan-RAS (daraxonrasib) and G12D-selective (zoldonrasib, MRTX1133-class) Phase 1b/2 data, plus mechanism talks on KRAS-pathway resistance.
  • Major symposium — Tumor microenvironment, stroma, immune evasion. CAF heterogeneity update; mechanical tension; immunosuppressive myeloid axis.
  • Mini-symposium — Models for translation. Organoid / PDX / GEMM platforms, co-clinical trial designs.
  • Evening poster session 1 — typically 200–300 posters; mix of basic biology, translational, and clinical-correlate work.

docs.title: Sunday Sep 27 (full day 2)
docs.text:
• Plenary session 2 — Immunotherapy and vaccines. mRNA neoantigen vaccine readouts (BNT122 follow-up), TCR-T (NCI / Rosenberg lineage), CD40 agonists (sotigalimab class), claudin 18.2 ADC / CAR-T.
  • Major symposium — Tumor evolution, plasticity, heterogeneity. Classical / basal subtypes, lineage tracing, single-cell + spatial.
  • Major symposium — Metabolism and metabolic vulnerabilities. Autophagy, glutamine, pyrimidine, MAPK-pathway metabolic rewiring.
  • Mini-symposium — Early detection and interception. CA19-9 successors, microbiome-based detection, AI imaging, high-risk cohort surveillance.
  • Evening poster session 2.

docs.title: Monday Sep 28 (half-day close)
docs.text:
• Plenary session 3 — Translational case studies / clinical readouts. Adaptive platform updates (PRECISION-Panc, Precision Promise); BRCA/HRD maintenance; novel combination Phase 2.
  • Closing symposium — Health disparities, prevention, survivorship. Programmatic priority per AACR Special Conference cadence.
  • Awards / closing keynote. Typically a forward-looking field-state synthesis from one of the co-chairs.

The above is hypothetical — confirmed session titles will replace this once AACR publishes the program (~August).

docs.title: Anticipated headline readouts
docs.text: The five highest-priority watch items (per JPM 2026 sponsor guidance + Q1 2026 earnings + ASCO 2026 preview material):

docs.title: 1. Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) Phase 2/3 in metastatic PDAC
docs.text:
• Sponsor: Revolution Medicines.
  • Trials: RASolute-302 (Phase 3, 2L+ KRAS-mut metastatic PDAC, daraxonrasib mono vs SOC chemo); Phase 1b/2 combos with mFOLFIRINOX / gem-nab.
  • What we'd watch: Magnitude of PFS / OS benefit in 2L+ monotherapy (Phase 3 may not read at this meeting — likelier ESMO 2026 / ASCO GI 2027 — but interim safety / pharmacodynamic updates are plausible). Combination Phase 1b/2 ORR / tolerability for 1L. AACR Pancreatic is the natural home for the depth-of-response / biomarker correlative story.
  • Stakes: If PFS magnitude in 2L+ mono is clinically meaningful (HR <0.65), pan-RAS becomes the first practice-changing agent for the broad KRAS-mut PDAC population. Pre-embargo: anticipated per sponsor guidance; final Phase 3 readout not certain at this venue.

docs.title: 2. Zoldonrasib (RMC-9805) Phase 1 PDAC-specific data
docs.text:
• Sponsor: Revolution Medicines.
  • Trial: First-in-human Phase 1 in KRAS-G12D solid tumors, with PDAC expansion cohort.
  • What we'd watch: First PDAC-specific ORR / DLT / PK-PD in the G12D-selective subset (~40% of PDAC). Comparison to pan-RAS daraxonrasib in the same allele.
  • Stakes: G12D-selective vs pan-RAS is the field's open question on tolerability vs efficacy trade-off in chronic-dosing PDAC management. Pre-embargo: expected per sponsor guidance.

docs.title: 3. BNT122 / autogene cevumeran Phase 2 randomized RFS
docs.text:
• Sponsor: BioNTech / Genentech / Memorial Sloan Kettering.
  • Trial: IMcode-004 / NCT05968326 (Phase 2 randomized, resected PDAC, mRNA neoantigen vaccine + atezo + mFOLFIRINOX vs mFOLFIRINOX).
  • What we'd watch: Whether the Phase 1 single-center RFS signal (Rojas et al. Nature 2023; mature follow-up ASCO 2024) replicates in a multi-center randomized Phase 2. T-cell persistence / immunogenicity correlatives. AACR Pancreatic is the natural home for the deep-immune-correlate story.
  • Stakes: If RFS benefit holds in randomized Phase 2, mRNA neoantigen vaccines become a credible adjuvant SOC component for resectable PDAC — the first immunotherapy to do so. Pre-embargo: Phase 2 readout timing not confirmed publicly; could land here, ESMO 2026, or 2027.

docs.title: 4. KRAS-G12C(ON) RMC-6291 PDAC subset update
docs.text:
• Sponsor: Revolution Medicines.
  • What we'd watch: Whether the G12C(ON) class (active-state binder) outperforms the G12C(OFF) class (sotorasib / adagrasib) in PDAC, where G12C(OFF) ORR has been modest.
  • Stakes: Within the ~1.5% G12C-mut PDAC slice, this defines the second-generation standard. Mechanistically informs the broader "active-state vs inactive-state" KRAS-inhibitor design question. Pre-embargo: data cut timing uncertain.

docs.title: 5. Stromal / microenvironment major symposium
docs.text:
• Lead: Olive / Tuveson / Hingorani lineage + emerging spatial-omics groups.
  • What we'd watch: Whether the iCAF / myCAF / apCAF resolution moves from descriptive to interventional — combination trial designs targeting one CAF compartment without the off-target stromal-collapse problem that sank prior stroma-targeting agents (hedgehog, hyaluronidase, FAK class).
  • Stakes: Stroma has been "next year's story" at AACR Pancreatic for a decade. Whether 2026 is the cycle that produces a credible combination-trial nomination is the open question.

docs.title: Sponsors / pipeline watchlist
docs.text:
Per JPM 2026 and Q1 2026 earnings:

  • Revolution Medicines — RMC-6236 (daraxonrasib, pan-RAS), RMC-9805 (zoldonrasib, G12D), RMC-6291 (G12C(ON)), RMC-5552 (mTORC1), RMC-4630 (SHP2). The largest PDAC-specific sponsor footprint at this meeting. RASolute-302 Phase 3 timeline is the central watch.
  • BioNTech / Genentech — BNT122 / autogene cevumeran. Phase 2 randomized adjuvant. Single Phase 3 anchor for the mRNA-vaccine class in PDAC.
  • Bristol Myers Squibb (Mirati legacy) — adagrasib (G12C), MRTX1133 next-gen G12D, MRTX0902 SOS1.
  • Astellas / Boundless Bio — RAS portfolio (RAS-Companion / PROTAC / next-gen).
  • Moderna / Merck — mRNA-4157 individualized neoantigen + pembro; PDAC arm timing uncertain.
  • AstraZeneca — claudin 18.2 ADC class extending into PDAC subset.
  • Amgen — sotorasib (G12C), broader KRAS-mut combinations.
  • Black Diamond Therapeutics / Frontier Medicines — KRAS / pathway-allele covalent / scaffolding inhibitors.
  • NCI Surgery Branch (Rosenberg lineage) — KRAS-G12D / G12V TCR-T cellular therapy.
  • Academic / cooperative platforms — PRECISION-Panc (UK), Precision Promise (PanCAN / US), AltCAP.

docs.title: Open questions / things to confirm
docs.text:
1. Exact abstract / late-breaker / program-release deadlines. AACR hasn't published these yet (May 11). Will update when announced.
  2. Named lecture slots. AACR Special Conferences typically include named-award lectures (Dorothy Landon-AACR Translational Cancer Research Prize lineage, AACR Distinguished Lectureship in Pancreatic Cancer if applicable). Lineup is TBD.
  3. Whether BNT122 Phase 2 randomized RFS reads here or at ESMO. Sponsor guidance has not been specific on venue. Either is plausible; AACR Pancreatic gets the deeper immune-correlate story, ESMO gets the broader oncology audience.

docs.title: Talks — AACR Pancreatic Cancer 2026
docs.text:
The primary artifact of this vault: one Markdown file per talk, hybrid-anchored. AACR Pancreatic 2026 is a mixed clinical-readout + basic-biology + translational meeting, so a single anchor type does not fit — each talk resolves to trial (clinical readout / interventional study), tool (model system / platform / assay), or study (mechanism paper / dataset / hypothesis-generating cohort).

Status: Template + master index. Per-talk pages will be populated as the AACR Pancreatic 2026 program is released (August–September 2026) and abstracts publish (~2 weeks pre-meeting). Pre-meeting stubs flagged *expected, subject to embargo* are sourced from prior-year AACR Pancreatic programs, AACR 2026 Annual pancreatic-track content, sponsor pipeline guidance (JPM 2026, Q1 2026 earnings), and ASCO 2026 preview material. Talk titles, session assignments, and named-lecture lineups are speculative until program release.

docs.title: Per-talk template (hybrid)
docs.text: Each talk file (e.g., daraxonrasib-rascolt-1.md, tuveson-organoid-platform.md, mcallister-microbiome-prevention.md) follows one of three anchored schemas depending on what the talk is centered on. The shared header is uniform; the body block differs.

docs.title: Shared header (all anchor types)
docs.text:
# <Talk title> — <one-line framing>

> **Anchor:** trial | tool | study · **Session:** <session name, date, time PT, room> · **Embargo:** <date>

## At a glance

- **Speaker / presenter:** <name, institution>
- **Senior author / lab:** <name, institution> (if different)
- **Talk type:** keynote / plenary / major-symposium invited / mini-symposium proffered / poster spotlight
- **Co-authors highlighted:** <if cross-institution collaboration is the story>

docs.title: Body — trial anchor (clinical readout / interventional)
docs.text:
For talks centered on a clinical trial or interventional study. Use when the headline is a Phase 1/2/3 readout.

## Trial

- **Trial name / acronym:** <e.g., RASolute-302, IMcode-004>
- **NCT ID:** <NCTxxxxxxxx>
- **Sponsor:** <pharma / cooperative group / academic IIT>
- **Phase:** <1 / 1b/2 / 2 / 2/3 / 3>
- **Design:** <arms, randomization, blinding, biomarker selection>
- **N:** <enrolled / analyzed at this readout>
- **Primary endpoint(s):** <ORR / PFS / OS / RFS / DLT / pharmacodynamic>
- **Comparator:** <SOC / placebo / single-arm>
- **Population:** <line of therapy; KRAS-mut subset; resectable vs metastatic; biomarker-selected>

## Headline result

<One paragraph. Numbers + HR + p-value if known. If pre-embargo, mark
`*expected per <company> topline <date>*` or `*pre-embargo per <analyst source>*`.>

## Mechanism / class

<Drug class, target. Cross-link to AACR Annual mechanism sessions or prior AACR Pancreatic readouts.>

## Practice-changing?

<Yes / no / pending, with rationale: FDA filing path, NCCN PDAC guideline implications, unmet need.>

docs.title: Body — tool anchor (model system / platform / assay)
docs.text:

docs.title: Cross-cutting themes (for the program-notes synthesis)
docs.text:
To trace across talks/ once populated:

  1. The KRAS-targeting class question. Pan-RAS (daraxonrasib) vs allele-selective (zoldonrasib G12D, RMC-6291 G12C(ON), Mirati G12D) vs combination backbones (with chemo, with checkpoint, with SHP2 / mTORC1 / autophagy partners). The 2026 question: does pan-RAS Phase 3 win on raw efficacy, or does allele-selectivity win on tolerability for the chronic-dosing window?
  2. mRNA neoantigen vaccines — durability and generalizability. Phase 1 BNT122 RFS signal needs Phase 2 randomized validation; the question is whether the result extends beyond a single-center Memorial Sloan Kettering / BioNTech / Genentech axis and into multi-site adjuvant SOC.
  3. Stroma — is it druggable yet, or is the answer still "model it better"? A decade of stromal-targeting clinical failures (hedgehog, hyaluronidase, FAK) sit against a decade of refined biology (iCAF/myCAF/apCAF, mechanical tension, exosomal cross-talk). 2026's slate will likely lean basic with a few combo-trial signals.
  4. Early detection moving from biomarker discovery to interception. CA19-9 successor assays + microbiome + AI imaging are converging — but high-risk cohort enrollment, screening-trial economics, and overdiagnosis questions are unresolved.
  5. PDX / organoid platforms maturing into co-clinical-trial infrastructure. The Tuveson / Tiriac and successor organoid platforms have been "almost ready" for several AACR Pancreatic cycles; 2026 may be the year where one of them is the formal SOC arm of an adaptive trial.

docs.title: Why this is in the vault
docs.text:
ACMG is the clinical-genetics decision-rules venue. Where ASHG runs the methods and population-genetics framing, ACMG runs the clinical-laboratory implementation: who orders the test, how is the variant classified, what does the report say, what does the clinician do with it. The overlap with the AACR / ASCO oncology cycle is concentrated but high-value:

  1. Hereditary-cancer panels and germline-somatic integration. ACMG runs the ACMG Secondary Findings list (most recent: v3.3, with continued debate over scope and implementation). Panel-classification accuracy, universal-testing thresholds, and pediatric-cancer-predisposition screening all live here. Same investigators show up at AACR with somatic-overlay analyses 4–6 weeks later.
  2. ACMG/AMP variant-classification standards. The ACMG/AMP 2015 standards and their successor SVI / ClinGen recalibrations (PS3/BS3 functional evidence, BA1 / BS1 allele-frequency thresholds, AlphaMissense-as-PP3 controversy) are debated and updated here. Every clinical-genetics laboratory in the US uses this framework. Cancer-variant classification rests on it.
  3. Clonal hematopoiesis and somatic mosaicism in cancer testing. ACMG 2026 ran a dedicated session "Clonal Hematopoiesis, Somatic and Post-Zygotic Mosaicism in Multigene Cancer Testing for Geneticists" — the clinical-lab translation of the population-scale CHIP findings that anchor ASHG / ASH talks.
  4. AI in clinical genomics. ACMG 2026 platform presentations included "Demystifying Base Large Language Model Reproducibility and Accuracy in ACMG/AMP Variant Classification" and AI-assisted genome interpretation in lab workflows. This is the clinical-lab-validation venue for foundation-model variant-effect predictors (AlphaMissense, ESM, EVO follow-ons) that debut at ISMB / ASHG.
  5. Newborn screening expansion to genomic sequencing. Presidential Plenary theme. Cross-cuts cancer predisposition (RB1, TP53, RET, APC, BRCA, Lynch) via the secondary-findings debate — should pediatric cancer-predisposition variants be reported from newborn WGS?

Hybrid template (and the design decision behind this vault): ACMG is neither pure-clinical-readout (ASCO / SABCS) nor pure-methods (ISMB / RECOMB) — most platform slots are "clinical-lab investigator anchored on a cohort + classification framework + lab implementation," with a substantial AI/ML methods overlay and a strong case-based-session thread. The closest sibling shape in the vault is ASHG 2026, which collapses to a single talks/ directory with a per-talk hybrid template; we apply the same shape here, with the clinical-lab / cancer-genetics / variant-classification subset prioritized.

docs.title: What's different from sibling meetings
docs.text:
• Clinical-lab orientation. Unlike ASHG (population genetics + methods) or AACR (cancer biology + trials), ACMG is the meeting where the clinical laboratory directors (FACMG-certified) and clinical geneticists (board-certified medical geneticists) meet. The questions are: is this variant pathogenic, what does the report say, what does the clinician do with it.
  • Standards-document venue. ACMG and ClinGen working groups release updates at this meeting — variant-classification standards, secondary-findings list revisions, gene-disease validity curations, prenatal sequencing position statements. These are practice-defining documents.
  • Smaller and more focused than ASHG. ~3,500 attendees vs ASHG's ~7,500; tighter program (~1,500 abstracts vs ASHG's ~3,000); deeper clinical-lab content density.
  • Hybrid clinical + research format. Many talks are clinical case readouts, not research presentations. The case-based session is a load-bearing slot type. CME / P.A.C.E. / NSGC credit programming dominates a meaningful fraction of session-hours.
  • Industry-press density. Higher than ASHG because every major clinical-genetics-lab vendor (Illumina, Baylor Genetics, GeneDx, Natera, Ambry, Myriad, Quest, LabCorp Diagnostics, Tempus, Caris) presents data and runs sponsor symposia.
  • March timing. ACMG is the first big genomics meeting of the year after JPM — clinical-lab pipelines that get pitched at JPM (January) often have their first peer-reviewed-style readout at ACMG (March), then a methods-paper at ASHG (October).
  • Open-access disposition. GIM is hybrid (most content paywalled, growing open-access); GIM Open is fully OA. Citability is moderate; trade-press recaps (GenomeWeb / 360Dx) often the most accessible source pre-publication.

docs.title: Cross-vault links
docs.text:
• ASHG 2026 — the methods + population-genetics sibling. Many ACMG investigators have ASHG talks in October with the research-methods framing of the clinical-lab work shown at ACMG.
  • AACR 2026 — cancer-biology / hereditary-cancer overlap. ACMG cancer-genetics platform sessions feed forward to AACR hereditary-cancer / germline-somatic posters 4–6 weeks later.
  • ASCO 2026 — clinical translation. Cancer-predisposition testing, germline-informed PARP / PD-1 trial eligibility, Lynch-syndrome surveillance — methods that mature at ACMG arrive at ASCO with patient outcomes.
  • ASH 2026 — clonal hematopoiesis bridge. CHIP / CCUS / germline-MN-predisposition is a shared topic; ACMG runs the clinical-lab classification framing, ASH runs the clinical sequelae.
  • ISMB 2026 / RECOMB 2026 — methods overlap. AlphaMissense, ESM-genomic, EVO, and DNA-language-model variant-effect predictors that debut at ISMB get clinical-lab-validation discussion at ACMG.
  • AGBT 2026 — platform-launch overlap. Long-read clinical sequencing (PacBio HiFi, ONT R10) clinical implementation discussion at ACMG follows AGBT February platform talks.
  • ESHG 2026 — European clinical-genetics sibling meeting; many overlapping speakers and topics, six weeks later (May/June).
  • JPM 2026 — financing layer for the clinical-lab vendors who show data at ACMG.
  • Conferences timeline — ACMG's position in the year's genomics cycle (JPM Jan → AGBT Feb → ACMG Mar → AACR Apr → ASCO May/Jun → ESHG Jun → ISMB Jul → ESMO/ASHG Oct → SITC Nov → ASH Dec → SABCS Dec).

docs.title: Beyond The List — Scope and Implementation of ACMG Secondary Findings (v3.3+)
docs.text:
ACMG 2026 standards-update symposium on the Secondary Findings list — current v3.3 implementation gaps, future scope expansion (including pediatric-onset cancer-predisposition reporting), and the "Beyond The List" question of whether SF should remain a closed gene-set or shift to a framework-based model.

  • Speaker / institution: ACMG Secondary Findings Working Group (SF WG); panel composition TBC from GIM supplement and ACMG Statements
  • Anchor type: guideline
  • Day / session: Mid-meeting featured symposium (Day 3–4, Mar 12–13, 2026); exact slot TBD
  • Status: post-meeting; from ACMG meeting site featured-session listing; whether SF v3.4 was officially released at the meeting TBD pending GIM supplement and ACMG Statements page

docs.title: Headline finding
docs.text: The Secondary Findings list — first published 2013 with 56 genes, now at v3.3 (2023, 81 genes) — is at a structural inflection: incremental gene-addition cycles are reaching diminishing returns, while the underlying clinical-lab universe has shifted (universal-WGS pediatric programs, expanded carrier screening, newborn-WGS pilots, NIFS) in ways that strain the original SF framing. Cancer-predisposition genes dominate the list — BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, APC, MUTYH, PTEN, RB1, RET, VHL, WT1, plus newer additions — and the policy load on the list comes disproportionately from cancer reporting. Specific SF v3.4 gene additions / removals (if any) and revised reporting recommendations TBD pending GIM supplement and the ACMG Statements page.

docs.title: Methodology / framework
docs.text: Framework discussion: (a) actionability criteria — clinical-management change must be available, validated, and meaningful; (b) penetrance thresholds — minimum age-of-onset-adjusted penetrance for inclusion; (c) gene-list maintenance cadence vs framework-based opt-in; (d) pediatric reporting framing — should adult-onset cancer-predisposition genes (BRCA, Lynch) be reported in pediatric WGS at all? Cross-references ClinGen Hereditary Cancer VCEPs for gene-disease validity backbone.

docs.title: Lab-translation deep dive
docs.text:
Validation requirements. SF reporting requires the lab to validate the same genes on the same sample to the same depth / completeness as the primary indication — there is no half-validated SF tier. Practical floor: ≥20x at >99% of coding bases for the entire 81-gene v3.3 list, with explicit PMS2 / PMS2-pseudogene disambiguation (a perennial SF-list bioinformatics failure mode), PMS2CL handling, MSH2 inversion detection, and SMN1/SMN2 distinguishing capability for any genes with paralog issues. Validation packages must include exon-level CNV detection for relevant genes (BRCA1, BRCA2, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, EPCAM).

Lab-stack changes. WGS labs absorb SF reporting more easily than panel / exome labs because coverage is uniform; panel labs must explicitly add SF capture probes when SF is offered as opt-in. Operational adds: opt-in / opt-out consent capture at order, SF-specific curation queue, separate SF report (or clearly delineated SF section), and patient-facing return-of-results workflow for the inevitable BRCA / Lynch positive that lands on a patient consented to SF but ordered for an unrelated indication.

Regulatory / insurance. SF reporting is in-scope under CLIA / CAP as part of any test offering SF — no separate FDA pathway. Payer coverage is the load-bearing constraint: BRCA / Lynch positives identified via SF need downstream surveillance / risk-reducing intervention coverage that often hinges on family-history criteria the patient may not meet. Equity / access is the most-cited gap.

Variant curation. ClinGen Hereditary Cancer VCEPs are the gene-disease-validity backbone; SF v3.3 already incorporates VCEP curation. SF v3.4 framework-vs-list question (TBD pending GIM supplement) materially changes curation cadence — a framework-based SF requires per-variant actionability gating, not just per-gene inclusion.

docs.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis, Somatic and Post-Zygotic Mosaicism in Multigene Cancer Testing for Geneticists
docs.text:
ACMG 2026 dedicated symposium on the clinical-lab translation of population-scale CHIP and mosaicism findings into multigene hereditary-cancer panel testing — incidental-finding handling, reporting thresholds, and germline-vs-clonal disambiguation.

  • Speaker / institution: Symposium panel — clinical-lab CHIP working-group representatives, Bick-aligned and Natarajan-aligned investigator pool, hereditary-cancer panel lab medical directors (Ambry / GeneDx / Color / Invitae-successor labs); specific speaker slate TBC from GIM supplement
  • Anchor type: methods + clinical
  • Day / session: Mid-meeting symposium (Day 3–4, Mar 12–13, 2026); exact slot TBD
  • Status: post-meeting; from ACMG meeting site featured-session listing; speaker slate and concrete reporting recommendations TBD pending GIM supplement and Digital Edition

docs.title: Headline finding
docs.text: Multigene cancer panels run on blood DNA routinely surface variants in genes (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, TP53, PPM1D, CHEK2, JAK2, ATM, others) at non-germline variant allele fractions — clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) — alongside post-zygotic mosaic variants that are biologically distinct from CHIP but operationally hard to distinguish in a clinical lab. The symposium frames the reporting decision tree: when is a sub-50% VAF call CHIP (don't report as germline), when is it post-zygotic mosaicism (report with caveat), and when is it germline-with-allelic-imbalance. Cohort numerics from contributing labs (CHIP detection rates in hereditary-cancer panel submissions, age-stratified prevalence, downstream MN-risk follow-up) TBD pending supplement.

docs.title: Methodology / framework
docs.text: Operational framework combining: (1) VAF distribution analysis with tissue-comparator (buccal / fibroblast / skin) when available; (2) gene-list stratification (canonical CHIP drivers vs hereditary-cancer-syndrome genes with CHIP overlap, particularly TP53, CHEK2, ATM); (3) deeper sequencing of borderline VAFs; (4) longitudinal resampling for suspected clonal expansion. ACMG/AMP framework adaptation: PM6 / PS2 cannot apply to clonal events; PM2 / BS1 frequency thresholds need clonal-event-aware modification.

docs.title: Lab-translation deep dive
docs.text:
Validation requirements. Disambiguating CHIP from post-zygotic mosaicism vs germline-with-allelic-imbalance requires the lab to validate (a) VAF accuracy at low fractions (10–40%) with replicate variance characterized, (b) sensitivity of variant callers at sub-50% VAF on hereditary-cancer-panel coverage depths (typically 300–500x), and (c) a tissue-comparator workflow (buccal swab, cultured fibroblast, or skin punch) with its own end-to-end validation. Many existing hereditary-cancer panels were validated only for germline (~50% / ~100% VAF expectations) — extension to clonal calls is a net-new analytical-validation event.

Lab-stack changes. Operational additions: reflex tissue-comparator collection workflow (logistics + consent), deeper sequencing for borderline VAFs, longitudinal resampling at defined intervals (6–12 months) for suspected clonal expansion, and pipeline-level flags that block germline-style reporting on canonical CHIP-driver variants (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, JAK2). LIMS schema needs a clonal-status field per variant.

Regulatory / insurance. No CAP-checklist requirement specific to CHIP disambiguation as of 2026 (TBD pending symposium recommendations and ACMG Practice Resources). Payer coverage for reflex tissue-comparator testing is patchwork — typically billed against the hereditary-cancer-panel CPT code rather than separately. Insurance implications of incidental CHIP reporting (life / long-term-care underwriting) are an emerging ELSI question.

Variant curation. ACMG/AMP framework modifications required: PM6 / PS2 (de novo) cannot apply to clonal events; PM2 / BS1 (population frequency) needs clonal-event-aware thresholds; functional-evidence interpretation (PS3 / BS3) must consider clonal-selection bias. Gene-specific guidance for TP53 / CHEK2 / ATM (overlap genes) is the highest-leverage curation deliverable from this symposium.

docs.title: Headline finding
docs.text: Platform 1 is the load-bearing cancer-genetics slot of the 2026 program — six to eight platform talks covering (1) BRCA1/2 and PALB2 panel-classification updates, including VUS-reclassification cohort outcomes and the impact of ClinGen Hereditary Breast/Ovarian/Pancreatic VCEP curations; (2) Lynch syndrome (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, EPCAM) — current MMR-gene classification landscape, universal-tumor-screening implementation data, and downstream cascade-testing yield; (3) the broader universal-testing-vs-criteria-based-testing debate for breast / ovarian / colorectal / pancreatic cancer. Specific per-talk cohort sizes, reclassification rates, and detection-yield percentages TBD pending supplement.

docs.title: Methodology / framework
docs.text: Clinical-lab cohort designs: multi-site hereditary-cancer panel submissions analyzed retrospectively for (a) pathogenic / likely-pathogenic detection rate stratified by ordering indication, (b) VUS reclassification rate using ClinGen VCEP-specific evidence frameworks (PS3 functional evidence recalibration, splice-evidence PVS1, multifactorial likelihood ratios for BRCA), (c) cascade-testing uptake from probands to first-degree relatives, (d) outcome implications for risk-reducing surgery and surveillance. ACMG/AMP 2015 framework with ClinGen Hereditary Cancer VCEP gene-specific specifications.

docs.title: Lab-translation deep dive
docs.text:
Validation requirements. Hereditary-cancer-panel labs are in a constant re-validation cycle as ClinGen VCEPs publish gene-specific evidence-code recalibrations. Each VCEP update (BRCA PS3 functional-evidence weighting, MMR-gene PVS1 splice-evidence, multifactorial-likelihood evidence integration for BRCA1/2) triggers a re-classification sweep across the historical VUS population and a validation refresh of the curation pipeline. CNV detection (BRCA1/2 exon-level, MLH1 / MSH2 / EPCAM 5' deletion, MSH2 inversion) remains a lab-stack differentiator and a recurring validation concern.

Lab-stack changes. Universal-testing scale (universal breast / ovarian / pancreatic / colorectal hereditary-cancer testing pilots) collapses sample volumes onto fewer reference labs and demands faster TAT (≤14 days as a working floor for treatment-decision pathways like PARP-inhibitor eligibility). Pipeline-side: structural-variant calling parity with SNV calling, exon-CNV detection, splice-impact prediction integration (SpliceAI as a near-universal PP3 / BP4 input), and ClinGen-VCEP-aware classification logic.

Regulatory / insurance. FDA LDT final rule applies — most hereditary-cancer panels operate as LDTs, with FDA-cleared kits (Myriad BRCA, Ambry / GeneDx panels) coexisting. Payer coverage hinges on NCCN guidelines (which moved toward universal breast / colorectal testing in recent revisions); cascade-testing reimbursement for first-degree relatives is the load-bearing implementation question for the universal-testing axis.

Variant curation. ClinGen VCEPs (HBOP — BRCA1/2; HBOP — PALB2; InSiGHT for MMR genes; CDH1; PTEN; etc.) provide the gene-specific evidence frameworks. VUS reclassification cadence (Open Question #3) reflects steady-state VCEP throughput. Multifactorial-likelihood evidence integration for BRCA1/2 is the most-mature curation paradigm — other genes are catching up.

docs.title: Demystifying Base LLM Reproducibility and Accuracy in ACMG/AMP Variant Classification
docs.text:
Platform benchmark of base (non-fine-tuned) large language models against the ACMG/AMP 2015 variant-classification framework — testing reproducibility, accuracy, and per-evidence-code drift across reruns and across models.

  • Speaker / institution: Platform speaker TBC from GIM abstract supplement; submission tracks to AI / Informatics track
  • Anchor type: tool / methods
  • Day / session: Day 3–5 (Mar 12–14, 2026), AI / Informatics platform session (specific slot TBD)
  • Status: post-meeting; from ACMG meeting site session listing; per-model accuracy numbers, dataset composition, and authorship TBD pending GIM supplement and Digital Edition recording

docs.title: Headline finding
docs.text: First systematic clinical-lab benchmark of base (off-the-shelf, non-fine-tuned) LLMs — including GPT, Claude, Gemini-class models — on the ACMG/AMP 2015 five-tier variant-classification task (Pathogenic / Likely Pathogenic / VUS / Likely Benign / Benign). The talk is positioned as a reproducibility study: how stable is the same model's output across repeated runs on the same variant, and how concordant are different models on the same evidence inputs? Quantitative concordance rates, per-evidence-code (PVS1, PS1–4, PM1–6, PP1–5, BA1, BS1–4, BP1–7) accuracy, and final classification agreement against ClinVar 2-star+ ground truth TBD pending supplement.

docs.title: Methodology / framework
docs.text: Benchmark design likely: curated test set of variants with established ClinVar expert-panel classifications (ClinGen VCEPs as gold standard); LLM prompted to apply ACMG/AMP 2015 rules to a structured evidence package; multiple reruns per variant to measure intra-model reproducibility; cross-model comparison for inter-model concordance. Distinguishes evidence-code assignment accuracy from final tier assignment accuracy — a model can hit the right tier with the wrong evidence stack. Critical comparison to existing classification aids (Franklin, VarSome, InterVar, CardioBoost, BayesDel as PP3 proxy).

docs.title: Lab-translation deep dive
docs.text:
Validation requirements. A base LLM that participates in any classification decision triggers CLIA-style analytical validation: stability of output across reruns (intra-run reproducibility), stability across model versions (vendor silently rotates model weights — a load-bearing validation hazard), and accuracy against ClinVar 2-star+ / VCEP-curated ground truth stratified by gene, evidence-code mix, and variant rarity. The reproducibility framing of the talk is precisely the failure mode CLIA requires labs to characterize before clinical use. Concordance floors and stability windows TBD pending GIM supplement.

Lab-stack changes. Most clinical hereditary-cancer labs already run rule-based classifiers (Franklin, VarSome, InterVar) under a curator-in-the-loop model. Inserting an LLM means: (a) prompt-engineering as a versioned, change-controlled lab document; (b) input-evidence package construction as its own validated module (PubMed search, population-frequency lookup, functional-evidence retrieval, splice-prediction summary); (c) audit-trail logging of every prompt + response per variant; (d) periodic re-validation when the underlying model is updated. RAG-with-ClinGen and fine-tuning shift more validation burden onto the lab.

Regulatory / insurance. FDA has signaled (via the LDT final rule and AI/ML guidance) that AI-augmented classification is in-scope as a clinical decision support tool. CAP MIN-checklist updates anticipated for AI-augmented variant curation. Payer impact is indirect — reclassification of historical VUS triggers re-billing and re-counseling pathways.

Variant curation. Highest-value role is likely VUS-triage assist (auto-summarize literature, propose evidence codes, flag candidate reclassifications) with mandatory human sign-out, rather than autonomous classification. Liability and CLIA framing currently preclude autonomous LLM classification.

docs.title: Non-Invasive Fetal Sequencing (NIFS) Is Coming: Are You Ready?
docs.text:
ACMG 2026 featured symposium on the clinical-lab inflection from cell-free-DNA NIPT (aneuploidy + select microdeletions) to whole-fetal-genome sequencing from maternal plasma — assay readiness, ELSI framing, and clinical-pathway integration.

  • Speaker / institution: Symposium panel — Natera, Illumina, academic prenatal-genomics center reps (likely Baylor, Columbia, UCSF, Penn fetal-genomics programs); specific slate TBC from GIM supplement
  • Anchor type: tool + cohort
  • Day / session: Mid-meeting featured symposium (Day 3–4, Mar 12–13, 2026); exact slot TBD
  • Status: post-meeting; from ACMG meeting site featured-session listing and vendor pre-meeting press (Natera + Illumina ACMG 2026 pages); specific clinical-readiness benchmarks TBD pending GIM supplement and on-demand recording

docs.title: Headline finding
docs.text: NIFS — extracting fetal whole-genome sequence from maternal cell-free DNA, bypassing amniocentesis / CVS for monogenic disorders and chromosomal aneuploidy — is moving from research demonstration to clinical-lab readiness. The symposium reports current state on (1) fetal-fraction enrichment and assay sensitivity for SNVs and small indels, (2) clinical-validation cohort size and per-disorder sensitivity / specificity, (3) the expanded gene list NIFS labs are validating beyond current NIPT scope. Quantitative cohort sizes and per-gene PPV numbers TBD pending GIM supplement; Natera / Illumina vendor-presented validation cohorts likely the load-bearing data.

docs.title: Methodology / framework
docs.text: Technical stack: deep WGS of maternal plasma cfDNA (typically 30–60x of mixed maternal+fetal DNA), fetal-fraction estimation, fetal-genotype inference via maternal-haplotype subtraction or direct fetal-read identification. Comparator: matched amniocentesis / CVS WGS for clinical-validation cohorts. ACMG/AMP variant classification applied to fetal calls; reporting framework for incidental findings (including ACMG SF v3.3 cancer-predisposition genes) is an open ELSI question this symposium addresses directly.

docs.title: Lab-translation deep dive
docs.text:
Validation requirements. NIFS is a screening modality that aims at diagnostic-grade per-variant sensitivity and specificity, which collapses the traditional NIPT validation envelope. Required: (a) fetal-fraction-stratified analytical sensitivity (typical NIPT validates ≥4% fetal fraction; NIFS likely needs ≥6–8% per-gene minimums TBD), (b) per-disorder per-gene clinical sensitivity from prospective amnio / CVS-matched cohorts, (c) PPV reporting per disorder (a hard learning from NIPT's microdeletion false-positive press), (d) gestational-age and maternal-condition (BMI, multiples, vanishing-twin, maternal cancer / CHIP) stratification.

Lab-stack changes. NIFS extends existing NIPT lab infrastructure with deeper WGS (30–60x mixed-DNA depth vs ~0.1–0.3x for aneuploidy NIPT) and fetal-fraction-aware fetal-genotype inference (haplotype subtraction or direct fetal-read calling). Throughput economics shift substantially — what was a low-pass massively-parallel assay becomes a deep-WGS workflow. Bioinformatics validation includes the maternal-CHIP false-positive failure mode (a maternal clonal variant misclassified as fetal).

Regulatory / insurance. FDA's LDT final rule and IVDR (Europe) materially shape the path; current US NIPT lives largely as LDT, and NIFS will inherit that posture with closer scrutiny given the per-variant diagnostic-adjacent claims. Payer coverage trajectory in 2026–2028 is the load-bearing commercial question — replacement of NIPT line-item vs supplemental coding.

Variant curation. Reporting framework for fetal incidental findings (ACMG SF v3.3, particularly adult-onset cancer-predisposition genes BRCA1/2, Lynch, TP53) is an open ELSI question this symposium addresses directly. Termination-decision ethics frame curation-policy choices, not just lab-stack choices. Specific fetal-NIFS curation recommendations TBD pending GIM supplement.

docs.title: Presidential Plenary: The Future of Expanded Newborn Genomic Screening
docs.text:
ACMG 2026's opening plenary frames the policy + clinical-lab debate over moving newborn screening from biochemical panels to whole-genome sequencing — with the cancer-predisposition reporting wedge as a load-bearing sub-question.

  • Speaker / institution: Presidential Plenary panel (ACMG leadership + BabySeq2 / GUARDIAN / NBSeq / EarlyCheck program PIs); combined with ACMG Foundation Awards ceremony and Rimoin Lecture
  • Anchor type: guideline + cohort
  • Day / session: Day 2 (Wed Mar 11, 2026) — Presidential Plenary, morning, Baltimore Convention Center
  • Status: post-meeting; from ACMG meeting site + PRNewswire pre-meeting press; per-talk speaker slate and concrete recommendations TBD pending GIM abstract supplement and Digital Edition recordings

docs.title: Headline finding
docs.text: The plenary is the field's coordinating moment on how, when, and with what consent framework the four major US newborn-genomic-screening pilots (BabySeq2, GUARDIAN at Columbia, NBSeq, EarlyCheck) translate into a generalizable clinical-lab service. Specific cohort numerics (cumulative consented infants, additional-condition yield, false-positive rates per disorder, return-of-results uptake) TBD pending GIM supplement. The cancer-predisposition reporting wedge — whether RB1, TP53, RET, APC, BRCA1/2, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 variants should be reported from newborn WGS, and to whom — is treated as a discrete policy axis.

docs.title: Methodology / framework
docs.text: Panel format combining cohort readouts (BabySeq2 randomized return-of-results trial; GUARDIAN's >100k-infant screening pilot; NBSeq; EarlyCheck) with framework discussion of the ACMG/AMP variant-classification thresholds appropriate for asymptomatic newborns, the role of the ACMG Secondary Findings v3.3 list, and gene-list selection (actionable pediatric-onset only, vs adult-onset cancer-predisposition genes reported deferred-to-adulthood vs reported-to-parents).

docs.title: Lab-translation deep dive
docs.text:
Validation requirements. Moving newborn screening from biochemical panels to WGS requires net-new CLIA/CAP validation packages for every step the pilots formalized as research-grade: maternal-blood / heel-stick DNA extraction reproducibility at neonatal volumes, library-prep performance on low-input gDNA, WGS coverage uniformity across the actionable gene list (≥20x median, ≥10x at >99% of targeted bases as a working floor — formal NBS-WGS minimums TBD pending plenary recommendations), and bioinformatics-pipeline validation against a contrived NBS truth set. The four pilots (BabySeq2, GUARDIAN, NBSeq, EarlyCheck) used overlapping but non-identical gene lists, which is itself a validation-portability problem.

Lab-stack changes. Existing biochemical NBS labs (state public-health labs) are not configured for clinical WGS turnaround; the plenary's translation question is whether NBS-WGS sits in (a) the existing state-public-health lab footprint with new sequencer capex, (b) a centralized reference-lab model (akin to current expanded carrier screening), or (c) hybrid biochemical-first / WGS-reflex. TAT expectations (current biochemical NBS: 5–7 days from heel stick) are a hard constraint that shapes the answer.

Regulatory / insurance. No CMS coverage policy for routine newborn WGS as of 2026; state Medicaid coverage is patchwork. FDA's stance on NBS-WGS as a screening (not diagnostic) modality is unresolved. ACMG SF v3.3 interaction is the load-bearing payer question.

Variant curation. Requires ClinGen-VCEP-aware automated triage at NBS scale (millions of births/year if universal). Manual sign-out per infant is not operationally viable; the workflow must be variant-prefiltered, with human review only for borderline P/LP and any reportable SF variant. Specific automation thresholds TBD pending plenary.

docs.title: David L. Rimoin Lifetime Achievement Award — John C. Carey
docs.text:
The ACMG Foundation's highest honor goes to John C. Carey, MD, MPH, FACMG, FAAP — Professor Emeritus of Pediatrics at the University of Utah and a >40-year career architect of clinical genetics, dysmorphology, and trisomy 13/18 patient advocacy.

  • Speaker / institution: John C. Carey, MD, MPH, FACMG, FAAP — Professor Emeritus of Pediatrics, University of Utah School of Medicine; former Division Chief of Medical Genetics; founding professional/medical advisor to SOFT (Support Organization for Trisomy 13/18)
  • Anchor type: award / legacy lecture
  • Day / session: Day 2 (Wed Mar 11, 2026) — Presidential Plenary, combined with ACMG Foundation Awards ceremony, Baltimore Convention Center
  • Status: post-meeting; verified recipient per ACMG Foundation PRNewswire pre-meeting announcement; lecture title and transcript TBD pending Digital Edition recording

docs.title: Headline finding
docs.text: Carey receives the 2026 David L. Rimoin Lifetime Achievement Award — the ACMG Foundation's highest honor, named for the founder of medical genetics as a clinical specialty. The citation recognizes a >40-year career spanning: creation/program-direction of the University of Utah Medical Genetics Training Program; >400 peer-reviewed articles; co-authorship of Medical Genetics and Genomics (now in its 6th edition); editorship of the American Journal of Medical Genetics (Editor-in-Chief, 2001–2016); and founding-professional-advisor role with SOFT, where Carey reshaped the clinical and ethical framing of trisomy 13 and 18 — moving the field from uniform non-intervention to individualized care.

docs.title: Methodology / framework
docs.text: Carey's contribution is clinical-genetics phenotype-first: detailed dysmorphology, longitudinal natural-history studies of underserved rare-disease populations (trisomy 13/18 most prominently), and the training-pipeline architecture (>40 years of fellows and residents) that built much of the current academic-medical-genetics workforce. The Rimoin Lecture is traditionally a career-arc keynote; specific 2026 lecture title TBD pending Digital Edition.

docs.title: Legacy impact
docs.text:
Career arc. Carey's trajectory traces the institutionalization of clinical genetics from a 1970s sub-discipline into the present sub-specialty. Trained in pediatrics with sub-specialty in dysmorphology, Carey joined the University of Utah faculty in the late 1970s and built one of the longest-running ACGME-accredited Medical Genetics Training Programs in the country. The training-pipeline contribution — >40 cohorts of fellows and residents — is the legacy his peers most consistently cite, alongside the editorial-leadership stretch at the American Journal of Medical Genetics (Editor-in-Chief 2001–2016) where he shepherded thousands of clinical-genetics manuscripts into print.

Scholarly footprint. >400 peer-reviewed articles spanning dysmorphology, natural-history studies of rare-disease populations, neurofibromatosis (Carey was a longtime NF community leader), and the trisomy 13/18 work that reframed clinical management of these conditions. Co-authorship of Medical Genetics and Genomics (now in its 6th edition) made him a canonical textbook voice for two generations of medical-genetics trainees.

Advocacy and ethics. As founding professional/medical advisor to SOFT (Support Organization for Trisomy 13/18), Carey reshaped the ethical framing of these conditions — moving the field from uniform comfort-care-only recommendations toward individualized assessment that recognized longer survival in select infants receiving cardiac surgery and other interventions. This was a structural ethical shift, not a clinical-technique shift, and it propagated into NICU practice, palliative-care literature, and disability-studies scholarship.

Forward connection. The 2026 Rimoin Lecture is delivered against a backdrop where newborn-WGS, NIFS, and SF v3.3 reporting all touch the same pediatric-genetics ethical questions Carey spent four decades shaping. Whether his lecture engages those contemporary debates directly TBD pending Digital Edition recording.

docs.title: AGBT 2026
docs.text:
Per-launch dossiers and program notes from the Advances in Genome Biology and Technology General Meeting (Marco Island, FL, February 22–25, 2026) — the sequencing-platform and spatial-genomics showcase of the year.

Status: Concluded. Build-out is queued from public coverage. AGBT runs under a closed-ish abstract policy (concurrent-session abstracts are visible to attendees but not posted publicly), so this vault uses a JPM-style "one degree removed" build: every claim is sourced to a vendor press release, GenomeWeb post, Bio-IT World story, C&EN recap, or substack/blog summary. No primary transcripts.

docs.title: Why this is in the vault
docs.text:
AGBT is upstream of every downstream tool dossier across the vault:

  • AACR 2026 posters that report Visium HD, Xenium, CosMx, or MERSCOPE data are running on platforms that were either first announced or roadmap-updated at AGBT.
  • EuroBioC 2025 Bioconductor packages (SpatialExperiment, SpatialFeatureExperiment, DESpace) consume output from these instruments — their relevance scales with whichever platform wins shelf space at AGBT.
  • GBCC 2025 tools (Voyager, spatialLIBD, SOSTA) likewise depend on the spatial-platform output formats announced here.
  • Long-read methods (PacBio HiFi/Revio, ONT PromethION) feed into structural-variant and haplotype-resolved assembly tracks at every downstream meeting.

So while AGBT itself isn't a Bioconductor or pharma-deal conference, its launches set the substrate for everything else.

docs.title: Program shape
docs.text:
AGBT 2026 ran four days at Marco Island with the customary structure:

  • Plenary sessions (mornings) — invited speakers in Genomics / AI in Genomics / Genetics & Technology / Evolutionary Genomics tracks.
  • Concurrent sessions (Tue/Wed evenings) — abstract-selected talks across Cancer, Computational Biology, Technology, and Biology tracks. Abstracts visible to attendees only.
  • Sponsor workshops — Illumina (Gold), Ultima/Bruker Spatial/Roche (Silver), plus nine Bronze workshops.
  • Poster sessions — closed (no public abstract book).

See program notes for the confirmed plenary speaker list and organizing-committee co-chairs.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• AGBT abstracts are closed-ish (visible to attendees but not posted to a public abstract server like AACR). Every claim in this vault is reconstructed from third-party coverage and vendor PR.
  • Vendor specs are routinely PR-distorted. Cost-per-genome numbers assume best-case duplex/reagent-only pricing and exclude library prep, instrument amortization, labor, and reanalysis. Treat them as ceiling claims.
  • Date/venue note: the agbt.org agenda page as fetched lists Orlando, Feb 23–26 — this conflicts with the dates/venue confirmed by the build brief and by 10times and historical record (Marco Island has been the canonical AGBT venue). Flagged on program notes for resolution.
  • Roche's Axelios 1 was announced the day after AGBT closed (Feb 26 press release) but its tech reveal happened at the meeting — treated as an AGBT 2026 launch for indexing purposes, with the press date noted.
  • 10x Genomics Atera had a roadmap preview at AGBT but its formal commercial launch happened at AACR 2026 in April. Dossier lives in the AGBT vault under "roadmap preview" with a cross-link to the AACR launch.

docs.text:
• Per build brief and historical record: Marco Island, FL, February 22–25, 2026.
  • Per agbt.org agenda page as fetched (May 2026): Orlando, FL, Feb 23–26, 2026 — with the 2027 meeting listed separately as Orlando Mar 1–4, 2027.
  • Per 10times.com listing: Marco Island, Feb 2026.

Resolution needed. The agbt.org page may have been overwritten with 2027 info after the 2026 meeting concluded, or one of the listings is for an alternate edition (e.g. Agricultural Meeting vs General Meeting). The vault uses Marco Island, Feb 22–25, 2026 per the build brief; revisit when archived AGBT 2026 program PDFs surface or after the AGBT media archive updates.

docs.title: Plenary speakers
docs.text:
Per agbt.org 2026 agenda as fetched:

Day 1 plenary — Genomics

  • William Pao (Revelio Therapeutics) — "Decoding nature: how curiosity-driven research leads to breakthrough medicines"
  • Scott Edwards (Harvard) — "How to make a flightless bird"
  • Emma Teeling (University College Dublin) — "Bats: new models of extended healthspan"

Day 2 plenary — AI in Genomics

  • Barbara Engelhardt (Gladstone Institutes / Stanford)
  • Jack Gilbert (UC San Diego)
  • Marylyn Ritchie (Medical University of South Carolina)
  • Megan Dennis (UC Davis)

Day 3 plenary — Genetics & Technology

  • Elaine Mardis (Rasmussen Institute, formerly Nationwide Children's)
  • Hilary Finucane (Harvard / Broad Institute)
  • Kathryn Paige Harden (University of Texas)

Day 4 plenary — Evolutionary Genomics & Technology

  • Katie Hinde (Arizona State University)
  • Chris Jiggins (University of Cambridge)
  • Dan Rokhsar (UC Berkeley)

Additional invited speakers indexed elsewhere on agbt.org: Elinor Karlsson (UMass Chan / Broad), Adam Phillippy (NHGRI), Neville Sanjana (NYGC / NYU).

docs.title: Cross-vault tool / talk links
docs.text:
Pre-existing vault pages that consume data from AGBT-launched platforms:

  • EuroBioC 2025 SpatialData — multi-platform spatial data abstraction; reads Visium / Visium HD / Xenium / MERSCOPE / CosMx output.
  • EuroBioC 2025 DESpace — spatially-variable gene detection on SpatialExperiment.
  • EuroBioC 2025 SpatialFDA — functional data analysis for spatial transcriptomics.
  • EuroBioC 2025 HistoImagePlot — visualizing H&E + spatial omics overlays.
  • EuroBioC 2025 OSTA — orchestrating spatial transcriptomics analysis (book/workflow).
  • GBCC 2025 Voyager — exploratory spatial data analysis (geographic data science for spatial omics).
  • GBCC 2025 spatialLIBD — Visium reference workflows.
  • GBCC 2025 SOSTA — spatial omics statistics.
  • EuroBioC 2025 themes — Bioconductor's spatial-genomics infrastructure track.

docs.title: AACR 2026 talks likely powered by AGBT-launched platforms
docs.text:
To be filled in when AACR 2026 poster-content extraction lands. Initial heuristics for the AACR poster scrape:

  • Xenium / Xenium RNA+Protein → search AACR posters for "Xenium", "in-situ", "in situ". Xenium RNA+Protein was AGBT-roadmap, mid-2026 availability — AACR 2026 (April) posters will mostly still use Xenium v1, but late-breaking abstracts may flag the multiomic upgrade.
  • Visium HD / Visium → "Visium" / "10x Visium HD" / "spatial transcriptomics".
  • Atera (10x) → unlikely to appear in AACR 2026 data (ships H2 2026), but expect prominent vendor-booth and methods-track mentions.
  • CosMx (Bruker / NanoString) → "CosMx" / "NanoString spatial".
  • MERFISH / MERSCOPE (Vizgen) → "MERFISH" / "MERSCOPE".
  • PacBio HiFi / Revio SPRQ / CiFi → "HiFi" / "Revio" / "long-read assembly". CiFi is too new for AACR 2026 data but expect methods-track posters from UC Davis collaborators.
  • Oxford Nanopore PromethION cfDNA/cfRNA → "nanopore" / "PromethION" / "cell-free RNA". Christopher Mason (Weill Cornell) and Jiwoon Park were AGBT presenters and recurring AACR poster authors — flag their AACR 2026 posters for cross-citation.
  • Element AVITI / VITARI → "AVITI" / "Element Biosciences" / "Avidity sequencing".
  • Ultima UG200 → "Ultima" / "single-end" + cancer cohort scale (Ultima's pitch is cohort-scale exome/WGS).
  • DNBSEQ-T7+ (Complete Genomics) → "DNBSEQ" / "MGI" / "T7".
  • Roche Axelios → too new for AACR 2026 data (formal launch summer 2026); expect vendor-booth presence only.

Once the AACR poster bulk-extract runs, populate program-notes.md with the matched poster IDs.

docs.title: GBCC 2025 / Bioconductor cross-refs
docs.text:
The Bioconductor spatial stack (SpatialExperiment, SpatialFeatureExperiment, Voyager, spatialLIBD, SOSTA, SpatialData) is platform-agnostic by design, but its release-cycle relevance scales with whichever spatial platform wins shelf space. Specifically:

  • Xenium / Xenium RNA+Protein output formats — primary consumer of SpatialFeatureExperiment + SpatialExperiment integrations.
  • MERSCOPE / MERFISH 2.0 — Voyager and SpatialData both have MERSCOPE readers.
  • CosMx (Bruker) — SpatialExperiment / SpatialData both support CosMx ingestion.
  • Atera (10x) — readers will need to be written once Atera ships H2 2026.

docs.title: Per-launch dossiers — AGBT 2026
docs.text: One page per vendor announcement. Because AGBT abstracts are closed-ish, the per-launch template is the natural unit of the vault (not the per-talk or per-tool template used elsewhere).

docs.title: Per-launch template
docs.text:
Each dossier follows this shape:

# <Platform/Launch name> — <vendor>

- Vendor / launch date / availability
- Chemistry / read length / throughput / accuracy / cost-per-Gb
- What's new vs prior generation
- Headline benchmarks (with source caveats)
- Reception / competitive context
- Cross-links to relevant tools and downstream talks

Every spec line ends with per vendor PR release dated or a third-party citation. Numbers are ceiling claims unless an independent benchmark exists.

docs.title: How to add a dossier
docs.text:
1. Create launches/<vendor>-<launch-slug>.md (e.g. launches/roche-axelios-1.md).
  2. Follow the per-launch template above.
  3. Every numeric spec line must end with a citation, e.g. *per [Element press release dated 2026-02-19](https://...)*.
  4. Flag any vendor figure that lacks third-party validation as (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  5. Cross-link to:
  6. Downstream Bioconductor packages (SpatialExperiment, SpatialFeatureExperiment, BSgenome, DESpace).
  7. Downstream AACR / EuroBioC / GBCC talks that report data from this platform.
  8. The relevant AGBT plenary or concurrent session (where attribution is possible from public coverage).

docs.title: Atera — 10x Genomics
docs.text: 10x's next-generation spatial platform: 18k-gene whole-transcriptome amplification + stackable 1k-gene panels; AGBT roadmap preview, formal launch deferred to AACR April 2026.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: 10x Genomics; roadmap preview at AGBT 2026 (Feb 22–25); formal launch at AACR April 2026; ships H2 2026 per 10x Genomics Atera PR, Apr 2026.
  • Chemistry / modality: Whole-transcriptome spatial amplification + stackable targeted panels.
  • WTA plex (PR): 18k-gene whole-transcriptome amplification per 10x Atera spec page, Apr–May 2026 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Panel plex (PR): Stackable 1k-gene targeted panels on top of WTA per 10x Atera spec page, Apr–May 2026 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • List price: $495k instrument per 10x Atera PR, Apr 2026.
  • Reagent cost: ~$2,200 per sample WTA reagent per 10x Atera PR, Apr 2026 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: Atera is 10x's first instrument to combine an unbiased 18k-gene whole-transcriptome readout with stackable 1k-gene targeted panels in the same workflow — answering the Visium HD vs Xenium "panel-or-WTA" choice with a single platform. Positioned to defend 10x's spatial franchise against Bruker CosMx mouse-whole-transcriptome and Vizgen MERSCOPE Ultra panel expansion.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
18k-gene WTA + stackable 1k-gene panels, $495k instrument, ~$2,200/sample WTA reagent (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — 10x Genomics PR, Apr 2026.

Resolution (subcellular vs single-cell), detection efficiency, and head-to-head with Visium HD / Xenium not yet in public coverage — TBD pending H2 2026 shipments.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: GenomeWeb's Q1 2026 earnings coverage frames Atera as the centerpiece of 10x's 2026 spatial refresh in a quarter of dimmed Visium / Xenium sales. AGBT 2026 served as the roadmap preview venue; AACR April 2026 was the formal launch. Strategic positioning: vs Visium HD (panel breadth) and Xenium (single-cell resolution) within 10x's own lineup; vs Bruker CosMx and Vizgen MERSCOPE Ultra externally.

docs.title: Xenium RNA+Protein — 10x Genomics
docs.text: 10x's in-situ multiomics expansion of the Xenium platform: 500-plex RNA co-registered with 28-plex protein, commercial mid-2026.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: 10x Genomics; announced at AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, Feb 22–25); commercial availability mid-2026 per GenomeWeb — AGBT showcases diversity of spatial genomics technologies, Feb 2026.
  • Chemistry / modality: In-situ multiomics — combined RNA in-situ hybridization + antibody-based protein detection on the Xenium analyzer.
  • RNA plex (PR): 500-plex RNA per GenomeWeb AGBT coverage, Feb 2026 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Protein plex (PR): 28-plex protein per GenomeWeb AGBT coverage, Feb 2026 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • List price / reagent cost: Not disclosed at AGBT — TBD.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: Xenium RNA+Protein adds an antibody-based protein channel co-registered with the existing Xenium in-situ RNA workflow. The 500-plex RNA target list is consistent with current Xenium 5K-class panels (subset selection), and the 28-plex protein channel is the first time 10x has shipped joint RNA+protein on Xenium hardware rather than requiring serial sections. Positioned to close the gap to CosMx / MERSCOPE proteomics roadmaps.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
500-plex RNA + 28-plex protein, commercial mid-2026 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — GenomeWeb, Feb 2026.

Detection efficiency, signal-to-noise for joint RNA+protein, and head-to-head comparisons to CosMx 6K / MERSCOPE Ultra not yet in public coverage — TBD pending independent benchmarks.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: GenomeWeb's AGBT spatial roundup (Feb 2026) places Xenium RNA+Protein as 10x's defensive answer to Bruker CosMx mouse-whole-transcriptome + 64-protein and Vizgen MERSCOPE Ultra. 10x's Q1 2026 earnings tie-in frames Xenium RNA+Protein and Atera as the two-pronged spatial refresh for 2026.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Bruker Spatial Biology (post-NanoString acquisition); roadmap previewed at AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, Feb 22–25); commercial availability TBD per GEN — AGBT 2026 Recap, Feb–Mar 2026.
  • Chemistry / modality: CosMx spatial molecular imager — cyclic in-situ hybridization for RNA, sequential immunofluorescence for protein, single-molecule resolution on FFPE / fresh-frozen sections.
  • Throughput (PR): Mouse whole-transcriptome panel (gene count TBD, vendor has not published a precise plex figure at AGBT) per GEN AGBT recap (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Multiomic plex: 64-plex protein co-detection on the same section per GenomeWeb — Spatial Omics roadmaps at AGBT (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Sample type: FFPE and fresh-frozen mouse tissue; specifics TBD pending Bruker's formal datasheet.
  • List price / cost-per-sample: TBD — Bruker has not published reagent kit pricing for the mouse WT panel.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: CosMx's prior human-only 6k / 18k-plex RNA panels and ~64-plex protein panels are extended into a mouse whole-transcriptome panel — the first time CosMx ships a rodent-scale WTA reagent rather than a curated human cancer / neuroscience panel. The 64-protein co-detection on the same section is the multiomic angle, mirroring the messaging 10x is using for Xenium RNA+Protein. This is also the first roadmap announcement under Bruker's post-acquisition ownership; messaging has shifted from NanoString-as-spatial-pureplay to CosMx-as-one-pillar of Bruker's CellScape + PaintScape + CosMx portfolio.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
Mouse whole-transcriptome RNA panel + 64-plex protein co-detection on the same FFPE / fresh-frozen section (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — GEN AGBT 2026 recap, Feb–Mar 2026.

No third-party benchmark dataset has been published for the mouse WTA panel as of mid-May 2026; sensitivity, specificity, and per-cell transcript-detection metrics relative to MERSCOPE-mouse or Visium HD-mouse are TBD.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: The mouse WTA panel is Bruker's direct counter to Vizgen's predesigned mouse MERFISH panels and to 10x's Xenium mouse Multi-Tissue v1 / v2 panel set. The 64-protein co-detection re-asserts CosMx's multiomic story against Xenium RNA+Protein (500-plex RNA + 28-plex protein, commercial mid-2026), where CosMx's protein plex is currently higher but Xenium's RNA plex is currently higher. The GenomeWeb roadmap recap frames CosMx-under-Bruker and Xenium as the two principal in-situ multiomic platforms going into H2 2026.

docs.title: Cross-links
docs.text:
• Bioconductor stack: SpatialData (CosMx reader), SpatialExperiment, SOSTA — all consume CosMx outputs natively.
  • Direct competitor at AGBT 2026: 10x Xenium RNA+Protein (500-plex RNA + 28-plex protein, mid-2026).
  • Sibling Bruker launches: CellScape, PaintScape — same portfolio narrative.
  • AACR 2026 cross-axis: single-cell-spatial-omics — CosMx mouse WTA opens preclinical-model tumor-microenvironment posters that previously had to rely on Visium / MERFISH mouse panels.

docs.title: CellCage — Cellanome
docs.text: Cellanome's CellCage pitches temporal single-cell tracking — repeated transcriptome readouts from the same physical cell over time — addressing the destructive-readout limitation that has dogged single-cell RNA-seq since its inception.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Cellanome; profiled at AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, Feb 22–25); roadmap (not commercially shipping at AGBT) per GEN AGBT 2026 recap.
  • Chemistry / modality: Temporal single-cell tracking — transcriptome measurement over time per cell rather than the destructive end-point single-readout of conventional scRNA-seq per GEN AGBT 2026 recap.
  • Throughput (PR): TBD — cells per run, timepoints per cell, and run-time figures not enumerated in public AGBT 2026 coverage.
  • Read length: n/a (CellCage is a single-cell sample-handling / readout platform; downstream sequencing chemistry not specified in public coverage).
  • Accuracy (PR): TBD — no per-cell capture efficiency, transcript-detection sensitivity, or temporal-resolution figures in public AGBT coverage.
  • List price / cost-per-sample: TBD — roadmap-status platform, no pricing surfaced.

Source caveat: AGBT 2026 public coverage of Cellanome is limited to the GEN recap inclusion and the program-notes line noting Gary Schroth (formerly Illumina) as CSO. Most quantitative fields are flagged TBD; (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) applies to all spec claims.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: The defining limitation of single-cell RNA-seq is that the readout destroys the cell — every dataset is a snapshot of a different population, and "temporal" inference relies on RNA-velocity modeling or pseudotime reconstruction rather than direct measurement. CellCage's pitch inverts that constraint: track the same cell across multiple timepoints, enabling direct trajectory measurement for differentiation, drug-response kinetics, and clonal-fate mapping. This places CellCage adjacent to (but mechanistically distinct from) lineage-barcoding methods like Watermelon, LARRY, and barbieQ that infer trajectories via clonal barcoding rather than direct repeated measurement.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text: TBD — no published demonstration cohort, no third-party comparison, no methods paper indexed at time of writing.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text:
CellCage entered AGBT 2026 as a category-defining roadmap announcement rather than a head-to-head competitor to a specific shipping product. The Gary Schroth CSO appointment signals serious chemistry pedigree (Schroth led Illumina's library-prep R&D for years). Conceptually adjacent platforms and methods at the same meeting / cross-conference:

  • Clonal-tracking methods at EuroBioC / GBCC — barbieQ and similar clone-tracking statistical frameworks are conceptually adjacent (both reconstruct cell-level trajectories, but barbieQ uses barcoded clonal inference; CellCage measures the same cell directly).
  • AACR axis — drug resistance / lineage tracing: CellCage's natural AACR application is direct measurement of drug-response trajectories in tumor cells (kinetics of resistance emergence per cell), competing with Watermelon and LARRY barcoding approaches that dominate current AACR drug-resistance posters.

docs.title: Cross-links
docs.text:
• Conceptually adjacent (clonal tracking): GBCC / EuroBioC barbieQ — clone-tracking statistical framework, complementary rather than directly competitive.
  • Single-cell platforms at AGBT 2026: Waters Rhapsody refresh, Codetta Concerto (different angle — multimodal bulk rather than temporal single-cell).
  • AACR axis — drug-resistance / lineage tracing: CellCage is too early-stage for AACR 2026 data posters; expect first methods abstracts at AACR 2027 / AGBT 2027 if the platform ships on schedule.
  • Bioconductor downstream: temporal single-cell data lands naturally in SingleCellExperiment with custom time-dimension annotations; trajectory tools (slingshot, tradeSeq) become direct measurement tools rather than inference tools when fed CellCage data.

docs.title: Concerto — Codetta Bio
docs.text: Codetta Bio's Concerto positions as a multimodal biomarker platform measuring DNA, RNA, and protein from the same sample — pitched as a single-instrument alternative to stacking separate genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics workflows.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Codetta Bio; profiled at AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, Feb 22–25); commercially available per GEN AGBT 2026 recap.
  • Chemistry / modality: Multimodal biomarker platform — co-measurement of DNA, RNA, and protein analytes from a single workflow per GEN AGBT 2026 recap.
  • Throughput (PR): TBD — public AGBT coverage did not enumerate samples/run or analytes/sample for Concerto.
  • Read length: n/a (Concerto is a biomarker-readout instrument, not a sequencer; outputs are analyte counts/signals, not reads).
  • Accuracy (PR): TBD — no LoD / sensitivity / specificity figures in the public AGBT 2026 trade-press coverage indexed in program-notes.
  • List price / cost-per-sample: TBD — no public list price or per-sample reagent cost surfaced in AGBT 2026 coverage.

Source caveat: AGBT 2026 public coverage of Codetta Bio is sparse — the GEN recap names Concerto in the multi-vendor sweep but does not break out chemistry or specs. Most quantitative fields here are flagged TBD pending a dedicated Codetta press release or third-party benchmark. (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) applies to all spec claims below.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: Codetta Bio is a newer entrant in the multimodal-biomarker category; Concerto is its AGBT 2026 commercial entry. The strategic differentiation versus single-cell multiomics workflows (10x Chromium multiome, BD Rhapsody, Parse Biosciences) is bulk multimodal measurement on the same physical sample without the dissociation/microfluidic overhead of single-cell methods, optimized for biomarker discovery and clinical-trial sample throughput rather than single-cell resolution.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text: TBD — no public benchmarks indexed at time of writing. Backfill when Codetta posts a methods paper, application note, or independent third-party comparison.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: Concerto sits at the intersection of two AGBT 2026 narratives: (a) the multiomics-from-one-sample push that 10x's Atera/Xenium-RNA+Protein and Bruker's CosMx + Singular's G4X are all pushing on the spatial side, and (b) the biomarker / clinical-trial-readout segment that traditionally relies on stacking ELISA + qPCR + NGS panels. For AACR-axis applications (clinical-trial biomarker panels, drug-response signatures), Concerto's pitch competes with single-cell multiome (Rhapsody, 10x Chromium multiome) on multimodal coverage and with Olink / SomaScan + RNA-seq stacks on workflow consolidation.

docs.title: Cross-links
docs.text:

  • AACR axis — biomarker / clinical trials: multimodal biomarker platforms feed clinical-trial pharmacodynamic readouts and pretreatment biomarker stratification; expect Concerto application notes to surface in AACR 2027 (too new for AACR 2026 data posters).
  • Bioconductor downstream: multimodal biomarker output naturally lands in MultiAssayExperiment for harmonized multi-modality storage.
  • AGBT 2026 lineage: Codetta Bio is profiled alongside Cellanome, Syndex Bio, and Volta Labs in the GEN AGBT 2026 recap as part of the "emerging platforms" sweep.

docs.title: DNBSEQ-T7+ — Complete Genomics (Swiss Rockets)
docs.text: The refreshed DNB short-read flagship — 48B reads / 24h across four flow cells, $100 genome list, and a new corporate parent (Swiss Rockets) announced at AGBT 2026.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Complete Genomics (announced at AGBT 2026); strategic license / acquisition by Swiss Rockets disclosed week of AGBT; shipping in US/Canada now per Complete Genomics AGBT 2026 PR and Swiss Rockets acquisition announcement.
  • Chemistry / modality: DNB (DNA nanoball) short-read SBS; four-flow-cell configuration.
  • Throughput (PR): 48 billion reads / 24h with four flow cells; ~28,000 30× human genomes per year per instrument per Complete Genomics AGBT 2026 PR (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Read length: Standard paired-end (2×150 and shorter PE configurations).
  • Accuracy (PR): Q40 per-base per Complete Genomics AGBT 2026 PR (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • List price / cost-per-genome: $800k instrument; $100 / 30× human genome; $1 / Gb per Complete Genomics AGBT 2026 PR.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: The "+" refresh is a throughput and accuracy bump on the existing DNBSEQ-T7 platform — pushing the four-flow-cell ceiling to 48B reads/24h and lifting per-base accuracy to a Q40 PR claim. The accompanying corporate change is the bigger headline: Swiss Rockets' announced license / acquisition restructures the route-to-market for MGI / Complete Genomics technology in regions where MGI has faced US import-restriction headwinds, providing the western commercial vehicle for the platform.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
• 48B reads / 24h, ~28k genomes/yr per instrument (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — Complete Genomics AGBT 2026 PR.
  • $100 / genome and $1 / Gb at the four-flow-cell configuration (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — Complete Genomics AGBT 2026 PR.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: DNBSEQ-T7+ is the $100 / genome twin to Element VITARI ($689k list, $100 / genome) — the two are the AGBT 2026 short-read lineup's joint price floor, sitting below Ultima UG200 ($850k–$1.25M) and above Roche Axelios's $750k / $150 genome target. GenomeWeb's "battle royale" recap calls out the Swiss Rockets acquisition as the policy-relevant pivot that lets Complete Genomics compete in US clinical accounts that had been hesitant on MGI-branded hardware.

docs.title: Cross-links
docs.text:
• Downstream Bioconductor tools: short-read aligners (Rsubread, Rsamtools), VariantAnnotation, methylKit for methylation workflows.
  • Direct AGBT 2026 competitor: Element VITARI (matched $100 / genome list, slightly lower instrument cost).
  • Throughput tier above: Ultima UG200. Cost-per-genome tier below: Roche Axelios 1.
  • Corporate note: the Swiss Rockets license/acquisition reshapes the regional sales footprint and is worth flagging in cross-citations to MGI / BGI Genomics commentary.
