docs.title: VITARI — Element Biosciences
docs.text: Element's high-throughput Avidity-chemistry sequencer, positioned as a $100 / genome production workhorse above the AVITI benchtop.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Element Biosciences; introduced via pre-AGBT webinar 2026-02-19; pre-orders open at AGBT; ships H2 2026 per Element press release dated 2026-02-19.
  • Chemistry / modality: Short-read sequencing-by-synthesis with Avidity chemistry (Avidite multi-base binders) on a dual-sided flow cell.
  • Throughput (PR): 10B reads per run; 3 TB of data per 2×150 dual-sided run per Element 2026-02-19 PR (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Read length: 2×75 and 2×150 at launch; 2×300 on the 2026 roadmap per Element 2026 innovation roadmap.
  • Accuracy (PR): >90% of bases at Q30 per Element 2026-02-19 PR (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • List price / cost-per-genome: $689k list; $100 / 30× human genome; $1 / Gb per Element 2026-02-19 PR.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: VITARI is Element's first high-throughput instrument, sitting above the benchtop AVITI / AVITI24 line. It moves Avidity chemistry onto a dual-sided flow cell at production scale, with output and per-genome economics targeted at NovaSeq X-class workloads rather than benchtop research. Roadmap items (2×300, expanded read structures) signal that Element is positioning VITARI as the long-term replacement for sites running both Element and Illumina production fleets.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
• 10B reads / run; 3 TB per 2×150 dual-sided run (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — Element 2026-02-19 PR.
  • $100 / 30× genome, $1 / Gb at the headline run configuration (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — Element 2026-02-19 PR.

  • 90% of bases at Q30 across the dual-sided 2×150 run (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — Element 2026-02-19 PR.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: VITARI shares the $100/genome price floor with Complete Genomics' DNBSEQ-T7+ and undercuts Illumina NovaSeq X / Ultima UG200 on instrument list price ($689k vs $850k–$1.25M for UG200 and ~$1.25M+ for NovaSeq X). GenomeWeb's "battle royale" AGBT recap frames VITARI as Element's first credible challenge to Illumina at production scale; the Element AGBT recap blog emphasizes booth traffic but does not publish third-party benchmark data.

docs.title: Cross-links
docs.text:
• Downstream Bioconductor tools: short-read aligners and variant callers (Rsubread, VariantAnnotation, methylKit for methylation panels).
  • Direct competitors in the AGBT 2026 lineup: Complete DNBSEQ-T7+ (price twin), Ultima UG200 (throughput competitor), Illumina TruPath (NovaSeq X synthetic long-read sidegrade).
  • AACR / EuroBioC tie-ins: Element AVITI is a recurring data source in AACR cancer-genomics posters; AACR 2026 posters tagged "AVITI" / "Element Biosciences" / "Avidity" will be the first cohort where VITARI-era workflows could surface in late-breaking abstracts.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor: Illumina
  • Launch date / venue: AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, FL, Feb 22–25, 2026)
  • Availability: Early access H2 2026; broad rollout TBD per Illumina AGBT 2026 conference page
  • Modality: Duplex chemistry kit for NovaSeq X (instrument-compatible, kit-only)
  • Target accuracy: Q70 duplex per Illumina AGBT 2026 PR (vendor PR — no independent benchmark)
  • List price: TBD (kit-only; no new instrument capex)

docs.title: What's new
docs.text: Q70 duplex kits are a chemistry upgrade for the installed NovaSeq X / X Plus base — no instrument swap required. The pitch is a 100× error-rate reduction over conventional Q40 short-read calls by using duplex (both strands of a molecule) consensus, putting Illumina in direct accuracy contention with PacBio HiFi and Roche Axelios SBX duplex on per-base error, while retaining NovaSeq throughput economics.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
• Q70 target accuracy — vendor ceiling claim; no third-party concordance or rare-variant validation has been disclosed at AGBT per Illumina AGBT 2026 page (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Throughput / cost-per-Gb impact vs. standard NovaSeq X kits not yet quantified in public materials.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: Q70 is Illumina's accuracy-ceiling answer to Roche Axelios 1 (Q38 duplex, long-read SBX) and PacBio SPRQ-Hq (HiFi at SMRT-cell-reuse economics). Because it ships on installed NovaSeq X fleets, the switching cost for existing high-throughput labs is reagent-only, which trade press flagged as the strategically important detail of Illumina's AGBT 2026 announcement bundle per GEN AGBT 2026 recap.

docs.text:

docs.title: TruPath — Illumina
docs.text: Illumina's synthetic long-read add-on for NovaSeq X — phasing short reads into long-range "constellation mapped reads" at $395 / genome list.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Illumina; announced at AGBT 2026 and shipping per Illumina AGBT 2026 event page.
  • Chemistry / modality: Synthetic long-read workflow on existing NovaSeq X — short reads are tagged and computationally reassembled into phased "constellation mapped reads" spanning kilobase-scale haplotypes.
  • Throughput (PR): 16 human genomes per day per NovaSeq X under the TruPath workflow per Illumina AGBT 2026 page (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Read length: Native short reads (2×150 NovaSeq X), phased into long-range constellation mapped reads.
  • Accuracy (PR): NovaSeq X base-call Q-scores carry through (Illumina has not published a TruPath-specific per-base accuracy figure) (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • List price / cost-per-genome: $395 / genome at the TruPath workflow configuration per Illumina AGBT 2026 page.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: TruPath is a chemistry + bioinformatics layer on top of the existing NovaSeq X — Illumina's answer to PacBio HiFi and Oxford Nanopore for haplotype phasing and structural-variant resolution without buying a separate long-read instrument. It is the consumer-side counterpart to Illumina's separately previewed Q70 duplex chemistry roadmap (early access H2 2026). GenomeWeb's spatial / multiomics AGBT recap frames the combined TruPath + Q70 + spatial announcement as Illumina's broadest single-AGBT release in years.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
• 16 genomes / day per NovaSeq X under the TruPath workflow at $395 / genome (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — Illumina AGBT 2026 page.

Independent benchmark data on phasing accuracy, SV recall, and effective long-range read length has not yet surfaced — third-party validation gap noted.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: TruPath competes with PacBio HiFi / Revio SPRQ (native long-read at HiFi accuracy, ~$300 / genome with SPRQ-Nx per Bio-IT World JPM 2026 coverage) on cost, and with Oxford Nanopore on read length. Illumina's bet is that most NovaSeq X sites would rather add a synthetic long-read chemistry than acquire a separate long-read instrument. The companion Q70 duplex kits (early access H2 2026) target the duplex-accuracy floor that PacBio HiFi and Roche SBX have been pulling toward.

docs.text:

  • Native long-read competitor in this AGBT lineup: PacBio CiFi and Revio SPRQ-Hq.
  • Companion Illumina roadmap item: Q70 duplex kits (separate dossier row in launches/index.md).

docs.title: PromethION cfDNA/cfRNA multi-omic — Oxford Nanopore Technologies
At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor: Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT)
  • Launch date / venue: Roadmap preview at AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, FL, Feb 22–25, 2026)
  • Availability: Roadmap — not shipping at AGBT 2026 per ONT AGBT 2026 page
  • Modality: PromethION-class long-read nanopore, optimised for combined cfDNA + cfRNA from a single liquid-biopsy sample
  • Throughput: PromethION-class (per-flow-cell output unchanged from current PromethION Plus generation) per ONT AGBT 2026 messaging
  • Accuracy: Q38 duplex target per ONT roadmap (vendor PR — no independent benchmark)
  • List price: TBD

docs.title: What's new
docs.text: ONT's pitch is a single PromethION workflow that interrogates cfDNA and cfRNA simultaneously from one liquid-biopsy draw, with native methylation and base modifications preserved. The roadmap also targets Q38 duplex accuracy, narrowing ONT's historical accuracy gap with HiFi and SBS chemistries while keeping native-long-read advantages (single-molecule methylation, structural variants, fusion detection).

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
• Q38 duplex accuracy target — roadmap claim, no independent dataset released at AGBT 2026 per ONT AGBT 2026 conference page (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • cfDNA + cfRNA co-extraction yield, LOD for low-frequency variants, and matched ctDNA-panel concordance not yet disclosed publicly.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: The cfDNA/cfRNA multi-omic angle puts ONT directly into the liquid-biopsy / MRD lane dominated by short-read incumbents (Illumina-powered Guardant / Natera / Tempus pipelines, plus Element AVITI cfDNA assays). ONT's differentiator is native methylation + long-read structural variant / fusion calling from the same molecules. Roadmap status means AGBT 2026 was about positioning, not benchmark data — expect first independent data at ASHG 2026 or AACR 2027 timelines.

docs.text:

  • Output: Chromosome-scale de novo assembly from 1 SMRT cell per PacBio CiFi PR (vendor PR — no independent benchmark)
  • Accuracy: HiFi base accuracy retained, Q≥30 per base per PacBio CiFi PR
  • Price: Reagent-only (consumes existing Revio SMRT cell footprint)

docs.title: What's new
docs.text: CiFi captures 3D chromatin proximity ligations (like Hi-C) but reads them on Revio as HiFi long reads rather than on a short-read sequencer. The combination of HiFi base accuracy and proximity signal collapses what historically required separate HiFi + short-read Hi-C runs into a single SMRT cell run, dropping chromosome-scale assembly cost and turnaround for non-model organism genomics.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text: • Chromosome-scale assembly of human and selected non-human references from a single SMRT cell — disclosed in the PacBio/UC Davis announcement; independent N50 / haplotype-resolution metrics from non-UC-Davis groups not yet published as of AGBT per PacBio CiFi PR (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: CiFi targets the de novo / pangenome / conservation genomics segment where Hi-C scaffolding is mandatory. By eliminating the short-read Hi-C arm, it tightens PacBio's grip on the chromosome-scale-assembly workflow and complements SPRQ-Hq's per-genome economics for population-scale long-read.

docs.text: PureTarget brings capture-based enrichment — long the standard for short-read clinical panels — to PacBio Revio HiFi reads. The combination targets clinical-genomics use cases that need both deep targeted coverage and long-read phasing / SV / methylation: pharmacogenomics, repeat expansions, HLA, large structural variants, and full-gene phasing of clinically relevant loci where short-read panels lose information.

docs.text: PureTarget is PacBio's clinical-genomics wedge: it brings long-read advantages (phasing, structural-variant resolution, methylation) into the targeted-panel workflows that drive most clinical sequencing volume today. Direct competitors include Twist / IDT short-read clinical panels and Oxford Nanopore adaptive-sampling targeted approaches; the differentiator is HiFi accuracy on capture.

docs.title: Axelios 1 — Roche
docs.text: Roche's nanopore "sequencing by expansion" (SBX) platform, pitched at a $150 / 30× duplex human genome.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Roche; revealed at AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, Feb 22–25); pre-orders open post-AGBT; formal commercial launch summer 2026 per GenomeWeb coverage dated Feb 2026.
  • Chemistry / modality: Nanopore sequencing-by-expansion (SBX) — template DNA is enzymatically expanded into a longer, more discriminable polymer before nanopore readout.
  • Throughput (PR): 16 human genomes per run per GenomeWeb / Roche AGBT release (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Read length: Average duplex ~230–250 bp per GenomeWeb Feb 2026.
  • Accuracy (PR): Q38 duplex per GenomeWeb Feb 2026 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • List price / cost-per-genome: $750k instrument; $150 per 30× duplex genome; $0.06 per million reads simplex per GenomeWeb Feb 2026.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: Axelios is Roche's first commercial sequencer since exiting 454 — a wholly new modality rather than an incremental upgrade. SBX expands template DNA into a longer reporter polymer that is then read on a nanopore, decoupling read accuracy from native base-by-base translocation speed and giving Roche a route to compete on cost-per-genome rather than read length.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
16 human genomes per run, average duplex 230–250 bp, Q38 duplex, $150 / 30× duplex genome (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — GenomeWeb, Feb 2026.

omicsomics' run-pricing teardown (Mar 2026) argues the $150 headline is conditional on full-run utilization and that effective cost rises sharply at lower batch sizes.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: Roche entered AGBT 2026 as the most-watched re-entrant; the $150 genome anchors the lower bound of the AGBT 2026 short-read lineup alongside Element VITARI and Complete DNBSEQ-T7+ (both at $100/genome list). Vilella Part 2 flags the short duplex length (~230–250 bp) as the strategic weakness vs Element / Ultima / Complete on long-insert applications.

docs.title: Pyxa — Stellaromics
docs.text: Stellaromics debuts Pyxa at AGBT 2026 as the "first commercial 3D spatial imager," opening a category that until now has been research-prototype-only.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Stellaromics; AGBT 2026 newcomer launch (Marco Island, Feb 22–25); commercial availability and pre-order terms TBD per GEN AGBT 2026 recap, Feb–Mar 2026.
  • Chemistry / modality: 3D spatial imaging — specifics (probe chemistry, optical sectioning approach, z-resolution) TBD; Stellaromics's AGBT messaging emphasizes "first commercial 3D spatial imager" without disclosing the underlying assay class per GEN AGBT recap (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).

  • List price / cost-per-sample: TBD.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: Pyxa is a category launch rather than an incremental refresh. Existing commercial spatial imagers (Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE, Visium HD) are all 2D — they image thin tissue sections and reconstruct neighborhoods within a single z-plane. Pyxa's pitch is to image native 3D tissue volumes and produce single-molecule data with true z-coordinates, which would let users study tumor architecture, vascular branching, and tissue-scale gradients that 2D platforms see only by serial-section reconstruction. Independent of how the chemistry actually works (which Stellaromics has not disclosed at AGBT), the marketing position is "the first 3D entrant," with Bruker's PaintScape as the most directly comparable roadmap claim from an incumbent.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
"First commercial 3D spatial imager" (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — GEN AGBT 2026 recap, Feb–Mar 2026.

No third-party benchmark, no spec table, no demo dataset URL has been published as of mid-May 2026. Stellaromics's category-defining claim is unverifiable from public sources at this point; AACR 2026 and follow-on user-group meetings are the next likely venues for spec disclosure.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: Stellaromics is a category-creating newcomer and was covered as one of the AGBT 2026 spatial surprise stories alongside Singular Genomics G4X and the Bruker / NanoString consolidation. The most directly comparable claim is Bruker PaintScape, which Bruker positions as "3D genome visualization" on its spatial roadmap. The two are likely to converge into a 3D-spatial subcategory over 2026–2027; until either ships, both are roadmap-only. The GenomeWeb spatial recap places Stellaromics squarely in the "AGBT showcased the diversity of spatial genomics" narrative arc.

docs.title: mcPCR — Syndex Bio
docs.text: Syndex Bio's mcPCR ("methyl-copying PCR") co-amplifies DNA sequence and methylation in a single reaction, sidestepping the bisulfite-conversion damage that has constrained methylation sequencing since the 1990s.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Syndex Bio; profiled at AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, Feb 22–25); roadmap (not commercially shipping at AGBT) per GEN AGBT 2026 recap.
  • Chemistry / modality: Methyl-copying PCR — single-reaction co-amplification of DNA sequence and methylation state, preserving methyl-mark information through amplification without bisulfite or enzymatic conversion per GEN AGBT 2026 recap.
  • Throughput (PR): TBD — reactions/run and amplicons/reaction not enumerated in public AGBT 2026 coverage.
  • Read length: n/a (mcPCR is a library-prep / amplification chemistry; read length is set by downstream sequencer choice).
  • Accuracy (PR): TBD — no per-CpG methylation-call accuracy, no conversion-efficiency-equivalent metric, no comparison to bisulfite / EM-seq / TAPS in public AGBT coverage.
  • List price / cost-per-sample: TBD — roadmap-status reagent kit, no pricing surfaced.

Source caveat: AGBT 2026 public coverage of Syndex Bio is limited to the GEN recap inclusion. All quantitative fields are flagged TBD; (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) applies to all spec claims.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text:
Methylation sequencing has historically required converting DNA before sequencing — bisulfite (Frommer 1992) degrades 90%+ of input, EM-seq (NEB) and TAPS (Cambridge Epigenetix) reduce damage but still require a chemical/enzymatic conversion step. mcPCR's pitch is to preserve methyl marks through amplification rather than reading them off a converted template, which would:

  • Reduce input requirements (relevant for liquid-biopsy cfDNA workflows where input is the binding constraint).
  • Preserve sequence context (no C→T conversion ambiguity).
  • Co-amplify sequence + methylation in one reaction (vs running parallel WGS + WGBS libraries).

The strategic positioning is liquid-biopsy methylation panels and cancer early-detection cfDNA workflows.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text: TBD — no published demonstration cohort, no comparison to bisulfite/EM-seq/TAPS on standard methylation benchmarks (e.g. SEQC2 reference, NIST methylation standards) indexed at time of writing.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: mcPCR enters a crowded methylation-prep landscape (bisulfite kits, NEB EM-seq, Cambridge Epigenetix TAPS, Illumina Infinium arrays for targeted methylation). Differentiation is on the amplification step rather than the conversion step — if mcPCR genuinely preserves methylation through PCR cycles, it would slot upstream of any methylation-aware sequencer and downstream methylation analysis stack. The natural commercial use case is cfDNA liquid biopsy where low input + multiplexed methylation + sequence calls in one reaction has obvious appeal for early-detection assays (Grail Galleri-class).

docs.title: Cross-links
docs.text:
• Downstream methylation analysis tools (Bioconductor):
  • bsseq (GBCC 2025) — methylation analysis on bisulfite-converted data; would need an mcPCR-aware import path if the chemistry ships.
  • decemedip (EuroBioC 2025) — methylation deconvolution; downstream of any methylation chemistry including mcPCR.
  • methylKit — general methylation differential analysis.
  • AACR axis — methylation / liquid biopsy: mcPCR is too new for AACR 2026 data posters; expect first methods abstracts at AACR 2027 if Syndex ships in 2026. Methylation cfDNA early-detection is one of the most-watched AACR axes (Grail, Exact Sciences, Freenome) and mcPCR's pitch lands squarely in that segment.
  • AGBT 2026 lineage: Syndex Bio is profiled alongside Codetta, Cellanome, and Volta in the GEN AGBT 2026 recap as part of the "emerging platforms" sweep.

docs.title: UG200 / UG200 Ultra — Ultima Genomics
docs.text: Ultima's wafer-based single-end SBS platform at production scale — 162 Tb/wk ceiling and Q60 ppmSeq duplex-equivalent reads, optimized for cohort-scale exome and WGS.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Ultima Genomics; presented and shipping at AGBT 2026 per Vilella Substack Part 1.
  • Chemistry / modality: Single-end sequencing-by-synthesis on circular silicon wafers using isothermal amplification; paired-end ("Solaris 2.0") on the 2026 roadmap per Vilella Substack Part 1.
  • Throughput (PR): Up to 162 Tb/week maximum; 60 wafers/week throughput on UG200 Ultra; ~1,350 genome-equivalents/week (Ultra) per Vilella Substack Part 1 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark).
  • Read length: Up to ~300 bp single-end; paired-end on the Solaris 2.0 roadmap per Vilella Substack Part 1.

  • List price / cost-per-genome: $850k (UG200 / single wafer) and $1.25M (UG200 Ultra) per Vilella Substack Part 1.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: UG200 follows the UG100 wafer-sequencer, doubling effective wafer throughput and introducing the UG200 Ultra tier (multi-wafer, ~1,350 genomes/week). Ppm­Seq accuracy moves from ~Q40 duplex-equivalent on the prior generation to Q60 on UG200, narrowing the duplex-accuracy gap with PacBio HiFi and Roche SBX while preserving the single-end / cohort-scale economics that have been Ultima's pitch since launch. The Solaris 2.0 paired-end roadmap, if it ships, would close the historical gap vs Illumina/Element for variant callers tuned to PE inserts.

Roche Axelios's $150 genome is an order of magnitude lower in instrument cost ($750k) but ships later (summer 2026). GenomeWeb's "battle royale" recap and the GEN AGBT recap both put Ultima in the "incumbent at cohort scale" position, with Element as the principal challenger.

  • Chemistry / modality: Automated library prep — digital-fluidics-based sample-to-library automation; AGBT 2026 expansion adds capability breadth and new partner-chemistry integrations per GEN AGBT 2026 recap.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text:
Callisto is already shipping; AGBT 2026 is an expansion rather than a new-platform launch. Three vectors of new news:

  1. Roche partnership. Roche's Axelios SBX chemistry (nanopore sequencing-by-expansion) requires a non-trivial template-expansion library-prep step before nanopore readout. Callisto integration positions Volta as the automation layer for Roche's first sequencer since 454. See Roche Axelios 1 dossier.
  2. Watchmaker Genomics partnership. Watchmaker's library-prep chemistry (and its broader Bronze-sponsor presence at AGBT 2026) plugs into Callisto's automation deck, broadening the chemistry menu for Volta customers.
  3. Capability expansion. Public coverage references "expanded capabilities" but does not enumerate the specific protocols or sample types added.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text:
Library-prep automation is the upstream layer for every sequencing platform in the AGBT 2026 lineup. Whichever sequencers win shelf space (Roche Axelios, Element VITARI, Complete DNBSEQ-T7+, Ultima UG200, PacBio Revio, Oxford Nanopore PromethION), the libraries feeding them have to come from somewhere — currently a mix of manual prep, Beckman/Hamilton/Tecan liquid-handlers running off-the-shelf kits, and integrated solutions (Illumina DNA Prep, MGI MGISP, etc.). Callisto's competitive positioning is:

  • vs. generic liquid-handlers (Beckman, Hamilton, Tecan): purpose-built for library prep, smaller footprint, simpler operator workflow.
  • vs. sequencer-integrated prep (Illumina DNA Prep, MGI MGISP): platform-agnostic — same instrument feeds Roche, Element, Complete, PacBio, ONT workflows once partner integrations land.
  • vs. other purpose-built library-prep instruments: the Roche + Watchmaker partnerships at AGBT 2026 are the strategic differentiator — being upstream of Roche's $150 genome is a meaningful moat.

  • Competitive: other automated library-prep instruments — Illumina DNA Prep, MGI MGISP, Tecan/Hamilton/Beckman liquid-handler-based workflows.
  • Bioconductor downstream: Callisto outputs sequencer-ready libraries — Bioconductor relevance is via the downstream sequencer's data path (e.g. Rsamtools, VariantAnnotation), not directly through Callisto.

docs.title: Rhapsody (refresh under Waters) — Waters (ex-BD)
docs.text: Waters re-introduces the BD Rhapsody single-cell multiomics platform under new ownership at AGBT 2026; the chemistry is unchanged but the portfolio framing and director-level hires are new.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Vendor / launch date / availability: Waters Corporation (acquired Rhapsody from BD); re-introduction at AGBT 2026 (Marco Island, Feb 22–25); platform is shipping as existing inventory under the new owner per GEN AGBT 2026 recap, Feb–Mar 2026.
  • Chemistry / modality: Rhapsody microwell-based single-cell multiomics — magnetic-bead barcoded mRNA capture, optional AbSeq protein co-detection, optional TCR / BCR targeted assays; unchanged from the BD-era platform.
  • Throughput / plex: Existing Rhapsody specs carry over; current figures are TBD under Waters branding (Waters has not republished a refreshed datasheet at AGBT).
  • Read length / accuracy: n/a (library output goes to a third-party short-read sequencer — typically Illumina or AVITI).
  • Personnel signal: Luciano Martelotto hired as director — flagged in program-notes.md as the most visible AGBT 2026 indicator that Waters intends to invest in the single-cell line rather than wind it down per GEN AGBT recap.
  • List price / cost-per-sample: TBD — Waters has not republished list pricing post-acquisition.

docs.title: What's new vs prior generation
docs.text: The Rhapsody instrument is essentially the same hardware-and-chemistry stack BD has shipped since the mid-2010s. What's new at AGBT 2026 is the portfolio framing: Waters is folding Rhapsody into its broader analytical-instruments business and signaling — via the Martelotto hire and the AGBT booth presence — that the platform stays alive rather than being sunset post-acquisition. Effectively a positioning launch, not a technology launch.

docs.title: Headline benchmarks
docs.text:
Existing BD Rhapsody specs carried over to Waters branding; no refreshed throughput, plex, or accuracy figure published at AGBT 2026 (vendor PR — no independent benchmark) — GEN AGBT 2026 recap, Feb–Mar 2026.

No new third-party benchmark accompanies the Waters re-introduction; cell-recovery, gene-detection, and AbSeq-protein-plex figures remain the BD-era numbers and should be treated as carry-over.

docs.title: Reception / competitive context
docs.text: Single-cell multiomics is dominated commercially by 10x Genomics Chromium at the high end and by Parse Biosciences / Scale Biosciences / Honeycomb / Fluent at the high-throughput / lower-cost end. Rhapsody's microwell architecture is a structural alternative to Chromium's droplet workflow with native AbSeq protein co-detection — historically a strong angle but commercially underexploited under BD ownership. AGBT 2026 coverage treats the Waters re-launch as a "will Waters actually invest?" question; the Martelotto director hire is the strongest answer-in-the-affirmative signal as of mid-May 2026. Indirect competition from Atera / Xenium / CosMx is now also relevant because in-situ spatial multiomics is pulling cancer-cohort budget that previously went to dissociated single-cell.

docs.text:

  • Spatial-multiomic crossover competitors at AGBT 2026: 10x Xenium RNA+Protein, CosMx mouse WT + 64-protein — both are pulling tumor-microenvironment work that historically used dissociated Rhapsody / Chromium.
  • AACR 2026 cross-axis: single-cell talks — Rhapsody + AbSeq is a recurring AACR poster modality especially in immune-monitoring and CAR-T workflows; AACR 2026 posters are still labeled "BD Rhapsody" but AACR 2027 / 2028 will see the Waters-branded reagent on incoming posters.
  • Bioconductor: standard SingleCellExperiment ecosystem applies; no Rhapsody-specific reader changes from the Waters re-brand.

docs.title: AGBT Precision Health 2026
docs.text:
Clinical-implementation, translational-genomics, and precision-medicine dossiers from the AGBT Precision Health Meeting (a.k.a. AGBT-PM) — San Diego, CA, September 14–16, 2026.

Status: Pre-meeting (T-4 months as of May 11, 2026). This vault is being scaffolded from the official conference site, the Inside Precision Medicine 10-year retrospective, and 2025 recap coverage. Full per-talk dossiers will be filled in once the agenda lands and during/after the meeting. AGBT-PM, like the main AGBT General Meeting, uses a partially-closed abstract policy — concurrent-session abstracts are visible to attendees, not posted publicly — so the build approach is the same "one degree removed" sourcing used in the AGBT 2026 vault: vendor PR, trade-press recaps, podcasts, society press releases, and PI-affiliated press.

docs.title: Why this is in the vault
docs.text:
AGBT-PM is the clinical / translational spinoff of AGBT. Where the main AGBT General Meeting is a platform-launch showcase (sequencers, spatial instruments, chemistry kits), AGBT-PM is where those platforms get used in patients: rare-disease diagnostics, newborn screening, MRD monitoring, liquid biopsy, biobank-scale population genomics, and pharmacogenomic implementation.

  • Downstream of AGBT 2026 platform launches — Roche Axelios, Element VITARI, Ultima UG200, PacBio CiFi/SPRQ-Hq, Oxford Nanopore PromethION cfDNA/cfRNA all targeted clinical workflows in their pitches. AGBT-PM is where the clinical evidence (or lack of it) for those platforms gets aired.
  • Adjacent to ASCO 2026 and ESMO 2026 liquid-biopsy and MRD trial reads — AGBT-PM sits between technology meetings (AGBT, ASHG) and oncology meetings (ASCO, ESMO, SITC), and recurring presenters here often have read-outs at all three.
  • Complements ASHG 2026 — ASHG is the academic human-genetics venue; AGBT-PM is the clinical-implementation venue. Same investigators, different framing.
  • Pulls from AACR 2026 liquid-biopsy posters — Guardant, Natera, Personalis, Tempus, Foundation Medicine all show clinical-validation data at both AACR and AGBT-PM in a given year.

docs.text:
AGBT-PM has run a consistent 3-day format since 2016:

  3. Every clinical figure (cohort n, sensitivity/specificity, PPV/NPV, OS/PFS, diagnostic yield) must end with a citation to a peer-reviewed paper, preprint, society press release, or vendor PR — never reconstruct from a tweet alone.
  4. Cross-link to:
  5. Upstream platform in ../../agbt-2026/launches/ if the program uses an AGBT-GM-launched instrument.
  6. Sibling read-outs at AACR 2026, ASCO 2026, ESMO 2026, SITC 2026, ASHG 2026.
  7. Tool / pipeline dossiers in EuroBioC 2025 / GBCC 2025 / Nextflow 2026 when the program is built on a publicly named workflow.
  8. Flag any vendor figure that lacks third-party validation as (vendor PR — no independent validation).

docs.title: Caveats specific to AGBT-PM dossiers
docs.text:
• Clinical implementation programs evolve faster than the conference cycle. A "real-world implementation" presented in September 2026 reflects data cut some months earlier. Note the data-cut date when known.
  • Patient privacy. Storytelling sessions and rare-disease case reports often include patient-family voices; do not reconstruct any patient-identifying detail beyond what the program has publicly released.
  • Vendor MRD claims are routinely PR-distorted. Each MRD vendor (Natera, Guardant, Personalis) has different limit-of-detection, longitudinal cadence, and indication-specific evidence. Compare to a common ASCO/ESMO endpoint (DFS, MRD-detection lead time) rather than vendor's preferred metric.
  • GREGoR diagnostic-yield numbers vary substantially by recruitment criteria (prior-WES-negative vs unselected, prior-WGS-negative vs WES-naive). Always include cohort selection in the dossier.

docs.title: ASCB | EMBO Cell Bio 2026
docs.text:
Cell Bio 2026 — An ASCB | EMBO Meeting · San Diego Convention Center, San Diego, CA · December 12 – 15, 2026. The joint annual meeting of the American Society for Cell Biology and the European Molecular Biology Organization — historically ~6,000 attendees, the largest pure cell-biology venue of the year.

Status: Scaffold — meeting is 7 months out as of today (May 11, 2026). The vault is being seeded now so we can move on the abstract cycle (submission site opened Apr 7, 2026; talk + early-poster deadline Jun 9; late-poster deadline Aug 4). Anything in this vault dated before Cell Bio 2026 is built from the published keynote / symposia slate, Cell Bio 2025 program shape, and ASCB-announced abstract topic categories — flagged inline.

docs.title: Why this is in the vault
docs.text:
ASCB Cell Bio is the cell-biology basic-science counterpart to the AACR clinical-and-mechanistic axis. Its overlap with the AACR corpus is modest but specific:

  1. Cancer cell biology — explicit ASCB topic category. Signaling, mitosis, autophagy, organelle biology, and cell-cycle work that lands at AACR as "mechanism of disease" sessions originates in labs that present basic findings at ASCB first.
  2. Advanced imaging and tools — ASCB is the bioimaging methods venue, where new microscopy modalities (super-resolution, lattice light-sheet, expansion microscopy, AI segmentation) and image-analysis pipelines (Cellpose, Stardist, napari, ZeroCostDL4Mic, MorphoNet) get their largest cell-biology audience. This is the methods axis that ties to MICCAI (medical imaging methods) and to EuroBioC / GBCC (image-analysis Bioconductor / Python packages).
  3. Organoids and 3D models — ASCB is one of the main venues where stem-cell-derived organoid biology and assembloid work is presented as cell-biology rather than clinical translation. Cross-links to AACR's translational organoid programs.
  4. AI / foundation models for cell biology — emerging track. Virtual-cell, cell-state, and image-foundation-model work is starting to land at ASCB alongside (and sometimes ahead of) AACR.

Hybrid template (and the design decision behind this vault): Cell Bio is neither pure-clinical (ASCO) nor pure-tools (EuroBioC) nor pure-AI (NeurIPS) — it's a basic-biology meeting where the unit of contribution can be either a biological finding (e.g., "this organelle contacts that one to do X") or a tool / method (e.g., "this new microscope / pipeline / cell line resource"). We're running one combined per-talk template in talks/ with an explicit anchor type field (tool vs cell-bio finding) — same schema, different surfaces. This matches the actual structure of the ASCB program where adjacent talks in a minisymposium can be a microscopy method and a mitosis-regulation finding.

docs.title: Program shape (verified slate + Cell Bio 2025 program shape)
docs.text:
Cell Bio 2026 runs Saturday Dec 12 – Tuesday Dec 15, four days. The structure (per ASCB 2025 / 2026 cadence):

  • Sat Dec 12 (PM): Opening Keynote + welcome reception. Subgroup meetings earlier in the day.
  • Sun Dec 13 – Tue Dec 15: Symposia + minisymposia + workshops + poster halls. Three keynote slots run across the meeting body.

  • Liqun Luo, PhD (Stanford / HHMI) — neural-circuit assembly, single-neuron tracing methods, cell-type taxonomy.

  • Tracks dominating the corpus (per Cell Bio abstract category list):

conferences/ascb-2026/
├── index.md             # this page

docs.title: What's different from the rest of the corpus
docs.text:
• Basic-science, not clinical. No drug readouts, no trials, no FDA-state surface. Cancer cell biology appears as mechanism work, not as therapeutic-class status.
  • Findings + tools in the same per-talk schema. Unlike SITC (trials/ + tools/ split) or EuroBioC (pure tools), Cell Bio mixes biological-finding talks and method-demonstration talks within the same minisymposium. The talks/ template carries an anchor field so the corpus surfaces this directly.
  • bioRxiv-mediated citation. Unlike SITC's JITC DOI per abstract, Cell Bio talks are best cited via the speaker's bioRxiv preprint. Per-talk pages should track the preprint link, not just the abstract.
  • December slot, with limited overlap. Cell Bio runs the same week as ASH (clinical hematology) and the week after SABCS (clinical breast cancer). Anyone attending ASCB is not at ASH — the corpus inherits zero scheduling conflict surface, but does inherit some readership conflict.
  • Hybrid format, smaller virtual surface than clinical meetings. ASCB has run hybrid Cell Bio meetings since 2021 but with less elaborate virtual infrastructure than ASCO / AACR — many minisymposia are in-person only.

docs.title: Cross-vault links
docs.text:
• AACR 2026 — cancer cell biology overlap. Mitosis / autophagy / cell-cycle / signaling work presented at ASCB often reappears at AACR as "mechanism of disease" sessions. Single-cell axis touches both meetings.
  • MICCAI 2026 — bioimaging methods overlap. ASCB advanced-tools track includes super-resolution and AI segmentation; MICCAI is the medical-imaging methods venue. Tool talks at ASCB frequently cite or extend MICCAI-published methods.
  • EuroBioC 2025 — image-analysis tooling overlap. Bioconductor and Python image-analysis packages (Cellpose, napari, Stardist, etc.) appear in both venues; ASCB is where they're demonstrated in cell-biology workflows, EuroBioC is where the R / Bioconductor wrappers are released.
  • CSHL BDS 2026 — overlapping early-November / December date band on biological-data-science methods.
  • Nextflow Summit — pipeline / workflow axis intersects with imaging-pipeline talks at ASCB.
  • Conferences timeline — Cell Bio's position in the year's cycle (AACR Apr → ASCO May/Jun → ESMO Oct → SITC Nov → SABCS Dec → ASH Dec → Cell Bio Dec → JPM Jan).

docs.title: Anticipated themes — top 5 to watch
docs.text: All entries below are speculative, sourced from the Cell Bio 2025 program, the keynote slate composition for 2026, AACR 2026 single-cell / spatial echo, and bioRxiv preprint pacing in the relevant areas.

docs.title: Theme 1 — Organelle contact sites as the new functional unit
docs.text:
ER – mitochondria, ER – lysosome, ER – plasma-membrane, mitochondria – lysosome contact-site biology has matured from descriptive cataloguing (2015 – 2020) into mechanism (2021 – 2024) and now into therapeutic substrate (2025 – 2026). The Hegde keynote on ER membrane biology and protein quality control sits squarely in this lineage. Expect symposia / minisymposia where:

  • Contact-site tethers (VAPA / B, ORPs, PDZD8) are characterized in cancer / neurodegeneration contexts
  • Lipid transfer at contact sites is linked to autophagy initiation and ferroptosis sensitivity
  • AACR overlap: ferroptosis-induction therapeutic strategies, autophagy modulator clinical programs

docs.title: Theme 2 — Autophagy / lysosomal biology as therapeutic mechanism
docs.text:
A continuing thread from the Cell Bio 2024 and 2025 programs. ULK1 / ATG complex regulation, selective autophagy receptors (NBR1, p62, NDP52, OPTN), mitophagy, ferritinophagy, lysosomal exocytosis. Therapeutic relevance accelerates from Deciphera, Sutro, autophagy-modulator clinical programs and the broader proteostasis / TPD axis. Expect:

  • Selective autophagy of organelles (mitophagy, ER-phagy, lipophagy) in cancer cell biology
  • Lysosomal biogenesis / TFEB axis as druggable
  • AACR overlap: KEAP1 / NRF2 axis, NSCLC autophagy-dependence sub-segments, pancreatic autophagy programs

docs.title: Theme 3 — AI / foundation models for cell biology and bioimaging
docs.text:
New surface. Cell-state foundation models, virtual-cell predictions, and image-foundation models are starting to appear in Cell Bio programs. The Luo keynote on cell-type taxonomy (single-neuron tracing) is methodologically adjacent to this thread. Expect:

  • Image-foundation models (CellSAM, MorphoNet) demonstrated on cell-biology workflows
  • Cellpose 3 / Stardist updates in tool talks
  • Virtual-cell models (CZI Virtual Cell Initiative, Tahoe-100M class) in cell-state prediction
  • AACR overlap: virtual-cells axis at AACR 2026 (ED03 educational session and topics/virtual-cells dossier)
  • MICCAI overlap: medical-imaging foundation-model work crosses into cell-bio imaging

docs.title: Theme 4 — Super-resolution + expansion microscopy + lattice light-sheet convergence
docs.text:
Imaging hardware and computational pipeline updates that are characteristic of ASCB's Advanced Tools track:

  • MINFLUX / DNA-PAINT / SMLM continued evolution and accessibility
  • Expansion microscopy with iterative protocols (e.g., 10x ExM, X10 ExM, magnify) for ultrastructural cell biology at light-microscope cost
  • Lattice light-sheet + adaptive optics in live tissue
  • Open-source image analysis (Cellpose 3, Stardist, napari plugins) and ZeroCostDL4Mic-style training resources
  • Cross-link: EuroBioC 2025 HistoImagePlot, GBCC 2025 image-analysis workshops, MICCAI 2026 medical imaging methods

docs.title: Theme 5 — Organoid / assembloid cell-state programming + regeneration biology
docs.text:
The Tanaka keynote (axolotl regeneration, blastema cell-state) frames the regeneration thread. Convergence with stem-cell organoid programs:

  • Brain / cortical assembloids and neural-circuit reconstruction at organoid scale
  • Gut, lung, liver, kidney organoid maturation and cell-state taxonomies
  • Single-cell + spatial mapping of organoid heterogeneity
  • AACR overlap: cancer organoid models in pre-clinical drug-discovery sessions
  • Cross-link: AACR 2026 single-cell axis, ASCO 2026 patient-derived-organoid trial cohorts

docs.title: Talks — Cell Bio 2026
docs.text:
The primary artifact for the ASCB vault: one Markdown file per talk at Cell Bio 2026 — across keynotes, symposia, minisymposia, and Advanced Tools sessions. Each talks/<slug>.md page captures either a cell-biology finding or a tool / method, with the same schema but an explicit anchor field that surfaces which it is.

Status: Template stub. Hybrid per-talk template carries over the EuroBioC 2025 tools structure (the closest sibling, since cell-bio talks often anchor on a tool or resource) with the anchor field added so that biological-finding talks aren't shoehorned into a tool-shaped schema. Once the program-at-a-glance posts in September – October 2026, ~30 – 50 entries get populated (4 keynotes + ~10 symposia + selected minisymposia + Advanced Tools talks).

docs.title: Per-talk entry template
docs.text:
Each talk gets its own page (talks/<slug>.md) following this structure:

# <Talk title>

**One-line summary** — what the talk reports, in plain language.

- **Anchor type:** `tool` | `cell-bio finding` | `hybrid`
- **Speaker:** <name>, <position>, <institution>
- **Lab / group page:** [link]
- **Session:** <Keynote / Symposium / Minisymposium / Advanced Tools / Workshop>
- **Day / time slot:** ...
- **Abstract:** [ASCB abstract page]
- **Preprint:** [bioRxiv DOI if posted]
- **Paper:** [DOI if published, e.g., MBoC / Cell / Nature]
- **Status at Cell Bio 2026:** <keynote / symposium feature / minisymposium / new tool release / methods talk / workshop>

(If anchor type = `tool`, also include:)
- **Tool / package / platform name:** ...
- **Repo / source:** [GitHub / GitLab / vendor link]
- **Vignette / docs:** [link]
- **Domain:** <microscopy hardware / image-analysis / segmentation / live-cell / reporter / cell-line resource / AI foundation model / synthetic biology / etc.>

## Talk at Cell Bio 2026

- **Slides:** [link if shared]
- **Video:** [ASCB YouTube link if recorded]
- **ASCB abstract:** [link]

## What it reports / what it does

2–3 sentences. For `cell-bio finding` anchor: the biological question, the
mechanism / result, the cell-biology context (organelle / pathway / cell-type).
For `tool` anchor: the problem it solves, key methodological idea, what it
consumes / produces, validation claimed.

## Where it fits in the corpus

- **AACR 2026:** [link if mentioned in an AACR talk, poster, or topic dossier]
- **MICCAI 2026:** [link if methods-overlap with a MICCAI paper]
- **EuroBioC 2025:** [link if an analogous Bioconductor package was shown]
- **GBCC 2025:** [link if mentioned in Galaxy image-analysis context]
- **Nextflow Summit 2026:** [link if pipeline / workflow cross-link]
- **CSHL BDS 2026:** [link if mentioned at the methods venue]
- **NeurIPS 2026:** [link if AI / foundation-model cross-link]

## Notes

Free-form impressions. For findings: what's new vs the 2024 / 2025 state of
the field, what comparable groups have shown, why this matters for the AACR
overlap (if cancer cell biology). For tools: benchmarks claimed, comparisons
to alternatives, sample-prep / hardware / compute requirements, license,

docs.title: Why this format
docs.text:
• Anchor field is the load-bearing piece — Cell Bio talks split roughly half between biological findings and tool / resource demos. A single schema with a typed anchor surfaces this split without forcing a forked template.
  • bioRxiv preprint field is upgraded relative to clinical templates — for ASCB, the preprint is often the citable record, not the abstract. Per-talk pages should track the preprint as a first-class field.
  • MBoC paper field — many Cell Bio talks become MBoC papers within 6 – 12 months. Surfacing this in the schema makes it easy to back-link talks to their published-paper record once those drop.
  • Cross-vault links surface the AACR / MICCAI / EuroBioC overlap directly — the corpus payoff for this vault is the cross-link to the cancer-cell-biology axis at AACR and to the image-analysis methods at MICCAI / EuroBioC.

docs.title: Open questions for the build
docs.text:
1. Keynotes vs symposia depth — keynotes get full pages with preprint + paper history; symposia probably also full pages; minisymposia covered selectively where they intersect with the cancer / tools axes. Open: how aggressively to populate minisymposium pages outside the cancer / imaging-tools tracks?
  2. bioRxiv preprint matching pre-meeting — many Cell Bio 2026 talks already have preprints posted (or will, in the Oct – Nov 2026 window). Open: build a preprint-search script to match by speaker / lab / topic into pre-populated stubs?
  3. Tools that are commercial platforms vs open-source — same Status badge treatment as SITC: Platform / vendor / open-source repo / vignette / preprint. Commercial microscopy vendors (Zeiss, Leica, Nikon, Olympus, ONI, Abberior, Lattice Bio) run industry symposia — treat as Status: vendor case-study?
  4. AI foundation-model talks — these are increasingly cross-cutting between Cell Bio's Advanced Tools track and the NeurIPS / ICML / ICLR foundation-models-for-science workshops. Open: build a unified foundation-model index across all four vaults?
  5. AACR cross-link granularity — at session level (e.g., "AACR 2026 mitosis sessions") vs at named-talk level (specific AACR talk → specific ASCB talk). Open: which is more useful as the join key?

docs.title: ASCO 2026
docs.text:
62nd ASCO Annual Meeting — McCormick Place, Chicago, IL · May 29 – Jun 2, 2026. ~40,000 attendees, the largest oncology meeting of the year.

Status: Scaffold — meeting is 3 weeks out as of today (May 11, 2026). The structure is landing now so live-coverage build (Plenary May 31, LBA-by-LBA reveal across May 29 – Jun 2) can run immediately. Abstract titles are public (released Apr 21); the regular-abstract embargo lifts May 21, 5:00 PM ET; LBAs (including all Plenary abstracts) release at 7:00 AM CT on the day of presentation. Anything in this vault dated before its embargo lift is built from company topline press releases, ASCO press-program previews, and analyst notes — flagged inline.

docs.title: Why this is in the vault
docs.text:
ASCO is the clinical-translation counterpart to AACR 2026. Same investigators, one phase later: where AACR shows the biology and the early-phase signal, ASCO shows whether it works in patients at randomized phase 3 scale. Strong overlap with AACR's clinical-trials axis — multiple plenary trials at ASCO 2026 (PROTEUS, LIBRETTO-432, HARMONi-6, Rasolute-302) have AACR 2025/2026 mechanism-of-action sessions backing them.

Format note (and the design decision behind this vault): ASCO is clinical, not tools-focused. The per-tool template that loads the EuroBioC2025 / GBCC2025 / ISMB 2026 vaults does not fit here — there are no Bioconductor packages debuting on the Plenary stage. The primary artifact for ASCO 2026 is the per-trial / per-readout entry. See trials/index.md for the schema.

The closest sibling vault in shape is JPM 2026 — also non-tools, also public-coverage-driven (no slide decks public for many sessions), also synthesis-by-day. The ASCO vault borrows JPM's "themes + day-by-day digest" pattern, but adds a per-trial detail page that JPM doesn't need (JPM doesn't have randomized phase 3 readouts).

docs.title: What we have / will have to work with
docs.text:
Source Coverage Notes ASCO Meeting Library abstract full-text (regular) post-May 21; LBA full-text on day of presentation asco.org/abstracts — primary source for the per-trial pages ASCO 2026 Program page session grid, Plenary slate, Discussant assignments asco.org/annual-meeting/program — Plenary is Sun May 31 ASCO Daily News first-pass post-session recaps, official ASCO editorial dailynews.ascopubs.org The ASCO Post weekly recap issues June – August 2026 ascopost.com OncLive / Targeted Oncology / CancerNetwork discussant-level depth, "expert reaction" video stand-ups onclive.com, targetedonc.com, cancernetwork.com Evaluate / ApexOnco / BioPharma Dive / Endpoints / STAT analyst framing, sponsor stock reactions, M&A read-through sub-required for some; STAT runs a real-time blog Company press releases toplines (often pre-embargo), full presentation decks (post-presentation) wire-service syndication via PRNewswire, BusinessWire Plenary livestream + replay full talk video + discussant ASCO Virtual; replay typically free for ~3 months post-meeting Social #ASCO26 on X / Bluesky useful for real-time room reactions; not primary

The ASCO Meeting Library is the load-bearing primary source — every accepted abstract has a permalink with title, authors, affiliations, methods, results, and conclusions. Per-trial pages should cite the abstract DOI / permalink, not the company press release.

docs.title: Program shape
docs.text:
ASCO 2026 runs Friday May 29 (Education Day) through Tuesday June 2 (closing), five days, McCormick Place West / South. The structure:

  • Plenary Session — Sunday May 31 (the practice-changing slot). Six abstracts: LBA1 PROTEUS (Erleada/apalutamide, prostate, perioperative), LBA2 SARC041 (abemaciclib, dedifferentiated liposarcoma), LBA3 LIBRETTO-432 (selpercatinib, adjuvant RET+ NSCLC), LBA4 HARMONi-6 (ivonescimab, 1L squamous NSCLC, China-only), LBA5 Rasolute-302 (daraxonrasib, 2L pancreatic PDAC, RAS), plus one TBD. Discussants for the Plenary are usually announced ~2 weeks pre-meeting; we'll capture them in program-notes.md.
  • Opening Session (Sat May 30) — Presidential Address + Karnofsky Award lecture.
  • 23 Oral Abstract Sessions + 25 Rapid Oral + 13 Clinical Science Symposia — ~450 oral abstract presentations.
  • >7,000 abstracts total (orals + posters + online-only publications).
  • Tracks dominating the corpus: GI (CRC, pancreatic, gastric), GU (prostate, RCC, bladder), Lung (NSCLC, SCLC), Breast (HR+/HER2-, TNBC, HER2+), Heme (DLBCL, MM, AML), Melanoma, GYN, Sarcoma, Symptoms/Survivorship. Cross-cutting: ADCs, bispecifics, radioligands, RAS-class inhibitors, perioperative IO.
  • Press program (separate, embargoed media briefings) Fri-Tue mornings; ASCO Daily News and STAT have AM newsletters during the meeting.

docs.title: What's different from AACR 2026
docs.text:
• No biology, no posters-on-AI-platforms. Pure clinical readouts. The AACR template (mechanism + assay + scRNA-seq cohort + xenograft + clinical-translation appendix) does not apply.
  • Public coverage is the load-bearing source, not full transcripts. Like JPM, much of what happens in the room only reaches us via trade-press editorial. Unlike JPM, every claim is backed by an embargoed peer-curated abstract — the Meeting Library makes ASCO the most-citable non-journal venue in oncology.
  • Embargo discipline matters. Anything written pre-embargo about a regular abstract is reconstructed from titles + company toplines + analyst preview pieces. Plenary LBAs only release the morning of presentation. Flag everything pre-embargo as *expected, subject to embargo* and update post-presentation.
  • Drug names are the index, not tool names. Cross-linking goes through INN / brand / mechanism (e.g., "PD-1×VEGF bispecific" links HARMONi-6 ↔ Summit ivonescimab JPM 2026 entry ↔ AbbVie RC148 deal ↔ BMS pumitamig).

docs.title: Cross-vault links
docs.text:
• AACR 2026 — the mechanism / biomarker / discovery side of the same investigator network. Many ASCO 2026 plenary trials have AACR 2025 or 2026 mechanism sessions (e.g., RAS-inhibitor preclinical at AACR → Rasolute-302 at ASCO Plenary).
  • JPM 2026 — the financing / dealmaking layer. Multiple ASCO 2026 trial sponsors were on the JPM stage in January (Lilly Retevmo / Verzenio, Pfizer Padcev, Summit/Akeso ivonescimab licensing, Revolution Medicines daraxonrasib).
  • Conferences timeline — ASCO's position in the year's oncology cycle (AACR Apr → ASCO May/Jun → ESMO Oct → ASH Dec → JPM Jan).

docs.title: Next step
docs.text:
• Now (pre-meeting, May 11–21): populate program-notes.md with the expected-LBA shortlist (~25 trials), plenary slate, and discussant watch list as named. Pre-build trial stubs for the top 10 — Plenary LBAs + frontMIND + OptimUM-02 + ALCHEMIST + KEYNOTE-B15.
  • Embargo lift (May 21, 5pm ET): drop regular-abstract full-text into trial pages. ~7,000 abstracts go public at once — batch the priority shortlist first.
  • Live meeting (May 29 – Jun 2): real-time capture per day-digest. Plenary day (May 31) is the high-priority slot — LBAs 1–5 reveal in a single 3-hour session.
  • Post-meeting (Jun 3 – Jun 30): finalize themes.md. Expected threads: RAS-class drugs become real (daraxonrasib + KRAS-G12D early-phase), perioperative IO expansion (KEYNOTE-B15, ALCHEMIST, PROTEUS), PD-1×VEGF bispecific class read-through (HARMONi-6 OS, AbbVie RC148 echo), ADC durability (ASCENT-04 PFS2), endocrine-backbone resistance (persevERA miss, SERENA-6 PFS2).

docs.title: Plenary Session — Sunday May 31, 2026
docs.text:
The Plenary is the practice-changing slot. ASCO 2026 features 5 confirmed LBAs + 1 TBD (the slate per the Aug 2025 → April 2026 abstract-acceptance and topline-disclosure cycle). All times released 7:00 AM CT morning of presentation; presentations begin ~2:00 PM CT, Hall B1.

# Trial Drug / regimen Indication Sponsor Status LBA1 PROTEUS Apalutamide + ADT vs ADT (perioperative) High-risk localized prostate (HRLPC) J&J Expected; readout long-delayed from 2024 LBA2 SARC041 Abemaciclib vs placebo Advanced dedifferentiated liposarcoma Lilly Expected; no topline yet LBA3 LIBRETTO-432 Adjuvant selpercatinib (Retevmo) Stage IB–IIIA RET-fusion+ NSCLC Lilly (Loxo) EFS positive per Lilly topline Feb 2026 LBA4 HARMONi-6 Ivonescimab + chemo vs tislelizumab + chemo 1L advanced squamous NSCLC Akeso / Summit PFS positive ESMO 2025; OS the watched endpoint LBA5 Rasolute-302 Daraxonrasib (pan-RAS) 2L pancreatic PDAC, RAS-mut Revolution Medicines mOS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo (HR 0.40, p<0.0001), per April 13, 2026 topline. The headline of the meeting if it holds. LBA6 TBD — — — Slot reserved; ASCO has historically added a 6th LBA close to date

Discussant watch list: Plenary discussants are usually announced ~10–14 days pre-meeting (so ~May 18–21). Track on asco.org/annual-meeting/program. Plenary discussant identity is itself a signal — ASCO assigns the senior-most figure in the relevant disease group, and their framing typically defines the post-meeting narrative for 6–12 months. Pre-meeting flag: the discussant slot for LBA5 daraxonrasib is the one to watch — the trial will redefine RAS-targeted therapy if the toxicity / G12-subgroup pieces hold, and the discussant will set the bar.

docs.title: Track shortlist — most-loaded tracks
docs.text: ASCO 2026 lists 23 oral abstract sessions; the following tracks are expected to dominate by abstract count and discussant attention:

docs.title: GI Oncology
docs.text:
• Pancreatic: Daraxonrasib LBA5 is the event. Plus KRAS-G12D early-phase combos (RMC-9805 / inhibitor + degrader combos previewed at ASCO GI Jan 2026).
  • CRC: BREAKWATER follow-up (encorafenib + cetuximab + FOLFIRI in BRAF-V600E mCRC, mOS 30.3 vs 15.1 mo presented at GI in Jan); amivantamab OrigAMI-1 durability data; ctDNA-guided adjuvant trials.
  • Gastric/GEJ: HERIZON-GEA-01 follow-up (zanidatamab + chemo ± tislelizumab vs trastuzumab + chemo — practice-changing at GI 2026); HER2-ADC updates.

Confirmed (sourced and dated): - Meeting dates, venue, format (ASCO.org) - Embargo policy and timing (Abstract Policies FAQ) - Plenary slate LBA1–LBA5 trial names (ApexOnco preview + per-sponsor press releases) - Topline results disclosed pre-meeting: LIBRETTO-432 EFS+ (Lilly Feb 2026), Rasolute-302 PFS+ / OS HR 0.40 (Revolution Apr 13, 2026), persevERA missed (Roche Mar 2026), frontMIND PFS+ HR 0.75 (Incyte Jan 2026), OptimUM-02 PFS+ HR 0.42 (IDEAYA Apr 13, 2026) - Selected LBA numbers (LBA1–5, LBA660, LBA1000, LBA1006, LBA1007, LBA7000, LBA8005, LBA8500, LBA9503) and their session day/time per OncLive previews

The primary artifact of this vault: one Markdown file per trial / readout. ASCO 2026 is a clinical-readout meeting, so the unit of analysis is the trial — not the speaker, not the tool, not the company.

docs.title: Cross-cutting themes (for themes.md)
docs.text:
To synthesize across trials/ once populated:

  1. RAS-class drugs become real. Daraxonrasib Plenary readout + KRAS-G12D early-phase combos. Cross-link to AACR 2025/2026 RAS mechanism sessions.
  2. PD-1 × VEGF bispecific class. Ivonescimab HARMONi-6 OS readout is the class-defining moment. Echoes AbbVie RC148 ($5.6B JPM Day 1 deal), Summit JPM presence, BMS pumitamig.
  3. Perioperative IO expands. PROTEUS (prostate), KEYNOTE-B15 (bladder), LIBRETTO-432 + ALCHEMIST (lung) — IO/TKIs moving earlier in disease.
  4. ADC durability story. ASCENT-04 PFS2 (TROP2-ADC), trastuzumab deruxtecan continued read-through, novel ADC targets.
  5. Endocrine backbone resistance. persevERA miss + SERENA-6 PFS2 — the limits of next-gen oral SERDs vs CDK4/6 + AI.
  6. China-origin assets dominate the LBA slate. HARMONi-6 (Akeso), Rasolute-302 partner activity, anbenitamab (KN026-004), WU-KONG28 (Dizal). Continuity from JPM 2026 "China is the story" thread.
  7. Radioligands move to randomized data. PEACE-3 enza+Ra-223, actinium-225 PSMA dose-escalation.

docs.title: ASCO GI 2026
docs.text:
2026 ASCO Gastrointestinal Cancers Symposium — Moscone West, San Francisco, CA · January 8 – 10, 2026. ~3,500 in-person attendees + virtual track. Co-sponsored by ASCO, ASTRO, AGA, and SSO; the dominant GI-cancer clinical-readout meeting of the year and a curtain-raiser for the GI track at ASCO 2026 (May 29 – Jun 2, McCormick Place).

Status: Retrospective vault — meeting closed four months ago (Jan 8–10, 2026). All abstract embargoes long since lifted; trial pages can cite the ASCO Meeting Library directly. Continuity link forward to the ASCO main meeting matters most here: several of the GI-track LBAs at ASCO 2026 (Rasolute-302 daraxonrasib Plenary; HERIZON-GEA-01 follow-up; BREAKWATER OS update) had their pivotal or precursor readouts at ASCO GI 2026 in January, and the discussant framing from January is the prior the May discussants will be reacting to.

docs.title: Why this is in the vault
docs.text:
ASCO GI is the subspecialty Plenary for GI oncology — the place pancreatic, CRC, gastric/GEJ, biliary, HCC, esophageal, neuroendocrine, and anal readouts land first. Roughly 700 oral + poster abstracts across three days, with a 4-track plenary-style format (CRC + anal Day 1; pancreatic + small-bowel + neuroendocrine + HCC + biliary Day 2; esophageal + gastric Day 3). The discussant culture is denser than ASCO main meeting — each oral session has a named GI subspecialist framing the data in real time.

The vault's GI sibling structure:

  • ASCO GI (Jan) — subspecialty readouts. Targeted-therapy biomarker-selected populations (HER2+, FGFR2+, IDH1-mut, BRAF-V600E, MSI-H, KRAS-G12C/G12D, claudin 18.2). Phase 1/2 dose expansion + Phase 2/3 confirmatory.
  • ASCO main meeting (May/Jun) — the broader GI track, including phase 3 OS confirmations of January's PFS readouts (e.g., Rasolute-302 Plenary LBA5 in May builds on daraxonrasib Phase 1/2 ASCO GI Jan 2025).
  • ESMO GI (Jul) — European subspecialty follow-up; later in the cycle, often EU-perspective updates.
  • ESMO main meeting (Oct) — global GI track + late-year OS readouts.

ASCO GI 2026 anchors the January end of this cycle and the discussant framing here propagates through the year.

docs.title: Program shape
docs.text:
ASCO GI 2026 ran Thursday January 8 (opening sessions, CRC + anal) through Saturday January 10 (esophageal + gastric), three days, Moscone West.

  • No formal Plenary slot (unlike ASCO main meeting). Instead, each disease group runs a General Session with the highest-impact orals: ~3–5 abstracts framed by a senior discussant, with the day's "headlines" emerging organically from these.
  • Day 1 (Thu Jan 8) — CRC, anal: CRC General Session anchored by BREAKWATER cohort 3 OS update (encorafenib + cetuximab + FOLFIRI in BRAF-V600E mCRC), CIRCULATE-NA ctDNA-guided adjuvant updates, FOxTROT-2 elderly perioperative. Anal cancer: POD1UM-303 / EA2176 retifanlimab maintenance follow-up.
  • Day 2 (Fri Jan 9) — pancreatic, neuroendocrine, hepatobiliary, small-bowel: Daraxonrasib + chemo combination updates (Revolution Medicines, ahead of Plenary LBA5 at ASCO 2026); RMC-9805 / zoldonrasib KRAS-G12D PDAC Phase 1 expansion (30% ORR, 80% DCR previously read at ASCO GI 2025; mature follow-up here). HCC: KEYNOTE-937 (adjuvant pembro, negative) + TACTICS-L (atezo-bev vs TACE intermediate-stage HCC). Biliary: REFOCUS (lirafugratinib in FGFR2-fusion CCA, ~100-patient Phase 2, durable responses); IDH1-mutant CCA combination data.
  • Day 3 (Sat Jan 10) — gastric/GEJ, esophageal: HERIZON-GEA-01 zanidatamab + chemo ± tislelizumab in 1L HER2+ G/GEJ (Jazz Pharma; positive PFS for both Ziihera arms vs trastuzumab + chemo; OS gain for IO-containing arm — practice-changing). ILUSTRO updates (zolbetuximab claudin 18.2 follow-up). Esophageal: HER2 ADC follow-ups; CheckMate-577 adjuvant nivolumab long-term.

The meeting hit 5,000+ in-person + virtual attendees (per ASCO press preview), an increase over 2025.

docs.title: What's different from ASCO main meeting
docs.text:
• Smaller, denser, more biomarker-focused. ~3,500 attendees vs ~40,000. Every abstract has a named biomarker selection criterion in the title — KRAS-G12D, BRAF-V600E, FGFR2-fusion, IDH1-R132, HER2+, MSI-H, claudin 18.2+, RET-fusion, NTRK-fusion. The era of "all-comer chemo trials" is over for GI.
  • Phase 1/2 dose-expansion data is the headline, not Phase 3. Unlike ASCO main where Plenary is randomized phase 3, ASCO GI's most-discussed abstracts are often Phase 1 dose-expansion biomarker-defined cohorts (e.g., RMC-9805 KRAS-G12D PDAC, lirafugratinib FGFR2 CCA, divarasib KRAS-G12C CRC). These define the next year's pivotal designs.
  • Discussant culture is denser. Three days, ~30 oral sessions, each with a named discussant — discussants here typically frame the field for 6–12 months until ASCO main meeting builds on it.
  • Strong ctDNA / MRD presence. CIRCULATE-NA, CIRCULATE-Japan, GALAXY, COLOMATE, DYNAMIC follow-ups — ASCO GI is where ctDNA-guided adjuvant trial design gets stress-tested before it migrates to broader oncology.

docs.title: Forward link to ASCO 2026 (May/Jun)
docs.text:
[Forward-looking — flagged] Several of the May/Jun 2026 GI-track readouts at ASCO main meeting are direct sequels to January's ASCO GI sessions:

  • Rasolute-302 daraxonrasib Plenary LBA5 (May 31) — builds on daraxonrasib Ph1/2 expansion data presented at ASCO GI Jan 2026 + AACR Apr 2026 updates. Discussant framing of "what counts as a meaningful PDAC OS improvement" was laid down at ASCO GI by the pancreatic discussant.
  • HERIZON-GEA-01 follow-up — January's pivotal Phase 3 readout (Jazz Pharma zanidatamab) generated FDA submission activity in Q1 2026; ASCO 2026 May likely sees subgroup analysis + biomarker correlates.
  • BREAKWATER continued OS maturation — cohort 3 OS readout from January (~30 vs 15 mo) will be reconciled with later follow-up at ASCO 2026.
  • KRAS-G12D combinations — Revolution Medicines' next disclosure step is at AACR 2026 (Apr) and ASCO main (May), with January's ASCO GI as the foundation.

docs.title: Format note
docs.text:
Unlike ASCO main meeting, ASCO GI has no formal Plenary slot. Each disease group runs a General Session with the highest-impact orals (~3–5 abstracts) framed by a senior subspecialty discussant. The "headlines" of the meeting emerge organically from these — at ASCO GI 2026, the consensus headlines were:

  1. HERIZON-GEA-01 (zanidatamab in 1L HER2+ G/GEJ) — Day 3
  2. BREAKWATER cohort 3 OS update (BRAF-V600E mCRC) — Day 1
  3. Daraxonrasib + RMC-9805 PDAC expansion — Day 2
  4. REFOCUS lirafugratinib FGFR2 CCA — Day 2

Plus the negative signal from KEYNOTE-937 (adjuvant pembro HCC), which preserves SOC.

docs.title: GI Oncology — Colorectal + anal (Day 1, Thu Jan 8)
docs.text:
Headline: BREAKWATER cohort 3 OS update positions encorafenib + cetuximab + FOLFIRI as new 1L SOC for BRAF-V600E mCRC.

  • BREAKWATER cohort 3 (Pfizer/Seagen). EC + FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI + bev in 1L BRAF-V600E mCRC. Response rates higher with EC; OS trending positive but data immature (~30.3 vs 15.1 mo per earlier press; full mature data pending). Neuropathy-free profile vs FOLFOXIRI is the differentiator. NCCN guideline update expected through 2026.
  • CIRCULATE-NA (CCTG CRC.10 / NRG-GI008). ctDNA-guided adjuvant design update. Co-presented by Alliance / CCTG / NRG cooperative groups; interim feasibility + randomization data.
  • ctDNA correlatives. Two abstracts — (a) ctDNA doubling time correlation with recurrence timing in resected colon cancer, (b) presurgical ctDNA prognostic value. Feeds the maturation of ctDNA as a per-trial enrollment biomarker.
  • FOxTROT-2 (UK MRC). Elderly perioperative colon cancer FOLFOX. Subgroup feasibility analysis.
  • OrigAMI-1 mCRC durability update (J&J). Amivantamab (EGFR×MET bispecific) in MSS / EGFR-amp mCRC; durability data post-AACR 2025.
  • POD1UM-303 / EA2176 anal cancer (Incyte / ECOG-ACRIN). Retifanlimab maintenance Phase 3 in advanced SCCA — possible first IO maintenance OS signal in anal cancer.

Discussant framing (Day 1, CRC): Howard Hochster (Rutgers) framed the BREAKWATER data as the moment 1L BRAF-V600E mCRC permanently leaves the all-comer chemo era. ctDNA-guided design framed by Aparna Parikh (MGH) as the path forward for adjuvant trial design.

docs.title: GI Oncology — Pancreatic, NET, hepatobiliary, small-bowel (Day 2, Fri Jan 9)
docs.text:
Headlines: RAS-class drugs become real for PDAC (daraxonrasib + RMC-9805). REFOCUS lirafugratinib defines next-gen FGFR2 selective TKI class for CCA. KEYNOTE-937 negative — preserves SOC for HCC adjuvant.

  • Daraxonrasib Phase 1/2 expansion (Revolution Medicines). Monotherapy + chemo-combo update in 1L+ metastatic PDAC. Foundation for Rasolute-302 Phase 3 Plenary readout at ASCO main meeting May 31 (mOS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.40, p<0.0001 per topline April 13, 2026).
  • RMC-9805 / zoldonrasib KRAS-G12D PDAC (Revolution Medicines). Phase 1 dose-expansion at 1200 mg QD / 600 mg BID. ORR 30%, DCR 80%, 86% of evaluable patients with >50% ctDNA KRAS-G12D decline, 39% with complete molecular clearance. First selective G12D inhibitor with PDAC activity. Sets up registrational design path.
  • KEYNOTE-937 (Merck). Adjuvant pembro vs placebo post-curative-intent HCC. Negative RFS — preserves active-surveillance SOC. Reinforces that adjuvant IO doesn't extrapolate cleanly from advanced-HCC IO success (atezo-bev IMbrave150).
  • TACTICS-L (Roche / academic). Atezo-bev vs TACE in intermediate-stage HCC. Longer time to treatment failure with atezo-bev. Challenges TACE-as-default in intermediate-stage; likely shifts patient flow toward systemic therapy earlier.
  • REFOCUS lirafugratinib (Relay Therapeutics). ~100-patient Phase 2 in FGFRi-naïve FGFR2-fusion CCA. Durable responses, favorable safety vs pemigatinib / futibatinib. Best-in-class candidate for FGFR2-selective TKIs (sparing FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia / ocular AEs).
  • IDH1-mutant CCA combinations (Servier + multiple). Ivosidenib + chemo / IO follow-up. Second-generation IDH1 strategies.
  • NETTER-2 follow-up (Novartis). Lu-177 dotatate + LAR vs LAR in 1L GEP-NET. Earlier-line radioligand use confirmation.

Discussant framing (Day 2, pancreatic): Eileen O'Reilly (MSK) framed the RAS-class signal as the inflection point for PDAC — the daraxonrasib + zoldonrasib combination data being the first credible "molecular targeted therapy in PDAC" story since gemcitabine. Discussant framing of toxicity / G12-subgroup will carry into the Rasolute-302 Plenary discussant slot at ASCO May 31. Andrew Hendifar (Cedars-Sinai) co-anchored.

docs.title: GI Oncology — Gastric / GEJ / esophageal (Day 3, Sat Jan 10)
docs.text:
Headline: HERIZON-GEA-01 is the practice-changing readout of the meeting. Zanidatamab + chemo (Jazz Pharma) displaces trastuzumab + chemo as 1L SOC reference frame in HER2+ G/GEJ.

  • HERIZON-GEA-01 (Jazz Pharmaceuticals). Phase 3 in 1L HER2+ locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. Three-arm: zanidatamab + chemo vs zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemo vs trastuzumab + chemo. Both zani arms showed statistically significant + clinically meaningful PFS improvement vs trastuzumab + chemo; the IO-containing arm showed OS gain. FDA submission triggered Q1 2026; NCCN guideline reconsideration through 2026.
  • ILUSTRO follow-up (Astellas). Zolbetuximab (anti-claudin 18.2) monotherapy + combination durability. Extends label rationale; reinforces claudin 18.2 selection biomarker.
  • HER2 ADC esophageal (T-DXd, disitamab vedotin). Durability updates in HER2+ esophageal / GEJ. Class read-through.
  • CheckMate-577 long-term (BMS). Adjuvant nivolumab post-CRT in esophageal / GEJ. Long-term DFS / OS update confirms established SOC.

Discussant framing (Day 3, gastric): Yelena Janjigian (MSK) framed HERIZON-GEA-01 as the trastuzumab-displacement moment in 1L HER2+ G/GEJ. The discussant question is now sequencing (which HER2 agent in 1L vs 2L+) and biomarker stratification (IHC 3+ vs 2+/FISH+; PD-L1 CPS interactions). Manish Shah (Weill Cornell) on the claudin 18.2 / zolbetuximab discussion.

  • Robin Kate Kelley / Ghassan Abou-Alfa — hepatobiliary. REFOCUS lirafugratinib + IDH1-mut CCA discussant continuity.

  • KEYNOTE-937 negative (Oncology News Central)
  • REFOCUS lirafugratinib ~100-pt Phase 2 durable responses (Top studies in biliary/liver at ASCO GI 2026)
  • RMC-9805 / zoldonrasib ORR 30%, DCR 80%, ctDNA clearance data (originally ASCO GI 2025; mature follow-up at GI 2026) (OncLive zoldonrasib coverage, original abstract DOI)

Speculative — flag if cited:

  • Exact mature OS / HR numbers for BREAKWATER cohort 3 (data not yet fully mature at January readout)
  • Discussant identity exact attributions for individual sessions (sourced from post-meeting recaps; primary-source slide deck attribution preferred when accessible)
  • Forward toplines to ASCO 2026 (May/Jun) sequels — pre-embargo for the May meeting

docs.title: Dead ends
docs.text:
• Full slide decks for individual oral presentations: ASCO Meeting Library publishes abstracts but slide decks are session-by-session and gated behind ASCO Virtual registration for many sessions. Trade-press summaries are the proxy.
  • Discussant slide content: discussant commentary is typically not published — captured via VJOncology / OncLive video standups and ASCO Daily News editorial only.
  • JCO publication delay for individual abstract pages: the JCO 4_suppl 2026 issue is the canonical citation source but individual DOIs were minted on the date of session; some abstracts published only as meeting library permalinks.

docs.title: Trials — ASCO GI 2026
docs.text:
The primary artifact of this vault: one Markdown file per trial / readout. ASCO GI 2026 is a clinical-readout meeting (Jan 8–10, 2026, Moscone West, San Francisco), so the unit of analysis is the trial — not the speaker, not the tool, not the company. Mirrors the ASCO 2026 trials template.

Status: Template + retrospective master index. Per-trial pages are deferred in May 2026 — priority is the ASCO main-meeting vault (asco-2026/) running live May 29 – Jun 2. The master index below captures the January readouts so forward cross-links from the May meeting (e.g., Rasolute-302 Plenary LBA5 builds on daraxonrasib Phase 1/2 here) resolve cleanly. Full per-trial pages can be backfilled from the ASCO Meeting Library on demand.

docs.title: Per-trial template
docs.text:
Each trial file (e.g., breakwater-cohort3.md) follows the same schema as ASCO 2026. Copy and fill:

# <Trial acronym / name> — <Drug regimen, indication, line>

> **Abstract:** <abstract #, e.g., LBA438> · **Session:** <session name, date, time PT, hall> · **JCO 4_suppl DOI:** <10.1200/JCO.2026.44.4_suppl.XXX>

## At a glance

- **Sponsor:** <pharma / cooperative group>
- **PI / presenter:** <name, institution>
- **NCT ID:** <NCTxxxxxxxx>
- **Phase:** <1 / 2 / 3 / 1-2 / 2-3>
- **Design:** <arms, randomization, blinding>
- **N:** <enrolled / analyzed>
- **Primary endpoint(s):** <PFS / OS / ORR / DCR / DoR / pCR>
- **Comparator:** <SOC / placebo / active comparator>
- **Indication:** <tumor type, subtype, biomarker selection>
- **Line:** <neoadjuvant / adjuvant / 1L / 2L / 3L+ / perioperative>

<One paragraph. Numbers + HR + p-value. Cite JCO 4_suppl DOI for post-meeting data.>

unmet need, prior SOC.>

docs.title: Cross-cutting themes
docs.text:
To synthesize across trials/ if/when populated:

  1. HER2+ G/GEJ — zanidatamab arrives. HERIZON-GEA-01 is the practice-changing readout of the meeting. Trastuzumab + chemo is no longer the SOC reference frame in 1L HER2+ G/GEJ. FDA filing motion + payer / NCCN follow-on through 2026.
  2. KRAS-class drugs become real in PDAC. Daraxonrasib (pan-RAS) Phase 1/2 update sets up Rasolute-302 Plenary at ASCO May 31. RMC-9805 / zoldonrasib (G12D-selective) PDAC activity is the next-class signal. Cross-link to AACR 2025/2026 RAS mechanism sessions and Revolution Medicines JPM 2026 presentation.
  3. BRAF-V600E mCRC moves to first-line. BREAKWATER cohort 3 (EC + FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI + bev) is the new 1L benchmark, displacing FOLFOXIRI + bev for biomarker-selected patients. Neuropathy-free profile is the practical edge.
  4. FGFR2-fusion CCA — second-generation TKIs. Lirafugratinib (REFOCUS) vs pemigatinib / futibatinib SOC; selective FGFR2 sparing FGFR1 toxicity. Class differentiation by hyperphosphatemia / ocular AE profile.
  5. Adjuvant IO in HCC fails (KEYNOTE-937). Preserves SOC. Bears on the broader perioperative-IO theme threading ASCO 2026 (KEYNOTE-B15 bladder, PROTEUS prostate, LIBRETTO-432 lung, ALCHEMIST).
  6. ctDNA-guided adjuvant designs mature. CIRCULATE-NA + correlative ctDNA presurgical / doubling-time data continue the DYNAMIC / GALAXY thread; will feed next-cycle CRC adjuvant trial design.
  7. Anal cancer gets its first IO maintenance signal. POD1UM-303 / EA2176 retifanlimab — small but real for a long-neglected disease.
