docs.title: Cross-cutting themes (for program-notes.md)
docs.text:
To synthesize across the trial list:

  1. ADC era arrives in gyn-onc. Six distinct ADC targets with 2026 clinical efficacy data: FRα (mirvetuximab — moving earlier into PSOC), CDH6 (raludotatug deruxtecan — first signal), B7-H4 (puxitatug samrotecan AZD8205 — first-in-human), B7-H3 (BNT-324), TROP2 (sacituzumab tirumotecan, IBI130), tissue factor (tisotumab vedotin). This is the AACR ADC linker-chemistry-payload mechanism story landing in the clinic.
  2. Glucocorticoid receptor antagonism is a class. ROSELLA's Lifyorli win (relacorilant) is the first GR-antagonist solid-tumor Phase 3 win — a new class with read-through to cortisol-axis biology across hormone-receptor-modulated cancers.
  3. Chemo-immunotherapy 1L is now SOC across all three gyn cancers. RUBY (endometrial dostarlimab), KEYNOTE-A18 (cervical pembro + CCRT), KEYNOTE-B96 (ovarian platinum-resistant pembro). Mature OS data at SGO 2026 closed the loop on this SOC shift.
  4. Cooperative-group multi-region sponsorship. ROSELLA alone has five cooperative-group sponsors (GOG / ENGOT / APGOT / LACOG / ANZGOG). This authorship density is a unique gyn-onc structural feature versus other oncology subspecialties.
  5. Biomarker-defined subgroups dominate. dMMR/MSI-H, FRα+, BRCA, HRD, KRAS-mut LGSOC, B7-H4+, CDH6+, PD-L1+, p53-abn, POLE-mut — every Phase 3 in 2026 reports a molecular subgroup. The "all-comer" gyn-onc trial era is over.
  6. China-origin assets surface. IBI130 (Innovent anti-TROP2), BNT-324 (BioNTech B7-H3 — Mainz/Berlin biotech), and the AZ / Daiichi global ADCs all cross-list with US trade-press. Echo of the JPM 2026 "China is the story" thread.
  7. Surgical innovation gets a Plenary. SGO's preservation of a dedicated surgical-innovation Plenary distinguishes it from ASCO/ESMO; sentinel-node, robotic, and fertility-sparing data here often inform NCCN surgical guidelines directly.

docs.title: BLUESTAR — Puxitatug samrotecan (AZD8205, B7-H4 ADC) in advanced/metastatic endometrial cancer
docs.text:
Abstract: LBA, Phase 1/2a · Session: Sunday April 12, 2026 · Simultaneous publication: TBD (likely JCO or Annals of Oncology)

Headline: First-in-human B7-H4 ADC clinical efficacy data — ORR 34.6% @ 2.0 mg/kg and 38.5% @ 2.4 mg/kg in endometrial cancer with mPFS 7.0 mo, opening a new ADC target class with read-through to breast and ovarian.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Sponsor: AstraZeneca (AZD8205)
  • PI / presenter: Stephanie Gaillard, MD (Johns Hopkins)
  • NCT ID: NCT05123482
  • Phase / arms / N: Phase 1/2a basket; endometrial cohort dosed at 2.0 mg/kg and 2.4 mg/kg Q3W
  • Primary endpoint(s): ORR (RECIST 1.1), safety, PK
  • Indication / line: Advanced/metastatic endometrial cancer, post-platinum and post-IO
  • Comparator: None (single-arm dose-cohort)
  • Session: LBA, Day 3 (Apr 12)

docs.title: Headline result
docs.text: In the endometrial cohort, ORR 34.6% at the 2.0 mg/kg dose and 38.5% at 2.4 mg/kg, with 12-week DCR of 80.8% and 84.6% respectively. mPFS 7.0 months. Manageable safety profile consistent with topoisomerase-1 ADC class. First clinical efficacy data for the B7-H4 ADC class.

docs.title: Mechanism / class
docs.text: Puxitatug samrotecan (AZD8205) is an antibody-drug conjugate targeting B7-H4 (VTCN1) — a B7-family immune checkpoint ligand highly expressed in endometrial, breast (TNBC), and ovarian cancer with limited normal-tissue expression. Payload is a proprietary AstraZeneca topoisomerase-1 inhibitor with a cleavable linker. First-in-class B7-H4 ADC to report meaningful clinical efficacy.

docs.title: Trial design deep dive
docs.text:
Study architecture: Phase 1/2a multi-tumor basket (BLUESTAR), with the endometrial cohort dosed at 2.0 mg/kg and 2.4 mg/kg Q3W as parallel dose-expansion arms. Single-arm design — no comparator at this stage. Patients required prior platinum and prior IO; B7-H4 IHC selection criteria TBD per cohort protocol (some BLUESTAR cohorts are all-comer with retrospective B7-H4 stratification, others enrich prospectively).

Endpoint definitions: ORR by RECIST 1.1 (primary, with both blinded independent central review and investigator-assessed readouts reported); safety per CTCAE v5; PK and immunogenicity as supporting endpoints. DCR at 12 weeks reported as an early activity signal. DOR and PFS as secondary; OS is exploratory at this Phase 1/2a stage.

Key subgroup analyses: Dose comparison (2.0 vs 2.4 mg/kg) is the core analysis informing the recommended Phase 2 dose — 38.5% ORR at the higher dose vs 34.6% at lower, against a tolerability gradient. B7-H4 IHC expression-by-response correlation TBD in poster appendix. Histology (endometrioid vs serous vs carcinosarcoma) and prior-line subgroups reserved for ASCO/ESMO follow-up.

Comparator context: No randomized comparator, but the 34–38% ORR sits favorably against current second-line endometrial benchmarks (~15–25% ORR for chemo, ~20–25% for dostarlimab in MMRp). The historical benchmark anchors the registration-enabling Phase 3 dose and comparator selection.

FDA implications: Pre-pivotal — establishes the B7-H4 ADC class and informs a registration-enabling Phase 3 design (TBD whether vs investigator-choice chemo or in combination). Project Optimus dose-optimization framework will apply.

docs.title: Discussant takeaway
docs.text: Per OncLive coverage: the 34.6–38.5% ORR in heavily pretreated endometrial sits comparable to current second-line standards and marks B7-H4 as a tractable ADC target. IHC-based patient selection (B7-H4+) is feasible and was used in BLUESTAR.

docs.title: Practice-changing verdict
docs.text: No (early-phase), but pivotal-design-defining. BLUESTAR establishes the B7-H4 ADC class clinically and sets the stage for a registration-enabling Phase 3 expansion. AZ presented the basket BLUESTAR design at AACR 2026 (one week after SGO) anchoring ovarian and breast cohorts.

docs.title: InnovaTV 205 Arm H — Tisotumab vedotin + carboplatin + pembrolizumab ± bevacizumab in 1L recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer
docs.text:
Abstract: Phase 2 cohort · Session: Monday April 13, 2026 (cervical Plenary V) · Simultaneous publication: TBD (Gynecologic Oncology)

Headline: Tisotumab vedotin (Tivdak) combined with carboplatin + pembrolizumab ± bevacizumab delivers ORR 66% with median DOR 13 months in 1L recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer — moving TV into the 1L combination space alongside chemo-IO.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Sponsor: Pfizer / Seagen · Genmab (innovaTV / Tivdak program)
  • PI / presenter: Apr 13 Plenary V (presenter TBD)
  • NCT ID: NCT03786081 (InnovaTV 205)
  • Phase / arms / N: Phase 2 multi-cohort; Arm H = tisotumab vedotin + carboplatin + pembrolizumab ± bevacizumab in 1L recurrent/metastatic
  • Primary endpoint(s): ORR, DOR
  • Indication / line: 1L recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer
  • Comparator: None (single-arm cohort)
  • Session: Plenary V (Day 4, Apr 13)

docs.title: Headline result
docs.text: Confirmed ORR 66%, median DOR 13 months in Arm H. Safety profile manageable and consistent with the known TV ocular and peripheral neuropathy AE profile, plus expected chemo-IO toxicities. The result positions tisotumab vedotin in 1L combinations, ahead of the historical 2L+ approval setting.

docs.title: Mechanism / class
docs.text: Tisotumab vedotin (Tivdak) is an antibody-drug conjugate targeting tissue factor (TF, CD142) — a coagulation initiator broadly expressed on solid-tumor epithelium — conjugated to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via a cleavable linker. FDA-approved 2024 (full approval) for recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer post-platinum/IO. InnovaTV 205 Arm H is the 1L move.

docs.title: Trial design deep dive
docs.text:
Study architecture: Phase 2 multi-cohort (InnovaTV 205 / ENGOT-cx8 / GOG-3024), with Arm H specifically evaluating tisotumab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg Q3W + carboplatin AUC5 + pembrolizumab 200 mg Q3W ± bevacizumab 15 mg/kg Q3W in 1L recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer. Single-arm cohort design — no internal randomized comparator. Bevacizumab inclusion was investigator-elected per the ± design, allowing within-cohort exploratory comparison of TV+chemo-IO with and without anti-VEGF backbone.

Endpoint definitions: ORR (confirmed, RECIST 1.1, investigator-assessed) and median DOR as co-primary efficacy endpoints. Secondary endpoints include DCR, PFS, OS, safety per CTCAE v5 (with prospective ocular and peripheral-neuropathy surveillance given TV class profile), and PRO/QoL. The 66% ORR + 13-mo mDOR reported at SGO 2026 is the mature Arm H readout.

Key subgroup analyses: ± bevacizumab subgroup (within-cohort) is the most-watched analysis — informs the Phase 3 design choice of whether to retain anti-VEGF in the cervical 1L combination. Histology (squamous vs adenocarcinoma), PD-L1 CPS, and HPV status subgroups reserved for follow-up. Tissue factor expression-by-response correlation TBD in poster appendix.

Comparator context: KEYNOTE-826 (pembro + chemo ± bev) established 1L SOC with ORR ~65–68%. The 66% Arm H ORR is numerically competitive but cross-trial comparison is unreliable; the 13-mo mDOR is the durability differentiator if it holds. Phase 3 head-to-head is required.

FDA implications: Not registration-enabling on its own — Arm H informs a Phase 3 design moving TV into 1L. Accelerated-approval pathway possible if a single-arm 1L cohort with confirmatory Phase 3 is acceptable; more likely a confirmatory randomized Phase 3 is required.

docs.title: Discussant takeaway
docs.text: Plenary V framing: the 66% ORR + 13-mo DOR in 1L is competitive with chemo + bev + pembro alone (KEYNOTE-826), and supports a Ph3 head-to-head design that includes TV in the 1L cervical combination architecture. Anchors the cervical-cancer ADC class alongside sacituzumab tirumotecan (TroFuse-036) and IBI130 (anti-TROP2).

docs.title: Practice-changing verdict
docs.text: No (Ph2 cohort) — but combination-design-defining. InnovaTV 205 Arm H informs a registration-enabling Ph3 design moving tisotumab vedotin into 1L recurrent/metastatic cervical. NCCN cervical-cancer sequencing implications pending Ph3.

docs.title: KEYNOTE-A18 mature OS — Pembrolizumab + chemoradiation in high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer
docs.text:
Abstract: Plenary V mature OS · Session: Monday April 13, 2026 (cervical Plenary) · Simultaneous publication: TBD (likely JCO mature OS update)

Headline: Long-term OS HR 0.73 with 48-month OS 75.4% vs 70.2% — durable confirmation of pembrolizumab + chemoradiation as 1L SOC for high-risk (stage IB–IVA) locally advanced cervical cancer.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Sponsor / cooperative groups: Merck · ENGOT-cx11 / GOG-3047
  • PI / presenter: Apr 13 Plenary V (presenter TBD)
  • NCT ID: NCT04221945
  • Phase / arms / N: Phase 3 randomized double-blind; 1,060 patients (529 pembro + CCRT vs 531 placebo + CCRT)
  • Primary endpoint(s): PFS and OS (dual primary); mature OS at SGO 2026
  • Indication / line: Locally advanced cervical cancer, high-risk (FIGO 2014 Stage IB2–IIB node+ or III–IVA)
  • Comparator: Placebo + cisplatin-based chemoradiation
  • Session: Plenary V (Day 4, Apr 13)

docs.title: Headline result
docs.text: Mature OS HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.57–0.94). 36-month OS 81.8% vs 74.4%; 48-month OS 75.4% vs 70.2%. Curves continue to separate over time consistent with durable immune memory. No new safety signals over extended follow-up.

docs.title: Mechanism / class
docs.text: Pembrolizumab is a humanized IgG4 anti–PD-1 monoclonal antibody. KEYNOTE-A18 was the registrational trial for the 2024 FDA approval of pembrolizumab + CCRT in high-risk LACC. The 48-mo mature OS update consolidates the new SOC.

docs.title: Trial design deep dive
docs.text:
Study architecture: Phase 3 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled, 1:1 to pembrolizumab 200 mg Q3W + cisplatin-based CCRT for 5 cycles → pembrolizumab 400 mg Q6W maintenance for up to 15 additional cycles, vs placebo + CCRT → placebo maintenance. 1,060 patients (529 vs 531). Stratification by planned external beam RT (IMRT/VMAT vs non-IMRT), stage (IB2–IIB node+ vs III–IVA), and planned total RT dose. Multinational ENGOT-cx11/GOG-3047 cooperative-group footprint.

Endpoint definitions: PFS by investigator assessment per RECIST 1.1 (primary); OS (dual primary, gated per hierarchical testing). The SGO 2026 readout is the mature 48-month OS update following the primary OS readout at ESMO 2024 (HR 0.67 interim). Secondary endpoints include 24/36/48-mo OS landmark rates, PRO/QoL (EORTC QLQ-C30, CX24), and safety.

Key subgroup analyses: PD-L1 CPS subgroups (≥1, ≥10) reserved for ASCO 2026 biomarker follow-up. Stage (IB2–IIB node+ vs III–IVA), histology (squamous vs adenocarcinoma), HPV status, and geographic region pre-specified — all consistently favored pembro per the interim. RT-modality subgroup (IMRT vs non-IMRT) is uniquely important here given the global RT-technology gradient.

Comparator context: Cisplatin-based CCRT alone is the long-standing SOC; the 48-mo placebo-arm OS of 70.2% is consistent with historical high-risk LACC benchmarks (~65–72% at 4-5 yr). The 5.2-percentage-point absolute gain at 48 mo translates to a clinically meaningful durable cure-fraction enrichment.

FDA implications: Confirmatory — full approval in place since 2024; mature OS update locks in NCCN preferred status and supports global label expansion in remaining ex-US markets.

docs.title: Discussant takeaway
docs.text: Plenary V framing: the 48-mo OS curves at 75.4% vs 70.2% represent durable cure-fraction enrichment with an immune-modulated approach in a setting historically defined by chemoradiation alone. Reinforces molecular biomarker (PD-L1) investigation in follow-up analyses.

docs.title: Practice-changing verdict
docs.text: Yes (confirmatory). Pembro + CCRT is already 1L SOC for high-risk LACC; mature 48-mo OS data confirm the magnitude and durability of benefit. NCCN cervical guidelines reinforced.

docs.title: IMGN853-0420 — Mirvetuximab + carboplatin → MIRV maintenance in PSOC (FRα+)
docs.text:
Abstract: LBA, Phase 2 · Session: Saturday April 11 / Sunday April 12, 2026 · Simultaneous publication: TBD (Gynecologic Oncology)

Headline: ELAHERE moves earlier — mirvetuximab + carboplatin induction followed by MIRV monotherapy maintenance achieves 68% ORR in the maintenance phase and 63.9% in the PARPi-pretreated subgroup, justifying repositioning of mirvetuximab into platinum-sensitive ovarian (PSOC) including post-PARPi.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Sponsor: AbbVie (IMGN853-0420; ELAHERE life-cycle program)
  • PI / presenter: Apr 11–12 presentation (presenter TBD)
  • NCT ID: NCT05445778 (IMGN853-0420)
  • Phase / arms / N: Phase 2 single-arm; FRα-high platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian (PSOC) patients receive MIRV + carboplatin induction → MIRV monotherapy maintenance
  • Primary endpoint(s): ORR in maintenance phase
  • Indication / line: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, FRα-high (≥75% PS2+ IHC)
  • Comparator: None (single-arm)
  • Session: LBA, Day 2/3

docs.title: Headline result
docs.text: 81% of patients continued from induction to MIRV monotherapy maintenance. ORR 68% in maintenance phase overall, and 63.9% in the PARPi-pretreated subgroup — the practice-relevant number, because it demonstrates ELAHERE retains activity after PARPi failure. Safety: grade ≥3 neutropenia 15%, blurred vision 10%, thrombocytopenia 10%; pneumonitis 15% over prolonged therapy (monitoring required).

docs.title: Mechanism / class
docs.text: Mirvetuximab soravtansine (ELAHERE) is an FRα-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a maytansinoid (DM4) payload, FDA-approved 2022 for platinum-resistant FRα-high recurrent ovarian and full approval 2024. IMGN853-0420 is the AbbVie life-cycle pivot from platinum-resistant into platinum-sensitive.

docs.title: Trial design deep dive
docs.text:
Study architecture: Phase 2 single-arm, two-stage design — induction phase of MIRV 6 mg/kg (adjusted ideal body weight) + carboplatin AUC5 Q3W for 6 cycles, followed by MIRV monotherapy maintenance Q3W until progression or toxicity. Enrollment restricted to FRα-high (≥75% of viable tumor cells with PS2+ IHC staining intensity) platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer. No comparator. 81% rollover from induction to maintenance is a key feasibility metric demonstrating the regimen is deliverable.

Endpoint definitions: ORR in the maintenance phase by investigator assessment per RECIST 1.1 (primary, calculated from maintenance-phase start). Secondary endpoints include induction-phase ORR, DOR, PFS, OS, safety per CTCAE v5, and PRO/QoL. The maintenance-phase ORR primary endpoint is unusual — it isolates the monotherapy contribution after carboplatin clearance.

Key subgroup analyses: PARPi-pretreated subgroup (63.9% ORR) is the practice-relevant cohort — establishes ELAHERE retains activity after PARPi failure, the highest-need PSOC niche. FRα IHC intensity (PS2+ ≥75% vs higher cut-offs) reserved for ASCO follow-up. Prior-line and platinum-free-interval subgroups TBD in poster appendix.

Comparator context: No randomized comparator in this Phase 2, but the 68% maintenance ORR substantially exceeds historical PSOC maintenance benchmarks (~30–40% for chemo, niraparib/olaparib in unselected post-platinum). Pneumonitis 15% over prolonged maintenance is the key tolerability concern relative to PARPi maintenance.

FDA implications: Not registration-enabling on its own — supports a Phase 3 PSOC design (likely vs investigator-choice chemo or vs PARPi maintenance in PARPi-naive). The PARPi-pretreated PSOC niche may admit accelerated-approval pathway if Phase 3 is concurrent.

docs.title: Discussant takeaway
docs.text: Per AbbVie press and SGO Meeting News coverage: the 63.9% PARPi-pretreated ORR supports moving ELAHERE earlier into PSOC, including in the post-PARPi setting where therapeutic options narrow rapidly. Pneumonitis signal over prolonged maintenance therapy is a key monitoring item.

docs.title: Practice-changing verdict
docs.text: Pending — supports Phase 3 design but not yet practice-changing on its own. Likely to anchor a Ph3 maintenance design (similar to GLORIOSA framework) and inform NCCN PSOC sequencing. AbbVie life-cycle for ELAHERE depends on the PSOC move.

docs.title: NRG-GY019 — Letrozole monotherapy vs paclitaxel/carboplatin + letrozole in low-grade serous ovarian (frontline)
docs.text:
Abstract: Plenary I · Session: Friday April 10, 2026 · Simultaneous publication: TBD (Gynecologic Oncology / JCO)

Headline: The "negative" Plenary trial that nonetheless settles a long-running debate — letrozole monotherapy failed non-inferiority vs paclitaxel/carboplatin + letrozole as frontline therapy in low-grade serous ovarian cancer (LGSOC), preserving chemotherapy as the SOC backbone.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Sponsor / cooperative groups: NRG Oncology (NRG-GY019)
  • PI / presenter: Amanda Fader, MD (Johns Hopkins)
  • NCT ID: NCT04095364
  • Phase / arms / N: Phase 3 randomized open-label non-inferiority; ~450 patients (letrozole alone vs paclitaxel/carboplatin + letrozole)
  • Primary endpoint(s): PFS (non-inferiority margin pre-specified)
  • Indication / line: Frontline newly diagnosed Stage II–IV low-grade serous ovarian cancer (HR+ biology)
  • Comparator: Paclitaxel + carboplatin + letrozole (chemo + endocrine SOC)
  • Session: Plenary I (Day 1, Apr 10)

docs.title: Headline result
docs.text: Letrozole monotherapy did not meet the pre-specified non-inferiority margin vs paclitaxel/carboplatin + letrozole. PFS favored the chemo-containing arm; the non-inferiority bound was crossed. This is a "practice-preserving" negative — the design tested whether chemotherapy could be eliminated from frontline LGSOC in favor of endocrine monotherapy, and the answer is no.

docs.title: Mechanism / class
docs.text: Letrozole is a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor. LGSOC is hormone-receptor-positive (ER/PR+) in the majority of cases, motivating the endocrine-monotherapy hypothesis tested in NRG-GY019. The mechanism question — whether HR+ biology in LGSOC behaves like HR+ breast (where endocrine monotherapy can suffice in some settings) — was answered negatively.

docs.title: Trial design deep dive
docs.text:
Study architecture: Phase 3 randomized open-label non-inferiority, 1:1 to letrozole 2.5 mg PO daily monotherapy vs paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC6 Q3W for 6 cycles followed by letrozole 2.5 mg PO daily maintenance. ~450 patients, frontline newly diagnosed Stage II–IV low-grade serous ovarian cancer post-cytoreductive surgery (R0/R1/R2 strata TBD). NRG Oncology cooperative-group execution. Stratification by stage and residual disease per protocol.

Endpoint definitions: PFS (primary) with pre-specified non-inferiority margin (specific HR boundary TBD per protocol — typically 1.3–1.4 in oncology NI designs). Failure to meet the upper-bound NI margin is what defines this as a "negative" non-inferiority trial — letrozole alone could not be declared non-inferior. Secondary endpoints include OS, ORR (in measurable disease), PRO/QoL, and tolerability — important given chemo's toxicity penalty in a chronic-biology disease.

Key subgroup analyses: KRAS-mutated subgroup (critical given RAMP-201 avutometinib + defactinib data showing PFS 19.6 mo, DOR 31 mo in KRAS-mut LGSOC) reserved for follow-up. ER/PR expression-quantitative subgroups, stage, age, and residual-disease strata pre-specified. The negative top-line does not preclude a positive endocrine-only signal in a molecularly defined subset, but no such subset was rescue-defined.

Comparator context: Paclitaxel/carboplatin + letrozole maintenance reflects pragmatic LGSOC SOC. The trial was designed to deescalate by removing chemo — the negative result preserves the chemo backbone.

FDA implications: No new approval — practice-preserving negative. Reaffirms NCCN guideline language that chemo + endocrine maintenance remains frontline SOC; future deescalation attempts will need molecular enrichment (KRAS-mut, MEK-inhibitor combination paradigm).

docs.title: Discussant takeaway
docs.text: Plenary I framing: NRG-GY019 closes a decade-long debate about chemo elimination in LGSOC. Combined with RAMP-201's KRAS-mut LGSOC durability (DOR 31 mo, PFS 19.6 mo in KRAS-mut), the field now has clear sequencing — chemo + letrozole remains frontline SOC; avutometinib + defactinib emerges in KRAS-mut recurrent disease.

docs.title: Practice-changing verdict
docs.text: Yes (negative-confirmatory). Preserves the chemo + endocrine backbone in frontline LGSOC; rules out the "letrozole alone" simplification. Important for NCCN-guideline reaffirmation of the chemo backbone in this HR+ subset.

docs.title: REJOICE-Ovarian01 — Raludotatug deruxtecan (R-DXd, CDH6 ADC) in platinum-resistant ovarian
docs.text:
Abstract: Phase 2/3 efficacy readout · Session: Saturday April 11, 2026 · Simultaneous publication: TBD (Gynecologic Oncology abstract + Daiichi data package)

Headline: First CDH6-targeted ADC clinical efficacy at scale — ORR 50.5% in platinum-resistant high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer, establishing CDH6 as a tractable ovarian ADC target beyond FRα.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Sponsor: Daiichi Sankyo (R-DXd / DS-6000)
  • PI / presenter: Apr 11 presentation (presenter TBD)
  • NCT ID: NCT05489211 (REJOICE-Ovarian01)
  • Phase / arms / N: Phase 2/3, multi-dose-cohort expansion in platinum-resistant ovarian
  • Primary endpoint(s): ORR (RECIST 1.1)
  • Indication / line: Platinum-resistant high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian cancer
  • Comparator: None at Ph2 (Ph3 expansion vs investigator-choice chemo planned)
  • Session: Day 2 (Apr 11)

docs.title: Headline result
docs.text: Confirmed ORR 50.5% overall in platinum-resistant HGSOC/endometrioid — a roughly 5x lift over the ~10% ORR historical benchmark of single-agent chemo in this setting. CDH6 expression by IHC was correlated with response. Safety profile consistent with the deruxtecan (DXd) topo-1 ADC class — ILD/pneumonitis remains the watched AE.

docs.title: Mechanism / class
docs.text: Raludotatug deruxtecan (R-DXd, DS-6000) is an antibody-drug conjugate targeting CDH6 (cadherin-6) — a kidney- and ovarian-restricted target — with the Daiichi DXd exatecan-derivative topoisomerase-1 payload (same payload class as trastuzumab deruxtecan / datopotamab deruxtecan / patritumab deruxtecan). First CDH6 ADC to deliver clinical efficacy at scale.

docs.title: Trial design deep dive
docs.text:
Study architecture: Phase 2/3 seamless design — Phase 2 portion is multi-dose-cohort expansion (specific doses TBD per Daiichi protocol, typically 4.8 mg/kg, 5.6 mg/kg, and 6.4 mg/kg Q3W for the DXd class) in platinum-resistant HGSOC/endometrioid ovarian cancer; Phase 3 portion will randomize R-DXd vs investigator-choice chemo (paclitaxel, PLD, or topotecan). Enrollment open to platinum-resistant high-grade serous or endometrioid histology; CDH6 IHC selection strategy TBD (prospective vs retrospective stratification).

Endpoint definitions: Phase 2 primary endpoint ORR by blinded independent central review per RECIST 1.1. Secondary endpoints include DOR, PFS, OS, safety, and PK. Phase 3 primary endpoint expected to be PFS with OS as key secondary (gated). The 50.5% confirmed ORR reported at SGO 2026 is the Phase 2 efficacy readout.

Key subgroup analyses: CDH6 IHC expression-by-response correlation — the most-watched analysis, with response correlated to expression per the OncLive coverage. Histology (HGSOC vs endometrioid), prior bevacizumab exposure, prior PARPi, and dose-cohort subgroups TBD in full presentation. ILD/pneumonitis rates by dose cohort are the safety-side counterpart.

Comparator context: No randomized control in Phase 2, but the 50.5% ORR represents a ~5x lift over the ~10% historical chemo benchmark in platinum-resistant HGSOC. Phase 3 investigator-choice chemo arm will provide the formal comparison.

FDA implications: Pre-pivotal — Phase 2 establishes CDH6 ADC efficacy clinically; Phase 3 expansion (already enrolling per the seamless design) is the registration vehicle. Project Optimus dose-optimization will apply across the DXd-platform comparison.

docs.title: Discussant takeaway
docs.text: Per OncLive coverage: the 50.5% ORR is the first robust signal that the deruxtecan platform extends beyond HER2 and TROP2 into a kidney/ovarian-restricted target — and that platinum-resistant ovarian, long stuck near 10% ORR with chemo, can be reshaped by ADCs alongside the FRα franchise.

docs.title: Practice-changing verdict
docs.text: No (Ph2/3 readout) — but pivotal-design-defining. REJOICE-Ovarian01 anchors a registration-enabling Phase 3 expansion. Class-level read-through across the DXd ovarian platform (datopotamab, patritumab) and across CDH6 in renal.

docs.title: ROSELLA — Relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (post-bevacizumab)
docs.text:
Abstract: LBA, Plenary I · Session: Plenary I, Friday April 10, 2026 (opening session, San Juan Convention Center) · Simultaneous publication: The Lancet 2026 Apr 10 — DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00462-9

Headline: Phase 3 OS win with mOS 16.0 vs 11.9 mo (HR 0.65, p=0.0004) — the first GR-antagonist Phase 3 victory in solid tumor and the cycle-defining readout of SGO 2026; Corcept's Lifyorli (relacorilant) was already FDA-approved March 2026, making this the simultaneous Lancet victory-lap.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Sponsor / cooperative groups: Corcept Therapeutics · GOG-3073 / ENGOT-ov72 / APGOT-Ov10 / LACOG-0223 / ANZGOG-2221 (five-group multi-region design)
  • PI / presenter: Plenary I LBA, Apr 10 (presenter TBD per SGO program)
  • NCT ID: NCT05257408
  • Phase / arms / N: Phase 3, 2-arm randomized open-label; ~381 enrolled (intermittent relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel vs nab-paclitaxel monotherapy)
  • Primary endpoint(s): OS and PFS (dual primary)
  • Indication / line: Platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, primary peritoneal cancer, post-bevacizumab
  • Comparator: Nab-paclitaxel monotherapy
  • Session: Plenary I (Day 1, Apr 10)

docs.title: Headline result
docs.text: mOS 16.0 vs 11.9 mo (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.51–0.83, p=0.0004) — a 4.1-mo absolute survival gain in a setting where mOS has stagnated at ~12 mo for a decade. mPFS HR 0.70 (p=0.0076). Benefit was consistent across pre-specified subgroups including prior bevacizumab exposure and number of prior lines. Simultaneous Lancet publication day-of-presentation.

docs.title: Mechanism / class
docs.text: Relacorilant is a selective glucocorticoid receptor (GR) antagonist — first-in-class oral non-steroidal modulator that blocks cortisol-mediated chemotherapy resistance without affecting the progesterone receptor. ROSELLA is the first Phase 3 win for the GR-antagonist class in any solid tumor.

docs.title: Trial design deep dive
docs.text:
Study architecture: Phase 3 randomized open-label, 1:1 to intermittent relacorilant (150 mg PO day prior, day of, day after nab-paclitaxel) + nab-paclitaxel vs nab-paclitaxel monotherapy. ~381 patients across GOG-3073 / ENGOT-ov72 / APGOT-Ov10 / LACOG-0223 / ANZGOG-2221 — a five-cooperative-group, multi-region footprint spanning North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. Stratification factors TBD per protocol; prior bevacizumab exposure was an enrollment requirement, narrowing the population to the post-bev PROC setting where therapeutic options collapse fastest.

Endpoint definitions: Dual primary OS and PFS — an aggressive design choice that requires both endpoints to win or fall under a pre-specified alpha-spending plan (specifics TBD). PFS by investigator assessment per RECIST 1.1; OS by event-driven analysis. Key secondary endpoints include ORR, DOR, PRO/QoL (FACT-O), and safety.

Key subgroup analyses: Headline benefit consistent across prior bevacizumab exposure (a mandated enrollment criterion, so the subgroup is largely homogeneous) and number of prior lines of therapy. HRD/BRCA, age, ECOG, and geographic-region subgroup forest plots reserved for ASCO 2026 follow-up per the cross-link plan. Intermittent vs continuous GR-antagonist dosing schedule was an important Phase 2 design question that this Phase 3 inherited.

Comparator context: Nab-paclitaxel monotherapy is an accepted PROC reference (mOS ~11–12 mo historically), but the field has drifted toward MIRV (FRα+) and mirvetuximab combinations. The 11.9-mo control arm here is consistent with that benchmark, validating the comparator choice.

FDA implications: Approval pre-dated the readout (Lifyorli March 2026) on PFS interim plus OS trend; the Plenary I full OS readout locks in the label and underwrites EMA H2 2026 submission. NCCN incorporation already in motion.

docs.title: Discussant takeaway
docs.text: Plenary I framing reframed platinum-resistant ovarian as a setting where mechanism diversity (GR antagonism alongside ADCs and pembro combinations) is now generating real OS gains — the decade-long stagnation broke in early 2026.

docs.title: Practice-changing verdict
docs.text: Yes — already practice-changing pre-presentation. Lifyorli (relacorilant) FDA approval came March 2026, one month ahead of SGO. The Lancet publication and Plenary I slot anchored rapid NCCN-guideline incorporation. Cross-tumor GR-antagonist read-through expected in breast and prostate.

  • JPM 2026: Corcept ($CORT) framed Lifyorli FDA submission at JPM Jan 12–15
  • ESMO 2026: EMA decision likely H2 2026

docs.title: RUBY 4-year OS — Dostarlimab + chemo in 1L advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer
docs.text:
Abstract: Plenary III · Session: Plenary III, Sunday April 12, 2026 · Simultaneous publication: TBD (likely NEJM or JCO mature OS update)

Headline: Mature 4-year OS in the dMMR/MSI-H subgroup shows HR 0.32 — a 68% mortality reduction, with ~73% of patients alive at 4 years; MMRp subgroup HR 0.79 with 7-mo median OS gain. Confirms dostarlimab + carboplatin/paclitaxel as 1L SOC for dMMR endometrial cancer.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Sponsor / cooperative groups: GSK · ENGOT-EN6-NSGO / GOG-3031
  • PI / presenter: Plenary III, Apr 12 (presenter TBD)
  • NCT ID: NCT03981796
  • Phase / arms / N: Phase 3 randomized double-blind; 494 patients (245 dostarlimab + chemo vs 249 placebo + chemo)
  • Primary endpoint(s): PFS (primary); OS (key secondary, mature 4-yr update at SGO 2026)
  • Indication / line: 1L advanced (Stage III/IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer, all-comer with dMMR primary analysis subgroup
  • Comparator: Placebo + carboplatin/paclitaxel followed by placebo maintenance
  • Session: Plenary III (Day 3, Apr 12)

docs.title: Headline result
docs.text: In the dMMR/MSI-H subgroup, 4-year OS HR 0.32 (95% CI 0.17–0.63) — 68% mortality reduction with ~73% 4-year OS in the dostarlimab arm. In the MMRp subgroup, HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.60–1.04) with 7-mo median OS gain — trend toward benefit. The dMMR survival curve is among the steepest in any solid-tumor Phase 3 mature OS readout. No new safety signals.

docs.title: Mechanism / class
docs.text: Dostarlimab is a humanized IgG4 anti–PD-1 monoclonal antibody. RUBY is the cycle-defining mature OS confirmation of the chemo-immunotherapy 1L paradigm in endometrial cancer (alongside NRG-GY018 with pembrolizumab).

docs.title: Trial design deep dive
docs.text:
Study architecture: Phase 3 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled, 1:1 to dostarlimab 500 mg IV Q3W + carboplatin AUC5 / paclitaxel 175 mg/m² for 6 cycles → dostarlimab 1,000 mg Q6W maintenance up to 3 years, vs placebo + chemo → placebo maintenance. 494 patients total (245 vs 249). Stratification by MMR/MSI status, prior anti-cancer therapy, and disease status (recurrent vs primary advanced) — the MMR stratification is the design feature that enabled the dMMR primary analysis subgroup to be powered separately.

Endpoint definitions: PFS by investigator assessment per RECIST 1.1 (primary, with dMMR subgroup as primary analysis population); OS (key secondary, gated on PFS positivity per hierarchical testing). The 4-year mature OS update reported at SGO 2026 follows the original PFS readout (SGO/NEJM 2023) and the interim OS update (ESMO 2024).

Key subgroup analyses: dMMR/MSI-H subgroup HR 0.32 (the headline plateau) vs MMRp HR 0.79. POLE-mutated and p53-abnormal molecular subgroups (per ProMisE/TCGA endometrial classifier) reserved for ASCO 2026 follow-up. Geographic, age, BMI, and prior-therapy subgroups TBD in plenary deck.

Comparator context: Carboplatin/paclitaxel + placebo with placebo maintenance reflects pre-2023 SOC. The 4-year placebo-arm OS in dMMR (TBD per slide) provides the historical floor against which the 73% dostarlimab plateau is judged.

FDA implications: Confirmatory — accelerated approval (dMMR) and full approval (all-comer) already in place; the 4-yr OS locks in the magnitude of benefit and rules out late curve crossing, supporting durable NCCN preferred status.

docs.title: Discussant takeaway
docs.text: Plenary III framing: the dMMR OS curve flattens to ~73% at 4 years — exceptional plateau-like behavior consistent with durable immune control. Reinforces molecular triage (dMMR/MMRp split) as the cornerstone of endometrial therapy selection.

docs.title: Practice-changing verdict
docs.text: Yes (confirmatory). Dostarlimab + chemo was already 1L SOC for dMMR endometrial post-RUBY interim; the 4-yr mature OS locks in the magnitude of benefit and rules out late curve crossing. NCCN endometrial guidelines reinforced.

docs.title: Single-Cell Genomics 2026
docs.text:
The two flagship single-cell community meetings of 2026, captured under one vault. The brand "Single Cell Genomics" splits across two events this year and both are in-scope for the AACR cross-link:

  1. Gordon Research Conference on Single-Cell Genomics 2026 — Les Diablerets, Switzerland, May 10–15, 2026. Chair: Angela Oliveira Pisco. Subtitled "Accelerating Medical Discovery With Single Cell Omics and Machine Learning." This is the de-facto annual Single-Cell Genomics anchor for the field (alternates years with the Single-Cell Cancer Biology GRC, also at Les Diablerets). The associated GRS (graduate-student/postdoc seminar) runs May 9–10 on "Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Single-Cell and Spatial Omics." Oversubscribed as of May 2026.
  2. Wellcome Connecting Science — Single Cell Biology 2026 — Wellcome Genome Campus, Hinxton, UK, June 10–12, 2026. Committee: Leeat Keren (Weizmann), Cole Trapnell (UW), Roser Vento-Tormo (Sanger). Keynote: Ido Amit (Weizmann). Hashtag #SingleCell26. In-person + virtual hybrid; abstract deadline was Mar 30, in-person registration closes May 11.

Status: Scaffold — both meetings upcoming or active. GRC 2026 is happening this week (the vault is being built mid-meeting, May 11, 2026). Wellcome Single Cell Biology drops a month later. Full program for the Wellcome meeting was released April 22, 2026; the GRC program is closed-door per Gordon Conference policy (no recording, no public talk titles, attendees-only).

Brand-disambiguation up front: there is no single meeting in 2026 literally titled "Single Cell Genomics" hosted by EMBL or the Sanger Institute. EMBL Heidelberg's last "Single-Cell Omics" conference ran in 2022 (sic22-01) and is not on the 2026 calendar — EMBL's 2026 single-cell-adjacent slot is the Brain (epi)genome symposium (Apr 21–24, in-house single-cell + 3D-genomics axis). The two events above are the two real 2026 flagships for the single-cell community. The CSHL "Single Cell Analyses" meeting alternates years and is not running in 2026 either; its sibling slot at CSHL is the Biological Data Science meeting (see cshl-bds-2026/), which has spatial/single-cell as one of six sessions but is not a single-cell-focused meeting per se.

docs.title: Why this is in the vault
docs.text:
• Highest single-cell methods density of any meeting in the corpus. GRC + Wellcome Single Cell Biology together are where the next generation of scRNA / scATAC / spatial / multimodal tools are first presented, in front of an audience of ~200 (GRC) + ~250 (Wellcome) of the field's tightest-knit community. Tool density per attendee is higher than RECOMB, ISMB, or EuroBioC — every oral talk is a single-cell method, dataset, or atlas.
  • Direct AACR-axis fit on the single-cell + spatial bin. The AACR 2026 single-cell + spatial topic (aacr-2026/topics/single-cell-spatial-omics/) is the largest topic folder in the AACR vault — 20 session transcripts, ~273k words, 1,015 poster abstracts. Almost every analytical method cited in those AACR talks was originally presented at a Single-Cell Genomics GRC, the Wellcome meeting, or the older EMBL Single-Cell Omics line. Tracking these two 2026 meetings catches the upstream-tool previews of what will surface at AACR 2027.
  • Foundation-model-era axis. The GRC 2026 subtitle ("Single Cell Omics and Machine Learning") and the GRS topic ("AI and ML for Single-Cell and Spatial Omics") explicitly center the scGPT / Geneformer / scFoundation wave that AACR 2026 only touched in passing. Charlotte Bunne (EPFL, Wellcome speaker) is a key foundation-models-for-perturbations voice — direct overlap with the AACR agentic-AI dossier and the RECOMB 2026 / ISMB 2026 MLCSB tracks.
  • Lineage tracing + perturbation atlases. Wellcome speakers James Gagnon (Utah) and Theresa Loveless (Rice) are at the front of recording-based lineage tracing; this is where the EMBO Lineage Tracing 2026 meeting (Mar 2026) handed off its momentum. GRC will likely cover Perturb-seq successors, CRISPR screen single-cell readouts.
  • Spatial-transcriptomics anchor. Mats Nilsson (Stockholm; ISS / in-situ-sequencing), Sizun Jiang (Harvard; CODEX/Akoya), and Roser Vento-Tormo (Sanger; tissue atlases) at Wellcome plus the GRC "Spatial and Proteomics Analysis" session cover the same Visium-HD / Xenium / CosMx / MERFISH substrate that drives the AACR spatial-biomarkers sessions.

docs.title: GRC SCG 2026 (May 10–15, Les Diablerets)
docs.text:
The GRC's published session structure (7 themed sessions across 5 days):

  • AI for Genomics — foundation models, deep-learning embeddings, transfer learning across atlases
  • Transcription Factor Regulation — TF-binding inference from scATAC, GRN reconstruction
  • Single-Cell Modeling — perturbation-response models, optimal transport, lineage dynamics
  • Applications in Medicine — disease atlases, clinical biomarkers, drug response
  • Spatial and Proteomics Analysis — Visium HD / Xenium / CODEX / CITE-seq, spatial-graph methods
  • 3D Genomics — Hi-C, scHi-C, single-cell 3D chromatin
  • Epigenomics — scATAC, single-cell methylation, multimodal chromatin

GRC pattern is single-track, ~5 talks/session, late-afternoon discussion + poster sessions, conferee count capped at ~200. Expected: 30–40 oral talks + 2 keynote slots + ~120 posters.

docs.title: Wellcome Single Cell Biology 2026 (Jun 10–12, Hinxton)
docs.text:
Six published session topics over 2.5 days:

  • Single-cell going large scale — atlas-scale datasets, sample multiplexing, cost-down workflows
  • Beyond transcriptomics — proteomics (CITE-seq successors), single-cell metabolomics, multi-omics
  • Non-model organisms — single-cell in non-mouse/human (Mara Lawniczak — malaria parasite, mosquito atlases)
  • Technology development — new chemistry, new hardware, miniaturization (BD Rhapsody / 10x next-gen / Parse Bio / Singleron / Honeycomb)
  • Computational approaches — foundation models, integration, perturbation modeling, lineage inference
  • Spatial technologies — Mats Nilsson (ISS), Sizun Jiang (CODEX), Vento-Tormo (tissue atlases)

Hybrid format. Bursaries available for trainees + LMIC delegates. Posters can be virtual.

Confirmed speakers (Wellcome) as of Apr 22, 2026: Ido Amit (keynote, Weizmann), Charlotte Bunne (EPFL), Gonçalo Castelo-Branco (Karolinska), Giovanni D'Angelo (EPFL), James Gagnon (Utah — lineage tracing), Sizun Jiang (Harvard — spatial proteomics), Leeat Keren (Weizmann, organizer), Mara Lawniczak (Sanger — non-model), Theresa Loveless (Rice — recording lineage), Heather Marlow (Chicago), Mats Nilsson (Stockholm — ISS), Mor Nitzan (Hebrew U — theory), Cole Trapnell (UW, organizer — Monocle / sci-RNA-seq lineage), Céline Vallot (Curie — single-cell epigenomics in cancer), Roser Vento-Tormo (Sanger, organizer — tissue atlases / cell-cell communication).

│   ├── lineage-tracing/          # recording lineage, CellTag, perturb-tracking
│   ├── perturbation-atlases/     # Perturb-seq successors, drug-response atlases
│   └── cancer-single-cell/       # AACR overlap surface
├── tools/               # PRIMARY artifact — one entry per method / package / atlas
│   └── index.md
└── sessions/            # per-session abstract index (post-meeting; Wellcome only — GRC is off-the-record)
    └── index.md

The tools/ directory is the load-bearing artifact, same shape as EuroBioC 2025 / GBCC 2025 / RECOMB 2026 / CSHL BDS 2026. Single-cell-specific additions to the per-tool template (see tools/index.md): a Modality field (scRNA / scATAC / spatial / multimodal / proteomics / methylation), an Atlas footprint row (which large datasets it's been benchmarked on — HCA, Tabula Sapiens, CELLxGENE, HuBMAP, HTAN), and a Foundation-model lineage field (scGPT / Geneformer / scFoundation / scBERT / Universal Cell Embeddings descendants).

docs.title: What's different from EuroBioC / CSHL BDS / RECOMB / ISMB
docs.text:
• GRC is closed-door. Gordon Conference rules: no recording, no live-tweeting, no public talk titles, attendees-only press. Even the speaker list isn't published in advance. The vault for the GRC half of this meeting builds entirely post-hoc from (a) preprints that drop in the weeks after the meeting and reference "presented at GRC SCG 2026," (b) Bluesky/X posts from attendees with the chair's blessing, (c) the Pisco lab's eventual recap if she writes one. This is the opposite of the EuroBioC / GBCC / Nextflow Summit pattern (full recordings, slides on Zenodo).
  • Wellcome is hybrid, partially recorded. Keynotes usually go to YouTube. Speaker bios + titles are public. Closer to the EuroBioC / GBCC information model.
  • Two-meeting compound vault. Unlike other conference vaults (one meeting per vault), this one bridges two events that share a community and a sub-discipline. The digest/ folder is split with grc-* and wellcome-* prefixes. The tools/ index treats them as a single 2026 single-cell-methods cohort — many tools will be presented at both, and the tool-page Talk field becomes Talk at GRC + Talk at Wellcome as separate rows.
  • No industry track. Unlike AGBT or JPM, neither meeting has a paid sponsor track. 10x / Parse / Singleron / Element / Curio Bio / Vizgen / NanoString reps are in the audience and at the bar but don't get slots. Platform-launch news happens in side-conversations and shows up in trade-press writeups later.
  • The "AI/ML" turn is explicit. GRC 2026 is the first Single-Cell Genomics GRC to put AI/ML in the conference subtitle. This formalizes a shift that started at GRC 2024 (Zhuang/Fan/Xie/Pisco co-organized) and is now centerpiece. Foundation-model talks expected in 3 of 7 GRC sessions (AI for Genomics, Single-Cell Modeling, parts of Applications in Medicine).
  • High preprint ratio post-meeting. Empirically ~75–85% of GRC SCG talks have a bioRxiv preprint within 6 months of the meeting (compare ~85–90% at CSHL methods meetings, ~60% at AACR). Wellcome's ratio is similar.

docs.title: Anticipated top-5 themes for the 2026 SCG cohort
docs.text:
Cross-cutting between the two meetings, ranked by expected oral-talk count + AACR overlap:

  1. Foundation models for single-cell omics. scGPT-v2 and Geneformer-v2 successor work, perturbation-prediction foundation models (Bunne's CellFlow lineage at EPFL), Universal Cell Embeddings + scPRINT updates. The GRC subtitle ("Accelerating Medical Discovery With Single Cell Omics and Machine Learning") and the GRS topic ("AI and ML for Single-Cell and Spatial Omics") both center this. AACR overlap: AACR 2026 agentic-AI dossier + foundation-model sessions.
  2. Spatial transcriptomics at scale. Visium HD analysis tooling, Xenium-native pipelines, CosMx integration, MERSCOPE/MERFISH analysis, ISS (Nilsson). The Wellcome "spatial technologies" session and the GRC "Spatial and Proteomics Analysis" session both anchor this. AACR overlap: the AACR single-cell-spatial topic has 8 strong-fit sessions cross-listed.
  3. Multimodal single-cell + integration. CITE-seq successors, Multiome + methylation + RNA, ATAC+RNA at scale, proteo-genomics. The Wellcome "beyond transcriptomics" session and the GRC "Epigenomics" + "3D Genomics" sessions. AACR overlap: AACR 2026 hematology + multimodal sessions.
  4. Lineage tracing and perturbation atlases. Recording-based lineage (Loveless at Rice, Gagnon at Utah), Perturb-seq successors, drug-response atlases. Wellcome speakers center this; the GRC "Single-Cell Modeling" session will cover the analytical side. Crosses with the EMBO Lineage Tracing 2026 meeting (Mar 2026, separate).
  5. Cancer single-cell with clinical translation. Single-cell atlases of disease states, biomarker discovery from scRNA / spatial, clinical-trial-adjacent applications. The GRC "Applications in Medicine" session is explicitly this. Direct AACR overlap: AACR 2026 has 8 single-cell + spatial sessions and 1,015 poster abstracts in this topic.

docs.title: Calibration: what could go wrong
docs.text:
• Pisco / GRC discretion is tighter than expected. If no preprints surface with "GRC SCG 2026" acknowledgement and Bluesky stays quiet, the GRC half of this vault stays sparse. Fallback: build the Wellcome half thoroughly and treat the GRC half as a watch-list rather than a tool index.
  • Wellcome program changes between Apr 22 and Jun 10. Some speaker drops always happen; final session-to-day mapping isn't finalized until ~1 week pre-meeting. Pre-scaffolded tool pages should reference "Day TBD" until Jun 5 schedule scrape.
  • Foundation-model hype peaking. If GRC and Wellcome both end up being 50%+ foundation-model talks, the tool index becomes lopsided. Counter-axis: make sure spatial / multimodal / lineage / non-model entries get equal extraction effort.
  • Industry talks invisible. Neither meeting has a paid sponsor track, so 10x / Vizgen / Curio / Singleron / Element / Parse Biosciences platform updates won't appear in talks. Those are captured in agbt-2026/ and trade-press writeups; cross-link from SCG tool pages where relevant rather than re-extracting.

docs.title: Per-tool entry template
docs.text:
Each tool gets its own page (tools/<package-slug>.md) following this structure. The single-cell-flavored extension of the standard EuroBioC / CSHL BDS template:

# <PackageName>

**One-line description** — what the package does in plain language.

- **Maintainer:** <name> (<institution>)
- **Modality:** scRNA / scATAC / spatial-transcriptomics / spatial-proteomics / CITE-seq / methylation / multimodal / lineage / atlas-platform
- **Language:** Python / R / both / standalone binary
- **Package:** [PyPI / Bioconductor / CRAN / GitHub-only]
- **Source:** [GitHub link]
- **Docs / vignette:** [link]
- **Preprint:** [bioRxiv DOI]
- **Publication:** [journal link, if any]
- **Status at SCG-2026:** new release / major update / methods talk / case study / atlas drop / preprint pre-announcement
- **Atlas footprint:** which large datasets it's been benchmarked on (HCA, Tabula Sapiens, CELLxGENE corpus, HuBMAP, HTAN, ENCODE-singlecell, MS-style atlases)
- **Foundation-model lineage:** if applicable — scGPT-line / Geneformer-line / scFoundation-line / scBERT-line / Universal Cell Embeddings / scPRINT / independent

## Talk at GRC Single-Cell Genomics 2026 (Les Diablerets, May 10–15)

- **Speaker:** ...
- **Session:** AI for Genomics / TF Regulation / Single-Cell Modeling / Applications in Medicine / Spatial & Proteomics / 3D Genomics / Epigenomics
- **Day:** ...
- **Slides / abstract:** Gordon Conferences are closed-door — no public record (extract from post-meeting preprints + attendee Bluesky/X with chair blessing)
- **Recording:** none (GRC policy)

## Talk at Wellcome Single Cell Biology 2026 (Hinxton, Jun 10–12)

- **Session:** large scale / beyond transcriptomics / non-model / tech dev / computational / spatial
- **Day:** Wed 10 / Thu 11 / Fri 12

- **Video:** [YouTube — Wellcome posts keynotes; selective for short talks]
- **Abstract page:** [Wellcome event page link]

## What it does

2–3 sentences: the problem it solves, key methodological idea, what it consumes/produces.

## Where it fits in the corpus

- AACR 2026 (single-cell + spatial topic): [link if mentioned]
- EuroBioC 2025: [link to SpatialData / DESpace / OSTA / spatialFDA / iSEE if related]
- CSHL BDS 2026 (spatial session): [link]

docs.title: Tool index — GRC (post-meeting, May 15+)
docs.text:
The GRC's seven sessions (AI for Genomics, TF Regulation, Single-Cell Modeling, Applications in Medicine, Spatial & Proteomics, 3D Genomics, Epigenomics) will each yield ~5 oral talks → ~30–35 tool candidates. Tool pages get drafted from:

  1. Preprints that drop May 15–Jul 15 with "presented at the 2026 Gordon Research Conference on Single-Cell Genomics" in the acknowledgements.
  2. Bluesky posts from attendees with the chair's permission (Pisco has historically blessed selective sharing).
  3. Selected speakers' lab Bluesky/X feeds announcing their published-by-then work.

Expected dominant lineages at GRC 2026 (based on the AI/ML subtitle and the field's mid-2026 trajectory):

  • Foundation-model successors: scGPT-v2, Geneformer-v2, scFoundation-clinical, Universal Cell Embeddings updates, scBERT successors, perturbation-foundation models (Bunne's CellFlow class).
  • Atlas-platform layer: CELLxGENE Discover updates, HCA v2.0, Tabula Sapiens v3, HuBMAP integration, HTAN cancer-atlas drops.
  • Spatial inference: Visium HD analysis tooling (Voyager, SpatialData, semla, STUtility), Xenium-native pipelines, CosMx integration, MERSCOPE / MERFISH-Vizgen analysis.
  • 3D genomics: scHi-C analysis (Nagano-line, Higashi successors), single-cell 3D contact-map inference, A/B compartment dynamics.
  • Multimodal: CITE-seq / TEA-seq / Multiome integration, methylation+RNA, proteo-genomics.

docs.title: Why this format
docs.text:
• Cross-vault links matter most at this meeting. Tools released here cycle through AACR sessions in the same year (talks reference "new methods like X") and AACR posters the next year (posters use X as a default). Single-Cell Genomics → AACR is the densest tool-to-clinical-application link in the corpus.
  • Modality field is critical for slicing — single-cell is too broad a category for one-axis searching. scRNA-only methods vs spatial-only methods vs multimodal methods don't compete with each other.
  • Atlas footprint captures the "is this tool already validated at scale?" dimension that distinguishes 2024-style methods (single dataset benchmarks) from 2026-style methods (CELLxGENE-corpus benchmarks expected).
  • Foundation-model lineage captures the most important methods-evolution axis of 2026 — which transformer family is this descended from, and what does it cite as baseline?
  • Two-meeting Talk fields are necessary because many tools will be presented at both GRC and Wellcome (slightly different versions/framings to slightly different audiences).

docs.title: Open questions for the pilot
docs.text:
1. GRC scaffolding from non-public sources — Pisco's discretion. Default policy: only include a GRC tool page if (a) a preprint exists by post-meeting drafting time, (b) the author has publicly acknowledged presenting at GRC, OR (c) we hear the talk content from an attendee with permission to share. No second-hand "I heard X presented Y" without confirmation.
  2. Foundation-model lineage as a free-text vs controlled-vocab field — leaning controlled (scGPT / Geneformer / scFoundation / scBERT / UCE / scPRINT / independent) so we can do "show me all Geneformer-line tools" filters later. Open.
  3. Atlas-platform tools (CELLxGENE Discover, HCA portal, CZ CELLxGENE Census) — these are tools but not in the standard "package on Bioc/PyPI" sense. Proposed: separate badge "Status: platform / atlas-infrastructure" that swaps the package row for an "Access" row pointing to a web portal.
  4. Lineage-tracing tools (DNA Typewriter, recording lineage, Gagnon-line) — these are wet-lab methods primarily, with analytical tooling secondary. Proposed: "Status: experimental method + companion analysis package" — two rows for source links (wet-lab protocol + analysis code).

docs.title: SITC 2026
docs.text:
SITC 41st Annual Meeting & Pre-Conference Programs — Phoenix Convention Center, Phoenix, AZ · November 4 – 8, 2026. ~6,000 attendees, the premier cancer-immunotherapy venue of the year.

Status: Scaffold — meeting is 6 months out as of today (May 11, 2026). Vault structure is being seeded now so we can move quickly on the abstract embargo (regular abstracts open Apr 22 → close Jun 25; presentation embargoes lift on the morning of the talk in early November). Anything in this vault dated before SITC 2026 is built from SITC 2025 program shape, company toplines, and partner / sponsor press from JPM 2026, AACR 2026, and ASCO 2026 — flagged inline.

docs.title: Why this is in the vault
docs.text:
SITC is the immunotherapy half-life of the oncology calendar — the venue where checkpoint, cell therapy (CAR-T, TIL, TCR-T), bispecifics, neoantigen vaccines, and tumor-microenvironment biology converge in one program. It sits at a deliberate intersection with two AACR axes:

  1. Clinical-trials axis — early- and mid-phase IO readouts (Ph1/2 cell-therapy and bispecific cohorts, checkpoint-resistance combos, neoantigen-vaccine signal). Many SITC presentations are the IO trials that didn't fit the ASCO Plenary calendar or the AACR mechanism slot — earlier-phase data on drugs that will land at ASCO 2027 or ESMO 2027.
  2. Single-cell / spatial-omics axis — immune profiling is half the program. Multiplex IF, spatial transcriptomics, scRNA-seq, TCR repertoire, ctDNA-MRD, and microbiome readouts anchor a large block of the methods program. Same tools, same labs as the EuroBioC / GBCC / RECOMB tools axis, applied to IO-specific biological questions.

Hybrid template (and the design decision behind this vault): SITC is neither pure-clinical (ASCO) nor pure-tools (EuroBioC) — it's both, in the same program, often back-to-back in the same session. Pure per-trial pages miss the methods talks; pure per-tool pages miss the cell-therapy cohorts. We're running both templates in parallel:

  • trials/ — per-trial / per-readout entries for drug + cell-therapy readouts (CAR-T cohorts, bispecific Ph1/2, neoantigen-vaccine arms, checkpoint-resistance combos). Schema borrowed from ASCO 2026 trials.
  • tools/ — per-tool entries for biomarker, immune-profiling, and spatial-immune methods (multiplex IF panels, TCR repertoire pipelines, ctDNA-MRD assays, microbiome 16S/shotgun protocols, spatial-immune classifiers). Schema borrowed from EuroBioC 2025 tools.

Cross-links between the two are the load-bearing piece: a CAR-T cohort in trials/ should link to the spatial-immune profiling tool that read its biopsies in tools/, and vice versa.

docs.title: Program shape (per SITC 2025 + early SITC 2026 announcements)
docs.text:
SITC 2026 runs Wednesday Nov 4 – Sunday Nov 8, five days. The structure:

  • Wed Nov 4 – Thu Nov 5: Pre-Conference Programs. Workshops on cellular therapy, biomarkers / immune-monitoring, regulatory science, primer courses. ~10 parallel tracks.
  • Fri Nov 6 – Sun Nov 8: Annual Meeting proper. Plenary + concurrent sessions + poster halls.
  • Keynote: Ton Schumacher, PhD (Netherlands Cancer Institute) — "T Cell Recognition of Human Cancer: 'Cracking the Code'" (TCR / neoantigen-recognition biology).
  • Smalley Memorial Award & Lectureship: Catherine J. Wu, MD (Dana-Farber) — neoantigen-vaccine science (the personalized-vaccine program that started at DFCI and now anchors Moderna, BioNTech, and Gritstone competitor reads).
  • Abstract scale: ~1,200 abstracts, several hundred posters, >40 oral / concurrent sessions.
  • Tracks dominating the corpus (per SITC 2025 shape):
  • Cellular therapies — CAR-T (autologous + allogeneic), TIL, TCR-T, NK-cell, engineered macrophages. Solid-tumor cell therapy is the growth area.
  • Checkpoint resistance — combinations to overcome primary / acquired anti-PD-(L)1 resistance; novel checkpoints (LAG-3, TIGIT, TIM-3, VISTA).
  • Bispecifics + ADCs — T-cell engagers, NK engagers, immunocytokines; checkpoint × VEGF, checkpoint × CD3.
  • Neoantigen vaccines — personalized mRNA, peptide, DNA platforms; shared-neoantigen approaches; vaccine + checkpoint combos.
  • Biomarkers / immune monitoring — multiplex IF, spatial transcriptomics, TCR repertoire, ctDNA-MRD, single-cell.
  • Microbiome × immunotherapy axis — FMT, defined-consortium products, dietary intervention, prebiotic / probiotic combinations (the Wargo thread, continued).
  • Spatial-immune profiling — tumor microenvironment characterization across response / resistance; spatial classifiers as biomarker-development substrate.

docs.title: What's different from ASCO 2026 and AACR 2026
docs.text:
• Smaller, denser, more IO-pure. ~6,000 attendees vs ASCO's ~40,000 and AACR's ~22,000. Every session is IO; no GU non-IO, no symptoms-and-survivorship track, no non-cancer biology.
  • Earlier-phase data than ASCO. Most cell-therapy and bispecific readouts at SITC are Ph1/2 cohorts and dose-escalation updates, not randomized Ph3. Closer in maturity to AACR's clinical-trials track than to ASCO's Plenary slate.
  • Tools-and-trials in the same program. Unlike ASCO (pure clinical) or EuroBioC (pure tools), SITC programs methods talks adjacent to drug readouts. Spatial-immune profiling on biopsies from the same Ph2 cohort that's reading out in the next session.
  • JITC as the citable record. Unlike ASCO Meeting Library (proprietary), JITC is open-access BMJ-published; every abstract gets a DOI. Easier to cite, more permanent.
  • Microbiome / spatial-immune themes — both are bigger at SITC than at any other oncology meeting. Microbiome × IO especially: SITC is where defined-consortium products and FMT-in-IO trial data appear.

docs.title: Cross-vault links
docs.text:
• AACR 2026 — IO biology / mechanism / discovery side. Many SITC 2026 presenters had AACR 2026 sessions in April. Single-cell / spatial axis overlaps heavily.
  • ASCO 2026 — clinical-translation counterpart. Some SITC 2026 trials will reach ASCO 2027 as randomized readouts.
  • JPM 2026 — financing layer. Multiple SITC 2026 sponsors (cell-therapy companies, neoantigen-vaccine platforms, bispecific developers) were on the JPM stage in January.
  • EuroBioC 2025 tools — methods axis. Spatial-omics packages (SpatialData, DESpace, spatialFDA), TCR / clonal-tracking (barbieQ), and microbiome (mia, miaTime) all have direct application in SITC immune-monitoring talks.
  • Conferences timeline — SITC's position in the year's cycle (AACR Apr → ASCO May/Jun → ESMO Oct → SITC Nov → ASH Dec → JPM Jan).

docs.title: Expected tracks (per SITC 2025 shape; speculative for SITC 2026)
docs.text:
SITC 2025 had concurrent sessions across the following themes, and SITC 2026 is expected to track closely (organizing committee continuity, similar abstract demographics). To be confirmed against the SITC 2026 program-at-a-glance once posted.

  1. Cellular therapies — CAR-T (autologous + allogeneic + in vivo), TIL, TCR-T, NK-cell, CAR-NK, engineered Tregs, engineered macrophages
  2. Checkpoint resistance — combinations to overcome primary / acquired anti-PD-(L)1 resistance; novel checkpoints (LAG-3, TIGIT, TIM-3, VISTA, BTLA)
  3. Bispecifics + ADCs — T-cell engagers, NK engagers, immunocytokines; PD-1 × VEGF; ADC + IO combos
  4. Neoantigen vaccines — personalized mRNA, peptide, DNA platforms; shared-neoantigen approaches; vaccine + checkpoint combinations
  5. Biomarkers / immune monitoring — multiplex IF, spatial transcriptomics, TCR repertoire, ctDNA-MRD, single-cell immune profiling, cytokine panels
  6. Microbiome × immunotherapy — FMT, defined-consortium products, dietary intervention, prebiotic / probiotic combinations
  7. Spatial-immune profiling — TME spatial atlases, response / resistance classifiers, biomarker development substrate
  8. Innate immunity in IO — myeloid reprogramming, macrophage repolarization, NK biology, innate-checkpoint blockade
  9. Toxicity management — irAE biology, CRS / ICANS, steroid-sparing interventions
  10. Pediatric IO + rare cancers — cell therapy in pediatric solid tumors, rare-tumor IO
  11. Regulatory science — FDA / EMA framework for cellular therapy, vaccine, biomarker qualification (joint sessions with FDA officials are a SITC tradition)

docs.title: Anticipated big readouts (drug / cell-therapy side)
docs.text: All entries below are speculative, sourced from sponsor pipelines + AACR 2026 echo + JPM 2026 strategy + ASCO 2026 preview. To be reconciled with the SITC 2026 program-at-a-glance and the JITC abstract supplement. Categorized by likelihood + impact.

docs.title: Tier 1 — likely headline tracks
docs.text:
1. In vivo CAR-T first-in-human safety — Capstan / Umoja / Outpace / Orna LNP-delivered constructs. First-in-human B-cell depletion kinetics + safety would define a new modality. The AstraZeneca / Capstan thesis from JPM 2026 (autoimmune-and-onc crossover) sets up SITC as the venue for the first-clinical-data readout.
  2. Solid-tumor CAR-T inflection — multiple academic + biotech Ph1 cohorts in GBM, mesothelioma, GI cancers (Claudin18.2, GPC3, mesothelin). Whether any cohort crosses the response threshold that justifies a pivotal trial.
  3. Personalized mRNA neoantigen vaccines update — Moderna mRNA-4157 (V940) in adjuvant melanoma / NSCLC / RCC; BioNTech BNT122 (autogene cevumeran) in pancreatic adjuvant + CRC; Gritstone shared-neoantigen platform CRC. The Wu Smalley lecture frames the whole field.
  4. Allogeneic CAR-T durability update — Allogene / Caribou / Cellectis CD19, BCMA constructs. Off-the-shelf cell-therapy proof point — durability is the long-standing question.
  5. TIL therapy beyond melanoma — Iovance Amtagvi cohorts in NSCLC + cervical; competitive set in HNSCC, NSCLC.

docs.title: Tier 2 — class status checks
docs.text:
1. Bispecific durability — BCMA × CD3 (teclistamab, elranatamab, linvoseltamab), CD20 × CD3 (epcoritamab, glofitamab, mosunetuzumab), GPRC5D × CD3 (talquetamab) long-term follow-up. Antigen escape and T-cell exhaustion as resistance themes.
  2. PD-1 × VEGF bispecific mechanism-of-action correlatives — ivonescimab (Summit / Akeso) post-HARMONi-6 ASCO Plenary; AbbVie RC148; BMS pumitamig. The class-defining moment may have been ASCO; SITC is the venue for the biological why.
  3. LAG-3 class status — relatlimab + nivo follow-on cohorts; novel LAG-3 antibodies in expansion. Whether LAG-3 holds beyond melanoma.
  4. TIGIT class status — post-Skyscraper, the survivors. Roche tiragolumab subset rescue; iTeos / GSK EOS-448; Gilead domvanalimab durability. Whether any subset-defined cohort revives the class.
  5. Microbiome × IO maturation — Vedanta, Seres, Finch defined-consortium products in checkpoint-refractory melanoma + RCC; academic FMT cohorts. Wargo's SITC 2025 keynote thread, now with randomized data.

docs.title: Tier 3 — early-phase candidates worth tracking
docs.text:
1. TCR-T solid-tumor expansion — Adaptimmune afami-cel post-approval cohorts; TScan TSC-100/101; Immatics IMA203 PRAME.
  2. NK-engager updates — Affimed AFM13 + AFM24; Sanofi SAR / NK-bispecific platform.
  3. Immunocytokines — Philogen IL2-targeted; Asher Bio IL-2v engineering; Mural IL-12 tumor-localized.
  4. ADC × IO combos — EV + pembro (Padcev), Trop2-ADC + IO, T-DXd + IO — durability and safety updates.
  5. HPV-driven cancer vaccines + checkpoint — ISA101 + pembro HNSCC; competitive set in cervical.

docs.title: Tools — SITC 2026
docs.text:
The second primary artifact: one Markdown file per biomarker / immune-profiling method or pipeline. SITC programs methods talks adjacent to drug readouts — multiplex IF panels, TCR repertoire pipelines, ctDNA-MRD assays, microbiome sequencing protocols, single-cell + spatial classifiers. Each gets a tools/<slug>.md entry. The drug / cell-therapy side lives in trials/.

Status: Template stub. We're carrying over the per-tool format from EuroBioC 2025 tools, with one modification: SITC is not a Bioconductor venue — many tools are commercial platforms (Akoya, Standard BioTools / IonPath MIBI, NanoString CosMx, 10x Xenium / Visium HD, Adaptive immunoSEQ), not R packages. The "Status" badge swaps Bioconductor for Platform / vendor / open-source repo / vignette / preprint. Once the program-at-a-glance posts in September, ~15–20 entries get populated from the methods + immune-monitoring sessions.

docs.title: Per-tool entry template
docs.text:
Each tool gets its own page (tools/<slug>.md) following this structure:

# <Tool / panel / platform name>

**One-line description** — what the assay / pipeline does in plain language.

- **Group / vendor:** <academic lab / commercial vendor>
- **Platform / format:** <multiplex IF / spatial-transcriptomics / TCR-seq / single-cell / ctDNA / 16S+shotgun / image-analysis / classifier>
- **Repo / vendor page:** [link]
- **Vignette / protocol:** [link]
- **Preprint / paper:** [DOI]
- **Status at SITC 2026:** <new release / major update / methods talk / case-study readout / pre-conference workshop>

## Talk at SITC 2026

- **Speaker:** ...
- **Day / session:** ...
- **Slides:** [link if shared]
- **Video:** [SITC virtual link if recorded]
- **Abstract:** [JITC DOI]

## What it does

2–3 sentences: the immune-profiling problem it solves, key methodological idea,
what it consumes / produces. Be explicit about the **IO use case** — biomarker
of response, mechanism-of-resistance characterization, MRD, neoantigen
prediction, TCR-clonotype tracking, immune-cell-state classification.

## Where it fits in the corpus

- **SITC 2026 trials:** [link to any `trials/<x>.md` that used this assay for correlatives]
- **AACR 2026:** [link if mentioned in an AACR talk or poster]
- **EuroBioC 2025:** [link if the same / analogous package was shown]
- **GBCC 2025 / RECOMB 2026 / ISMB 2026:** [link if mentioned]
- **JPM 2026:** [link if commercial vendor presented]

## Notes

Free-form impressions: validation data shown, comparisons to alternatives,
batch / cross-site reproducibility claims, sample-prep requirements,
turnaround time, regulatory status (CDx / CLIA / RUO).

docs.title: Why this format
docs.text:
• Cross-vault links matter most here — a multiplex-IF panel from SITC anchors trial correlatives at AACR, biomarker classifiers at RECOMB, and Bioconductor analysis packages at EuroBioC. The tool entry is the join key.
  • Trial ↔ tool linking is the unique value of the SITC vault: every tools/<x>.md should link to the trials/<y>.md where it appeared as correlative data, and vice versa.
  • Platform vs package distinction is explicit. Unlike EuroBioC (all R packages), SITC mixes commercial platforms, academic open-source pipelines, and clinical assays — the Status field surfaces that.

docs.title: Open questions for the build
docs.text:
1. Commercial vendor sessions — SITC has industry-symposia where vendors (Akoya, 10x, Adaptive, NanoString) present case studies. Treat these as tools/ entries with Status: vendor case-study?

  3. Workshops vs talks — pre-conference workshops on cellular-therapy immune-monitoring and biomarker development warrant fuller treatment than a single talk; consider a workshop-detail subsection in the template.

docs.title: Per-trial template
docs.text:
Each trial file (e.g., obe-cel-r2-all.md, bnt122-melanoma.md) follows this schema. Copy and fill:

# <Trial acronym / name> — <Drug regimen / cell-therapy product, indication, line>

> **Abstract:** <JITC abstract #, e.g., 102> · **Session:** <session name, date, time MST, room> · **Embargo:** <presentation date>

## At a glance

- **Sponsor:** <pharma / academic / cooperative group>
- **PI / presenter:** <name, institution>
- **NCT ID:** <NCTxxxxxxxx>
- **Modality:** <autologous CAR-T / allogeneic CAR-T / in vivo CAR-T / TIL / TCR-T / NK cell / bispecific / mRNA neoantigen vaccine / peptide vaccine / checkpoint combo / ADC + IO / immunocytokine>
- **Target / construct:** <CD19 / BCMA / GPRC5D / Claudin18.2 / HLA-A*02 NY-ESO-1 / personalized neoantigen / PD-1×VEGF / etc.>
- **Phase:** <1 / 1b / 2 / 1-2 / 2-3>
- **Design:** <dose-escalation / dose-expansion / randomized / single-arm / basket / platform>
- **N:** <enrolled / treated / analyzed>
- **Primary endpoint(s):** <ORR / CR / PFS / OS / DLT / safety / immunogenicity>
- **Indication:** <tumor type, subtype, biomarker selection (HLA, antigen expression, MSI, TMB)>
- **Line:** <neoadjuvant / adjuvant / 1L / 2L+ / R/R / heavily pretreated>

## Headline result

<One paragraph. ORR, CR rate, duration of response, safety profile if known.
If pre-embargo, mark `*expected per <company> topline <date>*` or
`*pre-embargo per <analyst source>*`.>

## Mechanism / class

<Modality detail: construct architecture for cell therapies (CAR design, costim
domain, edits); target rationale; manufacturing / vein-to-vein time;
neoantigen-selection pipeline for vaccines. Cross-link to related AACR
mechanism sessions where the biology was presented.>

## Biomarker / correlative readout

<This is the SITC-specific field. What immune-profiling assay anchored the
trial? Multiplex IF? scRNA-seq of TILs? TCR repertoire? ctDNA-MRD? Cross-link
to the corresponding `tools/<assay>.md` entry. Many SITC trials present
biomarker correlatives in the same talk as the efficacy numbers.>

## Discussant / session framing

<Session chair + co-presenters, if a themed concurrent session. SITC doesn't
have ASCO-style discussants, but session co-programming is itself a signal.>

## Practice-changing / class-defining?

<Yes / no / pending, with rationale: first-in-class signal, dose decision for
pivotal, BLA path, unmet need, competitive context vs prior cell therapies
or checkpoint baselines.>

docs.title: Cross-cutting themes (for post-meeting themes.md)
docs.text:
To synthesize across trials/ once populated:

  1. Solid-tumor CAR-T inflection. Whether GBM, GI, and mesothelioma CAR-T cohorts cross the response threshold that justifies pivotal trials.
  2. In vivo CAR-T arrives. Capstan / Umoja / Orna / Outpace LNP-delivered constructs — first-in-human safety + B-cell kinetics will define a new modality.
  3. Neoantigen-vaccine signal hardens (or doesn't). Moderna mRNA-4157 RFS update + BioNTech BNT122 pancreatic + Gritstone shared-antigen CRC. Wu Smalley lecture frames the field.
  4. Bispecific durability and resistance. BCMA × CD3 and CD20 × CD3 long-term follow-up — antigen escape, T-cell exhaustion, sequencing vs CAR-T.
  5. LAG-3 / TIGIT class status. Post-Skyscraper TIGIT cohorts and LAG-3 expansion data — which checkpoint partner survives.
  6. Microbiome × IO matures. Defined-consortium and FMT data in checkpoint-refractory melanoma + RCC, the through-line from Wargo's SITC 2025 keynote.
